structured_extraction.program_name: Allegany County Local Development Council Rocky Gap Slots Revenue Funding Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Allegany County Local Development Council distributes a portion of slots revenue from Rocky Gap Casino to eligible Allegany County non-profits and municipalities for capital projects. The county receives 5.5% of slots revenues generated from the casino operation at Rocky Gap, and by state law 20% of this revenue must be spent on capital requests from Allegany County municipalities and non-profits. The Local Development Council reviews requests and makes spending recommendations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding distributed from Rocky Gap Casino slots revenue. Funds may only be used for capital-related items and cannot be used for operating expenses. Awards are made after review and recommendation by a subcommittee of the 15-member Allegany County Local Development Council. Grant amounts vary based on available slots revenue and the number of qualifying requests received.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Allegany County non-profit organizations and municipalities seeking funding for capital improvement projects
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital projects and capital-related items only. Funds cannot be used for operating expenses, salaries, or administrative costs. Eligible uses include facility improvements, equipment purchases, infrastructure projects, and other permanent capital assets.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Allegany County, Maryland. Applicants must be located in or serve Allegany County.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a non-profit organization or municipality located in Allegany County
Organization must be in good standing and able to provide proof of non-profit or municipal status
Funding request must be for capital-related items and projects
Funding cannot be used for operating expenses, salaries, or administrative costs
Applicant must submit request by the annual deadline
Project must benefit the Allegany County community
Applicant may be required to provide financial documentation and project details
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit a request via the online form available on the Allegany County website or submit a letter of request to Jason M. Bennett. The letter or form should include: organization's name and proof of non-profit or municipal status, organization's mission or purpose, detailed description of capital needs and proposed project, total amount of funding requested, project timeline, and any matching funds or other funding sources. All requests are reviewed by a subcommittee of the 15-member Local Development Council. The Council evaluates requests based on community need and available funding. Award decisions are announced and funds are typically disbursed within approximately six weeks of approval.

structured_extraction.contact_name: Allegany College Foundation, Inc. / Frostburg State University Financial Aid Office
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents of Allegany County, Maryland who meet the minimum three-year residency requirement and are enrolled or planning to enroll at Allegany College of Maryland or Frostburg State University.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational expenses including tuition at Allegany College of Maryland or Frostburg State University.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Restricted to residents of Allegany County, Maryland with a minimum three-year residency requirement.
requirements_list: Must be a resident of Allegany County, Maryland
Must meet minimum three-year residency requirement
Must be enrolled or planning to enroll at either Allegany College of Maryland or Frostburg State University
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested applicants should contact the Allegany College of Maryland Foundation or Frostburg State University Financial Aid Office for application details and deadlines. Each institution administers the scholarship program through its own scholarship application process. Applications are typically processed through the institution's financial aid office.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: An annual exemption from the Chesapeake Bay Restoration Fund fee (flush tax) for residents experiencing financial hardship. A new application must be completed every year to be considered for the exemption. Eligible residents are exempt from paying the mandated fee if approved.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annual application; new application required each year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Allegany County residents experiencing financial hardship who are unable to pay the Bay Restoration Fund fee.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: This is an exemption program; funds are not provided to applicants. Instead, qualifying residents are exempted from paying the mandated Bay Restoration Fund fee.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Allegany County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be an Allegany County resident
Must be experiencing financial hardship
Must complete the Bay Restoration Fund Financial Hardship Exemption Application form
Must submit application annually to remain eligible
Household income must fall within established hardship thresholds
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Residents must complete the Bay Restoration Fund Financial Hardship Exemption Application form and submit it to the Tax & Utility Office in Allegany County. Applications are reviewed to determine eligibility based on demonstrated financial hardship. A new application must be submitted each year to remain eligible for the exemption. Applicants will be notified of approval or denial status.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides low-interest loans to homeowners, renters, private non-profits, and businesses in disaster-declared counties who sustained damages from flooding. Homeowners may borrow up to $500,000 to replace or repair their primary residences and up to $100,000 to replace or repair personal property. Businesses and most private non-profits may borrow up to $2 million to cover disaster losses not fully covered by insurance. Also offers Economic Injury Disaster Loans (EIDL) for small businesses and non-profits that have suffered substantial economic injury. Long-term repayment options are available with terms up to 30 years, determined on a case-by-case basis.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Physical Disaster Loans for homeowners up to $500,000 to replace or repair primary residences; up to $100,000 for homeowners and renters to replace or repair personal property. Business and non-profit loans up to $2 million to cover uninsured or underinsured disaster losses. Economic Injury Disaster Loans (EIDL) available for small businesses and non-profits experiencing substantial economic injury due to the disaster. Interest rates determined on a case-by-case basis. Repayment terms up to 30 years based on borrower's ability to repay.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Deadline to return SBA disaster loan applications for physical damages is July 21, 2025. Deadline to return SBA economic injury disaster loan (EIDL) applications is February 23, 2026.
structured_extraction.contact_phone: 1-800-659-2955 or 1-800-877-8339 for the deaf and hard-of-hearing
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners, renters, private non-profits, and businesses located in Allegany County that sustained damages from the May 13, 2025 flooding event
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Replace or repair primary residences; replace or repair personal property; cover disaster losses not fully covered by insurance; address substantial economic injury to businesses and non-profits
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Allegany County, designated as a contiguous county under Pennsylvania Disaster Number PA-20019. Applicants must be located in this disaster-declared area.
requirements_list: Must be located in Allegany County (contiguous county under PA-20019 declaration)
Must have sustained damages from the May 13, 2025 flooding event
For homeowners: must own and occupy primary residence in disaster area
For renters: must have rented primary residence in disaster area
For businesses and non-profits: must demonstrate business was operating in disaster area
Damages must not be fully covered by insurance (for physical disaster loans)
Must provide proof of disaster-related losses
Small businesses and non-profits must demonstrate substantial economic injury for EIDL consideration
Must be unable to obtain credit elsewhere at reasonable rates
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the SBA Disaster Customer Service by phone at 1-800-659-2955 (1-800-877-8339 for individuals who are deaf or hard-of-hearing) or by email at DisasterCustomerService@sba.gov. Reference Pennsylvania Disaster Number PA-20019 when contacting. Applications can be completed online at https://lending.sba.gov/. Applications must be submitted by the stated deadlines: July 21, 2025 for physical damage loans and February 23, 2026 for EIDL applications. Applicants should be prepared to provide documentation of losses, proof of occupancy/business operation, tax returns, and insurance information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program providing zero percent interest, deferred loans for up to 30 years or grants to finance accessibility improvements to the homes of seniors age 55 or older. Improvements may include grab bars, railings, ramps, widened doorways, and accessible showers to help seniors remain independent in their homes.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Zero percent interest, deferred loans for up to 30 years with no monthly payments until sale, transfer, or refinance of the property. Loans have interest rates based on applicant income and ability to repay, generally with a maximum of $50,000. Interest rates range from 0% to 6% based on the applicant's ability to pay. The maximum loan term is 30 years. Loans in excess of $5,000 or with deferred payments are secured by a mortgage. Grants up to $25,000 available for applicants who do not qualify for loan funding. Loans that serve families with incomes at or below 50 percent of the statewide or Washington, D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income may have deferred payments if necessary for project feasibility. All closing costs included in the loan.
structured_extraction.contact_phone: (301) 429-7409 or toll free 877-218-8101; TTY 711 or 1-800-735-2258; or 1-844-369-4150 for lead-based paint inquiries
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents age 55 or older who own and occupy their primary residence and need accessibility modifications. Household income cannot exceed 80 percent of the statewide or Washington, D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Accessibility improvements such as widening doorways, installation of accessible showers, ramps, grab bars, lever handles, first floor bathrooms and laundry rooms, chair lifts, handrails, and rubber treads on a case-by-case basis to address health and safety issues.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide, available in all Maryland counties. Income eligibility based on 80 percent of Statewide or Washington DC MSA median income. Income limits vary by household size and region (Washington DC PMSA including Calvert, Charles, Frederick, Montgomery, and Prince George's Counties vs. Rest of State). As of July 1, 2025, maximum income limits for 80% AMI range from $72,950 (1 person, Rest of State) to $141,000 (8 persons, Washington DC PMSA).
requirements_list: Be a Maryland resident with at least one resident age 55 or older
Own and occupy the home as primary residence (seniors living with relatives considered case by case)
Reside in a structurally sound home free of health and safety hazards
Not have outstanding federal or state tax liens, open bankruptcy, or foreclosure
Meet income requirements (household income not exceed 80% of Statewide or Washington DC MSA median income)
Provide photo ID for applicant and any co-applicant (driver's license, passport, military ID, etc.)
Provide proof of home ownership including copy of deed and current mortgage statement
Provide most recent property tax bill
Provide copy of the Declaration Page of Homeowners Insurance Policy
Provide copy of Flood Insurance Policy if applicable
If a person is on the deed but not the application, provide proof such as copy of their license or piece of mail documenting their different address; if deceased, provide copy of death certificate

Provide income verification documents including most recent two months of paystubs, two years of Federal Income Tax Returns, two months of bank statements, and award letters for Social Security, disability, pension, or public assistance

Provide documentation of critical repairs from a licensed and insured contractor including photos, bid quote (not more than 60 days old), contractor's phone number and email address, current MHIC or trade license, Certificate of Liability Insurance with per occurrence limits of at least $1 million, Letter of Good Standing, and completed W-9 form
Total of all bids should not exceed $50,000
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are available at local County Housing Offices or Maryland Access Point Agencies. Assistance in completing the application is available in-person or through in-home appointments. Applicants must submit a completed application with all required supporting documentation via email to DHCD.SLP_documentation@maryland.gov or by mail to Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, CDA, Special Loan Programs, 7800 Harkins Road, 3rd Floor, Lanham, MD 20706. Once submitted, the department reviews the application and contacts the applicant. Incomplete applications will not be processed.

structured_extraction.program_name: BeSMART Energy Efficiency Loan for Homeowners
structured_extraction.program_description: A financing program that provides low-interest, unsecured loans to Maryland homeowners to improve energy efficiency and comfort by replacing and upgrading appliances, heating, ventilation and cooling systems, and whole house envelope improvements, helping homeowners save on utility bills.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: An unsecured loan with a rate of 6.99% APR. Up to $30,000 in financing is available for energy efficiency measures for a term up to 10 years (borrowers can also choose shorter terms). The minimum loan amount is $5,000. Financing is based on verification of credit and ability to pay. Solar projects can be financed up to 50% of the total loan amount (1:1 match to energy efficiency measures cost). The loan structure includes a 30% down payment (2-party check made to borrower and contractor, or 1-party check for retail purchases) upon approval, and the remaining 70% is disbursed upon project completion and submission of Certificate of Completion. There are no pre-payment penalties, and borrowers can avoid interest by paying off the loan early.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners seeking to improve energy efficiency and reduce utility costs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency improvements including insulation and air sealing, ENERGY STAR heating and cooling systems, hot water heating equipment, ENERGY STAR appliances (excluding stoves, ovens, and microwave ovens which have no Energy Star ratings), windows and doors, lighting and controls, programmable and smart thermostats, ceiling fans and ventilation fans, geothermal heat pumps, solar photovoltaic installation (capped at 50% of total loan amount), health and safety costs related to energy improvements including mold remediation and radon mitigation (up to 25% of total loan cost), and other improvements identified in a certified energy audit.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide
requirements_list: Maryland homeowner
Credit score of 640 or greater
Debt to income ratio that does not exceed 50%
Projects or upgrades must not be already purchased or already completed
Contractor must be licensed and insured in Maryland (proof of license and insurance required)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the online BeSMART Loan Application or request a paper application by email. Submit required income documentation (30 days of pay stubs, recent mortgage statement, and driver's license) to get pre-approved on a financial basis. Complete DocuSign authorization to provide Social Security number and consent for credit report. Submit contractor estimate or proposal, or retailer estimate for appliances. Sign and return loan documents provided by DHCD. Receive 30% down payment (2-party check with borrower and contractor names for contractor projects, or 1-party check for retail purchases). Complete your project with licensed and insured contractor. Submit photos and Certificate of Completion signed by borrower and contractor. Receive final 70% payment. Begin making monthly loan payments.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Business Boost Microgrant provides grants ranging from $20,000 to $50,000 to support small businesses needing capital for growth and expansion opportunities. Offered through the Neighborhood BusinessWorks program, the initiative has a preference for helping home-based businesses establish their first commercial location outside of the home. Up to $2,000,000 in total funding is available.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from $20,000 to $50,000 are available to eligible businesses. Applicants must provide a matching contribution equal to or greater than the grant request amount. For example, if awarded a $50,000 grant, the business must contribute $50,000 of their own funds to the project. Funds can be used towards capital and operating expenses that support revenue growth from September 23, 2024, to March 23, 2025, including salary, rent, utilities, product advertising, product development, commercial real estate acquisition, and professional services. Only new expenses are eligible; existing expenses cannot be covered. Up to $2,000,000 in total funding is available through this program.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: The application round is projected to close on Monday, October 14th, 2024, at 5 PM EST. The round may close sooner if grant requests exceed available funding.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit small businesses located in Sustainable Communities areas with greater than 2 full-time equivalent employees and 50 or fewer employees, and annual revenue between $50,000 and $1 million.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital and operating expenses that support revenue growth from September 23, 2024, to March 23, 2025. Eligible expenses include salary, rent, utilities, product advertising, product development, commercial real estate acquisition, and professional services. Only new expenses are eligible; existing expenses such as current rent or payroll cannot be covered. Funds are intended to assist businesses in expansion by covering increased rent, increased payroll for new hires, new equipment, and marketing initiatives.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must be located in a Sustainable Communities area in Maryland. Applicants can use the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper at https://portal.dhcd.state.md.us/GIS/revitalize/index.html to verify if their business location qualifies by entering their business address in the incentive look-up tool.
requirements_list: Be a for-profit business
Be located at an eligible location in a Sustainable Communities area in Maryland
Have greater than 2 employees and 50 or fewer employees (full-time equivalent) as of September 23, 2024
Have an annual revenue of at least $50,000 but no more than $1 million
Have a matching contribution equal to or greater than the grant request amount
Be in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
Provide Articles of Organization for the business
Provide by-laws for the business
Provide most recent annual tax return filed (Tax year 2023)
Provide organization's financial statements as of August 31, 2024
Provide screenshot showing the business is in an eligible location
Provide proof of matching funds (bank statement or loan statement showing available funds)
Provide screenshot of Certificate of Good Standing from SDAT
Provide IRS W-9 Request for Taxpayer Identification Number and Certification
Business name must EXACTLY match on application, SDAT's Good Standing Certificate, and W-9
Professional services and sales-based businesses including Insurance, Accounting, Real Estate, Legal, and Finance are not eligible

Non-profit organizations, cannabis-based businesses, pawn shops, gun shops, massage parlors, adult video/book shops, adult entertainment facilities, rental real estate businesses, tanning salons, check-cashing facilities, gambling facilities, tattoo parlors, and liquor stores are not eligible
Previous award winners of an NBW Opportunity Zone grant or NBW Business Boost grant are not eligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The application is online and can be accessed at https://apps.dhcd.state.md.us/NBWOZGrant/account/login. The application round is projected to open on Monday, September 23, 2024, at 12:00 noon and close on Monday, October 14, 2024, at 5 PM EST (may close sooner if grant requests exceed available funding). Applicants must provide a brief description of their organization, answer questions about their organization, complete a budget table showing how grant funds and matching contribution will be used, and describe how the funds will advance their business within a sustainable community area. Only fully completed applications will be considered for funding. Incomplete applications will be returned and processed when resources are available. Applications are prioritized based on business location, expansion impact (new employees to be hired, capital investment, additional square footage), and quality of business financials and supporting documents. Priority attributes include innovative businesses driving technology advancements, businesses in new industries, businesses focused on regional strengths, businesses leveraging partnerships with educational institutions, and Minority Business Enterprises (MBEs). Award announcements will be made on a rolling basis during December 2024 to January 2025. Grant awards are expected to be paid in February-March 2025. Local governing body approval is required before funds are disbursed. Final reports are required by March 31, 2026, and awardees will be contacted nine months after receiving funds to complete a questionnaire and provide a one-page summary of grant impact.

structured_extraction.program_description: Funds help strengthen Maryland's communities by expanding affordable housing opportunities, creating jobs, stabilizing neighborhoods and improving the overall quality of life. The program is designed to assist county and municipal governments with activities directed toward neighborhood revitalization, housing opportunities, economic development and improved public facilities and services.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal funds allocated annually by Congress through the Community Development Block Grant Program. Maryland receives an allocation from the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development. Funds are awarded through two categories: the Community Development category (competitive, applications accepted once per year) and the Special Projects category (for planning, economic development, and special projects, applications submitted anytime after written approval). Over a three-year period, the state must cumulatively use 70% of its allocation to benefit persons of low and moderate income. For SFY 2026/FFY 2025, the state received $7,416,560 allocated as follows: State Administration (2% + $100,000) $248,331; Technical Assistance (1%) $74,165; Community Development (82% - $100,000) $6,000,000; Special Projects (15%) $1,094,064. The State provides CDBG funds primarily as gap funding for projects selected by jurisdictions to meet their needs.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Community Development applications accepted once each year. Special Projects applications can be submitted at any time throughout the year after written approval.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Units of general local government in non-entitlement counties with a population of less than 200,000 and non-entitlement cities and towns of less than 50,000 population. Multiple jurisdictions may jointly apply. Other entities, public or private, may be sub-recipients of the eligible local government. Eligible subrecipients include governmental agencies such as housing authorities or municipalities; non-profit organizations with IRS Section 501(c)(3) status; for-profit businesses in Good Standing in Maryland for economic development projects; Community Based Development Organizations (CBDOs) and Community Housing Development Organizations (CHDOs) certified for new housing construction projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eligible projects generally fall into three types: housing, public facilities (water/sewer, streets, child care facilities, senior or community centers, shelters), and economic development projects. Specific eligible activities include: acquisition of real property; acquisition, construction, reconstruction, or installation of public works facilities; code enforcement; clearance, demolition, removal, reconstruction, and rehabilitation of buildings; removal of barriers restricting mobility and accessibility for elderly or handicapped persons; provision of new or quantifiable increase in public services; planning; payment of reasonable administrative costs; assistance to neighborhood-based nonprofit organizations and local development corporations; energy conservation projects; direct assistance to facilitate homeownership among LMI persons; housing services such as housing counseling and energy auditing. Ineligible activities include improvements to buildings used for general conduct of government, political activities, furnishings, and operations or maintenance of public facilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Units of general local government in non-entitlement counties with a population of less than 200,000 and non-entitlement cities and towns of less than 50,000 population. Ineligible counties: Anne Arundel, Baltimore, Harford, Howard, Montgomery and Prince George's (also applies to municipalities in these counties). Ineligible cities: Annapolis, Baltimore, Bowie, Cumberland, Frederick, Gaithersburg, Hagerstown and Salisbury. Projects must be located in a Maryland Priority Funding Area, except for public services; single family housing rehabilitation; acquisition, renovation and sale of existing houses; downpayment assistance; or where the Secretary of DHCD determines that the project is necessary to protect public health, alleviate personal economic hardship in an emergency, promote economically integrated housing, is consistent with an overall economic development strategy, or where an exception is necessary and has been granted through the Maryland Department of Planning exception process.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a unit of general local government in a non-entitlement county with population less than 200,000 or non-entitlement city/town with population less than 50,000

Project must meet one of three national objectives: benefit persons of low and moderate income, eliminate slum and blight, or meet an urgent need that is an immediate threat to community health, safety or welfare
Over a three-year period, state must cumulatively use 70% of allocation to benefit persons of low and moderate income
Proposed activities must be eligible under Title I of the Housing and Community Development Act of 1974, as amended
Project must be located in a Maryland Priority Funding Area (with limited exceptions)
Subrecipients must be eligible governmental agencies, nonprofits with 501(c)(3) status, for-profit businesses in Good Standing, or certified CBDOs/CHDOs
Non-profit organizations must have organizational by-laws and mission statements clearly stating they primarily serve LMI persons or a specific eligible population
Grantees must comply with the Uniform Relocation Assistance and Real Property Acquisition Policies Act of 1970 when acquiring property or displacing residents or businesses
Grantees spending more than $750,000 in federal funds must have a Single Audit prepared in conformance with 2 CFR Part 200
Environmental review must be completed prior to project initiation per National Environmental Policy Act
Grantees must comply with federal fair housing and equal opportunity laws and regulations
Construction projects with $200,000 or more in combined HUD funding must comply with Section 3 requirements (25% of labor hours by Section 3 workers, 5% by Targeted Section 3 workers)
Broadband infrastructure required for construction or substantial rehabilitation of buildings with more than 4 rental units (exceptions may apply)
For housing acquistion/renovation/resale programs, maximum CDBG funds per house is $200,000
For rental properties, rents must be affordable per HUD Fair Market Rents with affordability terms of 10-20 years depending on funding amount
For homeownership assistance, fixed-rate mortgages of minimum 30 years required, no subprime or adjustable-rate mortgages allowed, 8 hours of HUD-approved housing counseling required
Build America, Buy America (BABA) requirements apply to infrastructure projects (domestic procurement preferences for iron, steel, manufactured products and construction materials)
Grantees must have written Conflict of Interest Policy complying with federal standards and Maryland Public Ethics Law
No employee, officer or agent may participate in selection, award or administration of contracts if they have real or apparent conflict of interest
Generators must be installed if CDBG funds used for multi-family rental housing or government-owned facilities like senior centers
Housing rehabilitation programs limited to county governments with exceptions for active municipal programs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The State notifies eligible localities of the availability of funds and conducts training sessions on application development. Community Development applications are accepted once per year through a competitive process with formal rating and award procedures. Special Projects applications can be submitted at any time throughout the year after written approval has been received from CDBG program staff. Applications submitted must meet all eligibility requirements and include required exhibits such as Citizen Participation Plan, Public Hearing Notice, Local Resolution, Residential Anti-Displacement and Relocation Assistance Plan, Program Income Re-Use Plan, Certification Regarding Debarment and Suspension, and other required certifications depending on project type. Grantees must ensure environmental review is completed and Release of Funds issued by CDBG Environmental Officer prior to project initiation. Municipal or county governments may submit applications on behalf of subrecipients or businesses, which requires a risk analysis reviewing financial and administrative capacity of the entity.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grant opportunities to improve the livability and economic potential of Maryland communities through targeted investments in the physical environment that impact health and safety.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant opportunities for targeted investments in the physical environment that impact health and safety.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland communities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Targeted investments in the physical environment that impact health and safety to improve livability and economic potential.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that awards tax credit allocations to 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations to use as incentives attracting contributions from individuals and businesses for local projects and services. Donors contributing $500 or more receive tax credits equal to 50% of their contribution value, in addition to federal and state charitable tax deductions.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Nonprofit organizations receive competitive annual awards of Maryland state income tax credit allocations up to a maximum of $50,000 per award. Individual and business donors contributing $500 or more earn tax credits equal to 50% of the value of money, goods, or real property contributions. Tax credits must be used against taxes owed for the year the contribution was made and cannot be used retroactively. Awardees must raise double the amount of tax credits requested (e.g., $50,000 in credits requires $100,000 in donations). All CITC award contracts have a 24-month life. For FY2026 awards, the contract period runs from January 1, 2026, through December 31, 2027. A total of $1.75 million in Maryland income tax credits is available annually.
structured_extraction.program_audience: IRS designated 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations seeking to fund initiatives in Priority Funding Areas. Individual and business donors interested in making charitable contributions and receiving state tax credits.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects can be capital and/or operating initiatives including education and youth services, housing and community development, job and self-sufficiency training, neighborhood and business district enhancement, arts and culture and historic preservation, economic development and tourism promotion, technical assistance and capacity building, and services for at-risk populations. Eligible budget line items include staff costs, rent, utilities, program supplies, training, travel, construction soft costs such as planning, design, engineering, and permitting, as well as direct construction expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in or serve residents of a Priority Funding Area (PFA). For capital projects, the project site address must be located within a PFA boundary. For operating projects, organizations must document that clients reside within PFA boundaries and provide supporting documentation. Additional consideration given to initiatives in ENOUGH Act Grantee areas and Just Communities.
requirements_list: Applicant must be an IRS designated 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization with current determination letter
Organization must be in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
Organization must be registered as a charity with the Maryland Secretary of State or hold a religious exemption letter
Project must be located in or serve residents of a Priority Funding Area (PFA)
Donors must contribute $500 or more to be eligible for tax credits
Donors must obtain Donor Acknowledgement Form from nonprofit and submit completed form with contribution
Real property donors must contact nonprofit prior to making donation
Businesses conducting trade or business in Maryland subject to state income tax, public service company franchise tax, or insurance premiums tax are eligible donors
Individuals must be natural persons or fiduciaries with personal tax liability in Maryland
For capital projects, organization must demonstrate site control via deed, lease with lessor permission, or title/real estate settlement documents
Organization must maintain annual charitable registration and good standing status throughout award period
Organization must submit electronic Tax Credit Certification Request within 30 days of each donation
Organization must submit four semi-annual reports on July 10 and January 10 during the 24-month award period
Organization must maintain records for seven years following completion of award
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Nonprofit organizations submit competitive annual applications through the DHCD Project Portal online grants management system. New users must register through the portal; registration requests may take up to 72 hours for approval. Organization records and all required legal documents must be completed in the user profile before creating an application. Applications must include current articles of incorporation, bylaws, IRS 501(c)(3) determination letter, list of current board of directors and officers, charitable registration letter or religious exemption letter from Maryland Secretary of State, screenshot of SDAT good standing status, executed corporate resolution, Priority Funding Area maps for each project site, and evidence of site control for capital projects. All documents must be uploaded in PDF format. Applicants must provide a complete task and timeline table covering the entire 24-month award period and a detailed budget narrative corresponding to project activities. Applications are submitted online and only fully completed applications with all required documents are reviewed. Award announcements are made in Fall 2025. Awardees may not accept donations prior to January 1, 2026, or prior to the award agreement being fully executed, whichever occurs later.

structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Legacy program provides local governments and community development organizations with funding for essential projects aimed at strengthening communities through activities such as business retention and attraction, streetscape improvements, and residential rehabilitation.
Provides emergency rental assistance to eligible student households enrolled in Maryland community schools who are experiencing housing instability and homelessness.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Emergency rental assistance provided directly to eligible student households experiencing housing instability and homelessness who are enrolled in Maryland community schools.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Student households enrolled in Maryland community schools experiencing housing instability or homelessness
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Emergency rental assistance to help eligible student households maintain housing
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide, limited to households enrolled in Maryland community schools
requirements_list: Must be enrolled in a Maryland community school
Must be experiencing housing instability or homelessness

structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.program_description: Funding to support Community Action Agencies and other non-profit organizations in eliminating poverty, promoting self-sufficiency, and stimulating community revitalization, including training, technical assistance, and direct services. This program provides funds to seventeen Community Action Agencies across Maryland to help low-income individuals and families achieve self-sufficiency.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program distributes 90% of Maryland's allocated funds to designated Community Action Agencies. The state uses the other 5% for discretionary funding to support activities that fight poverty.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: The FY25 application round is closed. Check this page for information about future funding rounds.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland's designated Community Action Agencies, non-profit organizations, and local government units that serve low-income individuals and families.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support direct services for low-income individuals to help them become self-sufficient, including programs for employment, education, housing, and health. Funds can also support training, technical assistance, and community revitalization projects.
requirements_list: Services must benefit individuals and households with incomes at or below 200% of the federal poverty guidelines.
Community Action Agencies must have a specific board composition: one-third public officials, one-third representatives of low-income persons, and one-third from community groups.
Applicants for discretionary funds must propose a program with measurable outcomes for self-sufficiency.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The application period for fiscal year 2025 has closed. Check the program's webpage for information about future application opportunities.

structured_extraction.program_description: Supports local governments, community-based organizations, nonprofits, and anchor institutions in creating or upgrading computer labs and centers to provide public computer and internet access for underserved populations including individuals with disabilities, homeless individuals, veterans, and incarcerated or returning citizens.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $65,000 per application covering up to 100% of costs for creation, upgrade, and retrofit of computer labs and centers. Funding also available up to $10,000 for Internet Service Subscription costs for up to three years. At least 50% of those served must fall into covered populations: individuals with disabilities, homeless individuals, veterans, or incarcerated/returning citizens. Eligible uses include: computer equipment (desktops, laptops, keyboards, mice, monitors, webcams, headphones, microphones); networking equipment (routers, switches, network cables, Wi-Fi access points, firewalls); software (operating systems, office suites, educational/training software, antivirus); audiovisual equipment (projectors, screens, smartboards, speakers); assistive technology (screen readers, magnifiers, adaptive keyboards); marketing and outreach (up to 10% of total budget); operational expenses (payroll, supplies - up to 15%); administrative expenses (training, security monitoring - up to 15%). Total program funding: $2 million from American Rescue Plan Act funds.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, community-based organizations, nonprofits, and anchor institutions seeking to close the digital equity gap by providing public computer access for individuals with disabilities, homeless individuals, veterans, and incarcerated or returning citizens.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Creation, upgrade, and retrofit of computer labs and centers providing public computer and internet access. Eligible uses include computer equipment, networking equipment, internet service subscription (up to 3 years), software, audiovisual equipment, assistive technology, marketing and outreach (up to 10% of budget), operational expenses (up to 15%), and administrative expenses (up to 15%). Ineligible uses include utilities, rent, building construction or renovation, furniture, personal use items, travel, entertainment, political activities, and duplicative projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide across all Maryland counties
requirements_list: Applicant must be Maryland jurisdiction, incorporated municipality, local government agency delegated by local Maryland jurisdiction, not-for-profit IRS approved 501(c) entity providing services within Maryland, or Community Anchor Institution within Maryland
At least 50% of those served must be individuals with disabilities, homeless/unhoused individuals, veterans, or incarcerated/returning citizens
At least one of the covered populations must be primarily served
Project must be completed by December 31, 2026
Applicant must submit IRS W-9 Form and Certificate of Good Standing from Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation
Nonprofits must submit 501(c) documentation
All federal rules regarding American Rescue Plan Act funding must be adhered to
Computer equipment must come with standard manufacturer warranty or extended warranty
Internet service funding limited to wired internet connection only (no Wi-Fi hotspots)
Applicants may identify other funding sources to leverage available grant funding
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications must be submitted by November 29, 2024 at 11:59 PM ET. Submissions accepted electronically via email to osb.de@maryland.gov with subject line 'Maryland Computer Labs Program Application–[Organizational Applicant Name]', or by mail/hand delivery. Paper applications must show proof of mailing (USPS postmark, dated receipt, or commercial carrier receipt) or be hand-delivered Monday-Friday, 8:00 AM-4:00 PM ET to: Ronnie Hammond, Office of Statewide Broadband, Department of Housing and Community Development, 7800 Harkins Road, Lanham, MD 20706. Files should be converted to PDFs. Application must include: completed application form with organizational information, budget request, and project information; written executive summary and scope of work with timeline; detailed project budget showing operations, contracted services, and travel; IRS W-9 Form; 501(c) documents (nonprofits); Certificate of Good Standing; and all required attachments. Technical assistance available prior to November 22, 2024. OSB may contact applicants for clarification. Awardees will be notified beginning December 2024 and must execute a Memorandum of Understanding.

structured_extraction.program_name: Connect Maryland: FY23 Network Infrastructure Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants to local jurisdictions or their internet service provider partners to construct new broadband networks serving unserved households and businesses in Maryland at minimum speeds of 100 Mbps downstream and 100 Mbps upstream.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants between $800,000 and $4,500,000 covering 70% to 90% of capital construction costs for new broadband networks serving unserved homes and businesses. Match requirements vary based on infrastructure density: Wired projects require 10-30% match depending on premises per mile (fewer than 8 premises per mile = 10%, 8-14 premises per mile = 20%, 15+ premises per mile = 30%). Wireless projects require 10-30% match based on premises per tower (fewer than 40 premises per tower = 10%, 40-69 premises per tower = 20%, 70+ premises per tower = 30%). Match must be in cash, available upon grant agreement execution. Eligible capital expenses include construction of outside plant, last mile and middle mile infrastructure, electronic equipment, equipment shelters, wireless radios, antennae, and customer premises equipment. Operating expenses, tower purchases, land, buildings, building renovations, and customer devices are ineligible.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local jurisdictions, incorporated organizations recognized as partners by local jurisdictions, cooperatives, private corporations, limited liability companies, and other legal entities (except individuals and partnerships) seeking to serve unserved areas with broadband infrastructure
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital construction costs for new broadband network infrastructure including outside plant (fiber, coaxial, copper), last mile and middle mile infrastructure, electronic equipment (cabinets, switches, routers, wireless radios, antennae, access points, equipment shelters), customer premises equipment (ONTs, routers), and tower construction/structural improvements. Funds cannot be used for operating expenses, leases, bandwidth, spectrum costs, salaries unrelated to construction, customer devices, tower purchases, land acquisition, building purchases or renovations, or professional services unrelated to the project.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Unserved areas statewide where no broadband service currently exists at 100 Mbps download and 20 Mbps upload speeds. Areas having received state grant funding in prior broadband programs (2019-2021 Expansion, 2020-2021 Infrastructure, 2022 Neighborhood Connect, 2022 Infrastructure) are ineligible. Proposed Funded Service Area (PFSA) must be entirely unserved and can span single or multiple jurisdictions but need not be contiguous.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Maryland local jurisdiction, incorporated organization recognized as a partner by local jurisdiction, cooperative, private corporation, or limited liability company organized on for-profit or non-profit basis
Applicant must have legal capacity and authority to own and operate broadband facilities and enter into contracts
If partnering with another entity to operate the system, a draft or final agreement addressing specific financial terms and entity qualifications must be provided with application
Service area must have no broadband service currently available (verified by OSB prior to award)

Must serve all premises in PFSA at minimum 100 Mbps downstream and 100 Mbps upstream (100x100) with maximum 50 millisecond latency, or reduced requirement of 100 Mbps down and 20 Mbps up if scalable to 100x100 and applicant submits certification of circumstances preventing full speeds
Minimum grant request: $800,000; Maximum grant request: $4,500,000
Match requirement of 10%-30% in cash based on infrastructure density (wired or wireless)
All equipment and materials must be new and non-depreciated
Project must be commenced by September 1, 2023 and completed by August 31, 2026
Applicant must obtain all necessary federal, state, and local permits, licenses, and approvals prior to commencement
Areas previously funded through state broadband programs are ineligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications must include: (A) Completed Broadband Grant Application Form (Schedule A-1), IRS Form W-9, evidence of legal existence and good standing, and local jurisdiction partnership letter; (B) Executive Summary describing PFSA, project benefits, applicant history, and partnership details; (C) Scoring Criteria Documentation; (D) System Design with network diagram; (E) Service Area Demographics and map; (F) Scope of Work including construction milestones (Schedule F-1) and project budget (Schedule F-2); (G) Financial Information and Sustainability including historical and pro forma financial statements (Schedule G-1) and assumptions (Schedule G-2); (H) Statement of Experience; (I) Evidence of Other Funding Commitments; (J) Reporting and Compliance documentation. Applications must be submitted postmarked, shipped, or emailed by December 5, 2022 at 11:59pm ET. Paper applications with original signatures and USB flash drive can be mailed to Kenrick M. Gordon, P.E., Director, OSB, DHCD, 7800 Harkins Road, Lanham, MD 20706. Electronic applications should be emailed to OSB.MD@maryland.gov with subject line "Maryland Network Infrastructure Grant Application – your company name" and files zipped or split into multiple emails if too large. Technical assistance available until November 18, 2022. Completed applications submitted after deadline will not be considered.

structured_extraction.program_name: Connect Maryland: FY24 Network Infrastructure Grant Program – Smith Island
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants to local jurisdictions or their internet service provider partners to construct new broadband networks serving unserved households and businesses specifically on Smith Island. The program aims to deploy broadband infrastructure at speeds of 100 Mbps downstream and 100 Mbps upstream (or 100 Mbps down and 20 Mbps up if scalable to symmetrical speeds) to all unserved premises on the island.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants between $1 million and $3 million covering up to 90% of capital construction costs for new broadband networks on Smith Island. Applicants must provide at least 10% cash match (11.11% of the requested grant amount) of capital construction costs. Grant funds may be used for construction of outside plant (last mile and middle mile infrastructure), electronic equipment necessary to deliver service (OLTs, ONTs, routers, switches, firewalls, wireless radios, antennas, equipment cabinets, shelters), and other capital costs directly necessary to provide broadband service. Tower construction and structural improvements may be treated as match. Funds are disbursed on a reimbursement basis as the project progresses, with at least 50% of grant funds required to be expended by the second anniversary of the grant agreement effective date.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Kenrick M. Gordon, P.E., Director, Office of Statewide Broadband
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local jurisdictions, incorporated organizations recognized as partners by local jurisdictions, cooperatives, private corporations, limited liability companies, and other legal entities (except individuals or partnerships) on Smith Island seeking to construct broadband infrastructure
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital construction costs for new broadband network infrastructure including outside plant deployment (fiber optic cabling, conduit, poles), electronic equipment (OLTs, ONTs, routers, switches, firewalls, wireless radios, antennas, equipment shelters and cabinets), middle mile infrastructure, customer drops, and engineering costs directly necessary to provide broadband service at the required speeds to all unserved residents, businesses, and anchor institutions on Smith Island. Eligible capital expenses must be for new, non-depreciated items. Ineligible uses include operating expenses, bandwidth costs, leases, salaries, purchase or leasing of towers or land, building purchases or renovations, and customer premise equipment beyond the ONT or fixed wireless antenna.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Smith Island, Maryland (Somerset County). The Identified Service Area (ISA) includes all locations on Smith Island. Applications must serve the entire ISA where broadband service does not currently exist at 100 Mbps download and 20 Mbps upload speeds or higher. Latitude/longitude coordinates for each location requiring service are provided in the application package.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local jurisdiction, an incorporated organization recognized as a partner by the local jurisdiction, a cooperative legally formed in Maryland and recognized as a partner by the local jurisdiction, a limited liability company recognized as a partner by the local jurisdiction, or other legal entity recognized as a partner by the local jurisdiction (not an individual or partnership)
Service area must be Smith Island and project must serve all unserved premises in the Identified Service Area
Minimum 10% cash match (11.11% of requested grant amount) of capital construction costs required; match must be available cash and cannot fund operational costs except as specified in guidelines

Applicant must provide evidence of good standing and legal existence (corporations/LLCs must provide Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation corporate information showing good standing; local jurisdictions recognized by Maryland Manual On-Line are recognized as having legal existence)
Applicant must have a current IRS Form W-9 and Unique Entity ID from SAM.gov

Local jurisdiction partnerships require a letter from the sponsoring jurisdiction acknowledging the partnership, extent of participation, and support offered; legal agreements between local jurisdiction and applicant must be provided

If applicant is seeking to partner with another entity to operate the system, a draft agreement or final agreement must be provided addressing specific financial terms and identifying the specific entity or entities with their qualifications to operate the system
Applicant must demonstrate legal capacity and authority to own and operate the broadband facilities, enter into contracts, and comply with applicable federal or state statutes and regulations

Project must provide minimum 100 Mbps download and 100 Mbps upload speeds with maximum 50 millisecond latency, or meet reduced requirements (100 Mbps down, 20 Mbps up) if scalable to symmetrical speeds with certificate explaining circumstances preventing minimum connectivity
Network must be capable of providing minimum connectivity to all subscribers; subscriber offerings of less than minimum are allowable only in conjunction with offerings meeting or exceeding minimum

In the past four years, applicant must not have been debarred by any federal, state, or local government entity and must not be subject to civil claims for non-payment with potential or realized value of $30,000 or more
All costs incurred before submission of completed application or before grant approval are ineligible for funding; only new, non-depreciated equipment and materials eligible

If other federal funds have been awarded for broadband construction within the ISA, those federal funds can only be supplemented, not supplanted; any grant cannot supplant previously awarded federal funds
Applicant must commence project by September 1, 2024 and complete by August 31, 2027
Grant funds must be used only for approved project and approved area in accordance with eligible purposes and project budget
Prior to project commencement, applicant must obtain all federal, state, and local government approvals, permits, and licenses
Upon project completion, applicant must obtain all certifications, licenses, permits, and approvals necessary to operate the project
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Submit a completed application package by 11:59pm ET on January 31, 2024 (postmarked, shipped, or received via email). 2. Applications must include: Broadband Grant Application Form (Schedule A-1), IRS Form W-9, evidence of good standing and legal existence, Executive Summary of the project, Scoring Criteria Documentation, System Design with network diagram, Scope of Work with construction build-out milestones and project budget, Financial Information and Sustainability (historical and pro forma financial statements), Statement of Experience, and Evidence of Funding Commitments from other sources. 3. Applications may be submitted by: (a) postmarked or shipped paper copy with original signatures accompanied by electronic version on USB Flash Drive to Kenrick M. Gordon, P.E., Director, OSB, Department of Housing and Community Development, 7800 Harkins Road, Lanham, MD 20706; or (b) email to OSB.MD@maryland.gov with subject line 'Maryland Network Infrastructure Grant Application – Smith Island – your company name' with files attached as zipped file and converted to PDFs (except formats specifically called out in guidelines). Paper applications must show proof of mailing or shipping via USPS postmark, legible mail receipt dated by USPS, or dated shipping label from commercial carrier. 4. Prior to submission, applicants may request technical assistance before January 19, 2024. Technical assistance is not meant to create or edit applications or determine eligibility. 5. Applicants submitting late will be notified applications will not be considered and will be returned. 6. Applications will be scored on criteria including Project Strength, Organizational Capacity, Financial Sustainability, and Community Benefit. Maximum score is 200 points. Awards will be made on a competitive basis from highest to lowest scores as funding permits. 7. Selected applicants must enter into a grant agreement with the Department before funds are disbursed. 8. Grant funds are disbursed on a reimbursement basis as project progresses based on requests for disbursement with supporting invoices and documentation.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants of internet-enabled devices to counties and municipal governments for distribution to eligible low-income households. The program aims to bridge the digital equity gap by providing devices to families who cannot afford the cost. Funded through American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds with $30 million appropriated by the State of Maryland.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of internet-enabled devices (HP Chromebook 14 G7 or similar) provided by the State to counties and municipal governments for distribution to eligible households. Device cost is $198.75 per device. Recipients receive an additional $6 per device stipend to assist with distribution costs (storage, security, venue, and personnel). Eligible households must have incomes at or below 200% of federal poverty guidelines or be enrolled in qualifying government assistance programs. One device per address/MDU unit maximum. Round two application deadline was September 29, 2023. Approximately 145,000 devices total procured; first round approved 91,300 chromebooks. Performance period is six months from delivery of first device shipment; devices must be distributed within that timeframe or returned at awardee's cost.
structured_extraction.program_audience: County and municipal governments distributing devices to eligible low-income households
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Distribution of internet-enabled devices to households with incomes at or below 200% of federal poverty guidelines. Stipend may be used for: cost of securing devices in storage, cost of securing devices during distribution, cost of distribution venue, and personnel costs associated with distribution.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide - all Maryland jurisdictions eligible
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Maryland local jurisdiction (county or municipal government) listed on the Maryland Manual On-Line website

Eligible households must have income at or below 200% of federal poverty guidelines OR be enrolled in Affordable Connectivity Program (ACP) OR participate in qualifying government assistance programs (SNAP, Medicaid, WIC, SSI, FPHA, Veterans Pension and Survivors Benefit, Free/Reduced-Price School Lunch Program, or received Federal Pell Grant in current award year)
One device per address or recognized MDU unit maximum
Applicant must be registered in System for Award Management (SAM) and maintain active registration
Applicant must provide valid DUNS number
Applicant must develop and implement eligibility verification process
Applicant must have secure storage facility with loading/unloading capabilities
Applicant must inspect devices upon receipt and notify OSB of any damage immediately
Applicant must develop outreach program to inform targeted population of program eligibility and distribution details
Applicant must use Department Device Tracking Portal for address verification during distribution
Devices must be distributed within six months of first delivery
Any devices not distributed within six months must be returned at awardee's cost
Applicant must maintain record-keeping documentation of distribution and eligibility verification for six-month performance period
If municipality and county both apply, they must coordinate efforts to ensure complementary and not conflicting distribution
New eligible applicants receive priority review over returning applicants in round two
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications must be submitted by September 29, 2023 at 11:59 PM ET via email to OSB.MD@maryland.gov (subject line: Maryland Connected Devices Program Application – your jurisdictional name) or via USPS/commercial carrier to Ronnie Hammond, OSB of Statewide Broadband, DHCD, 7800 Harkins Road, Lanham, MD 20706. Electronic submission is preferred. Paper applications must show proof of mailing via USPS postmark, dated mail receipt, or commercial carrier receipt dated on or before deadline. Application must include completed application form (with EIN, DUNS, SAM.gov unique identifier), written project narrative (executive summary not exceeding 2 pages, verification and distribution methodology, scope of work, outreach program, potential barriers, partners and local engagement, intended outcomes and metrics, project schedule), scope of work detailing partnerships, data collection, storage, distribution method, eligibility verification, and methodology to ensure one device per household, monthly device delivery schedule, and Federal Form W-9. Application completeness is required; missing information may result in ineligibility. Technical assistance available prior to September 22, 2023 by contacting Ronnie Hammond. Selected applicants must execute Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with Department. Successful applicants chosen based on qualifications, evaluation of responses, and possible interview. Awardees receive devices in up to five monthly shipments over five-month period.

structured_extraction.program_name: EmPOWER Maryland Limited Income Energy Efficiency Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides energy efficiency upgrades and repairs to homes at no charge for limited income households. The program installs materials and equipment to reduce energy use, lower monthly power bills, improve comfort, and enhance air quality and family health.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides energy efficiency upgrades at no charge to eligible homeowners. Services include installation of insulation in attic, floors and walls, hot water system improvements, lighting retrofits, furnace cleaning and tuning, safety repairs, refrigerator retrofit if applicable, and health and safety items. The program begins with a free energy audit to identify the most effective energy-saving measures, followed by contractor work to complete recommended improvements, and a final evaluation to ensure the home is operating more efficiently. There are two application tracks: a Quick Application for those already receiving benefits from participating assistance programs, and a Standard Application for general applicants. The Quick Application requires Client Information, Household Income Information, Energy Consent Form, copy of most recent electric utility bill, and copy of benefit approval notice. The Standard Application requires more comprehensive documentation including proof of last 30 days gross household income, Social Security cards for all household members, Photo ID for applicant, and various other financial and home ownership documents depending on whether repairs beyond energy efficiency are needed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Limited income households in Maryland who are customers of participating utility companies (BGE, Delmarva Power, FirstEnergy, Pepco, SMECO, or Washington Gas).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency upgrades and repairs to homes including attic, floor and wall insulation; hot water system improvements; lighting retrofits; furnace cleaning, tuning and safety repairs; refrigerator retrofit; and health and safety items.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be customers of one of six participating utility companies: BGE, Delmarva Power, FirstEnergy, Pepco, SMECO, or Washington Gas. Geographical eligibility for certain areas also applies. Applications are submitted to Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, Attn: Weatherization, 7800 Harkins Road - Lanham, MD 20706.
requirements_list: Household income must be at or below 250% Federal Poverty Level based on family size (ranging from $72,950 for a family of one to $165,050 for a family of ten, with $13,750 added for each additional person beyond ten)
Must have a utility account with one of six participating companies: BGE, Delmarva Power, FirstEnergy, Pepco, SMECO, or Washington Gas

Automatically income-eligible if currently participating in: Utility Bill Pay Assistance through OHEP, Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF), Supplemental Security Income (SSI), HUD housing assistance programs, Fuel Fund Assistance, DHCD Rehab Programs, Baltimore Lead Hazard Control Program, Medicaid, MEA Energy Equity Grant, or MEEHA
Must have power to the home
Homeowners or renters eligible (landlord information required for renters)
For Quick Application track: Must currently receive benefits from participating assistance programs
For Standard Application track: Must provide proof of last 30 days gross household income, Social Security cards for all household members, and Photo ID
If claiming zero income: Must provide signed and notarized Zero Income Form
May have documented medical condition requiring functioning heating, cooling, or water heating systems (physician's letter required)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants can apply through one of two tracks. Quick Application: Applicants who currently receive benefits from participating programs (Utility Bill Pay Assistance through OHEP, SNAP, TANF, SSI, HUD housing assistance, Fuel Fund Assistance, DHCD Rehab Programs, Baltimore Lead Hazard Control Program, Medicaid, MEA Energy Equity Grant, or MEEHA) can complete the Quick Application online through the application portal or submit a paper application with Client Information, Household Income Information, Energy Consent Form, copy of most recent electric utility bill, and copy of benefit approval notice. Alternatively, if approved to receive Energy Assistance payments from Maryland Department of Human Services, applicants may contact the intake line at 1-855-583-8976. Standard Application: All other applicants complete the Standard Application which requires more comprehensive documentation. Submit complete application to Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, Attn: Weatherization, 7800 Harkins Road - Lanham, MD 20706, or call 1-855-583-8976. Once determined eligible, a local agency will contact the household to schedule an energy audit, discuss results, schedule contractor work for recommended improvements, and conduct a final evaluation of the home.

structured_extraction.program_name: FY24 Home Stretch - Difficult to Serve Properties Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants to county jurisdictions to assist with capital construction costs for installing broadband service to remote or geographically isolated properties that have difficulty obtaining service from commercial internet service providers. The program utilizes $24,223,815 of Coronavirus Capital Projects Fund (ARPA/CPF) to enable difficult to serve premises to connect to broadband infrastructure that is available nearby but not easily accessible.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $1,100,000 per eligible county jurisdiction applicant for capital construction costs of broadband infrastructure. Maximum funding per individual premises location is $8,000. Applicants must provide 25% match of eligible project costs, which can come from the local jurisdiction, ISP partner, property owner, or combination of these sources. Match must be in the form of cash; in-kind matches are not acceptable. County jurisdictions develop sub-grant program with ISP partner(s) and must establish program guidelines including end user selection process, assistance for low-income residents, and ACP (Affordable Connectivity Program) promotion. Projects must be completed by December 31, 2025.
structured_extraction.program_audience: County jurisdictions serving difficult-to-reach or remote areas in partnership with Internet Service Providers
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital construction costs for installation of broadband service infrastructure to connect unserved difficult to serve premises to existing broadband networks. Eligible uses include: construction of facilities for service deployment to difficult to serve premises; electronics and equipment necessary to deliver service including optical network terminals (ONTs), routers, switches, firewalls, wireless radio equipment, antennae, access points, modems, and necessary equipment shelters; minor extensions of ISP existing infrastructure. All equipment and materials must be new and non-depreciated. Ineligible uses include: duplication of existing service, middle-mile infrastructure, telephone or video service expenses, land or tower purchases, building construction or renovations, and operating expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide for remote or geographically isolated properties lacking terrestrial fixed internet service at speeds of 100 Mbps download and 20 Mbps upload with latency above 50 milliseconds.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local county jurisdiction with an established partnership with one or more Internet Service Providers

Property must be unserved (lacking broadband at 100 Mbps download and 20 Mbps upload with latency at or below 50ms) and have difficulty obtaining service due to remoteness, distance from infrastructure, or geographic issues
Maximum $8,000 funding per individual difficult to serve premises location
Maximum $1,100,000 total funding per eligible applicant
25% match of eligible project costs required from any combination of local jurisdiction, ISP partner, property owner, or other sources (match must be cash, not in-kind)

Projects must be capable of delivering minimum 100 Mbps download and 100 Mbps upload with maximum 50ms latency, or with certification, 100 Mbps download and 20 Mbps upload with maximum 50ms latency (network must be scalable to 100 Mbps symmetrical speeds)
All partnering ISPs must participate in federal Affordable Connectivity Program (ACP)
Applicants must develop jurisdictional-specific funding program including end user selection process, low-income assistance options, and ACP promotion
No duplication of any existing broadband service from other entities or other state, local, or federal funding for the same location
Applicant must have legal authority to enter partnership with ISP partner prior to funding agreement execution
Applicant responsible for all non-capital expenses related to state and federal reporting and ongoing administrative costs for project duration
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Local county jurisdiction must establish partnership with Internet Service Provider(s) prior to application. 2. Submit one electronic PDF copy of complete application response to osb.md@maryland.gov by December 22, 2023, with subject line including 'Difficult to Serve Premises Grant Application' and local county jurisdiction name. 3. Application must include: Grant Application Form (fillable PDF available at https://dhcd.maryland.gov/broadband); Executive Summary describing unserved premises, demographics, problems addressed, and project benefits; Application Partnership statement naming ISP partner(s) and describing applicant cooperation; Experience statement from senior team members (both applicant and ISP partner); Network Discussion describing ISP network, technology, speed capabilities, and offerings; Subscriber Profile with description of locations and demographic data; Subscriber Costs and Limitations listing ISP service options, costs, and any data caps or service limitations; Budget with capital construction cost estimates; Program Overview with detailed program design including end user selection, low-income assistance, ACP promotion and assistance, and ISP billing methods; Proposed Implementation Schedule with timeline and key milestones (assuming Spring 2024 start); IRS W-9 Form and SAM.gov registration documentation. 4. Combine all application materials into single zip file to ensure submission integrity. 5. Applications will be scored on 45-point scale based on: Need for Service and Project Benefits (0-5 points); Match Contribution Source and Percentage (0-15 points); Network Delivery Speed (0-5 points); Subscriber Options and Affordability (0-20 points). 6. Awards expected February 2024. Applications must address all required sections; incomplete applications may be deemed ineligible.
