structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program that provides funding to state and local governments to support affordable housing. Funds can be used to build, buy, or fix rental housing, owner-occupied housing, and special needs housing such as group homes. HOME funds are used to increase the number of housing units for very low income individuals and households, with targeting for the lowest income households.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: HOME funds are typically provided as non-interest bearing deferred loans with terms ranging from 20 to 40 years depending on the type of housing financed. Funds may also be provided as amortizing loans, recoverable grants requiring repayment when property is sold or stops being used for low-income housing, or as outright grants at the State's discretion. For rental projects, equity sharing may be required when low-income usage is discontinued. The maximum amount of assistance to a single project generally will not exceed the amount needed to make the project viable and comply with federal HOME regulations. The number of income-restricted units is usually calculated by dividing the amount of HOME funds by the total project cost, then multiplying by the total number of units in the project. If the property is sold or stops being used for low-income housing, the borrower must share any equity gain with DHCD. HOME funds may be used as non-interest bearing or deferred loans, other flexible terms, amortizing loans, or recoverable grants. HOME funds are allocated among Multifamily Housing Programs, Single Family Programs, and administrative expenses. Multifamily rental housing projects use HOME funds in conjunction with the Rental Housing Fund. Single Family Programs include homeownership projects, group homes for special needs, rehabilitation programs, and may provide soft seconds to reduce home costs. HOME funds may be used for tenant-based rental assistance, security deposit assistance, and disaster relief on a limited basis.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Dale Quisgard, HOME Program Manager; Kiaya Nickens, Program Manager
structured_extraction.program_audience: State government agencies, local governments, local housing agencies, nonprofit organizations, Community Housing Development Organizations (CHDOs), and developers seeking to develop affordable housing for very low income households.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Build, buy, or rehabilitate rental housing, owner-occupied housing, special needs housing such as group homes, acquisition of property for resale or rental, soft seconds for homeownership, land acquisition, development costs, construction financing, group home projects, single-family rehabilitation, replacement housing, tenant-based rental assistance, security deposit assistance, and disaster relief assistance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland with primary use in non-Participating Jurisdictions. Non-Participating Jurisdictions include the entire State except for Baltimore City and Anne Arundel (except for the City of Annapolis), Baltimore, Harford, Howard, Montgomery, and Prince George's counties, which receive direct HOME allocations. State government agencies are automatically eligible for HOME funds and receive either their formula allocation or $3 million, whichever is greater.
requirements_list: For rental housing units, resident household incomes must be at or below 80 percent of area median household income adjusted for household size
For owner-occupied housing units, owner household income must be at or below 80 percent of area median household income adjusted for household size
Income limits are based on household size and set annually by HUD
If using HOME funds with other CDA programs, projects must meet both CDA program eligibility requirements and HOME program federal requirements
Eligible applicants include state government agencies, local governments, local housing agencies, and nonprofit organizations
Applications from Community Housing Development Organizations (CHDOs) and non-profit organizations receive priority for HOME Special Reserve Fund
CHDOs must be certified by the State and meet HUD-established qualifying criteria
Properties must comply with maximum rent limits established by HUD
Projects receiving HOME funds must meet federal HOME monitoring and reporting requirements including site inspections and tenant certifications
Borrowers must share any equity gains with DHCD if property is sold or stops being used for low-income housing
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Program Manager (Dale Quisgard at dale.quisgard@maryland.gov or 301-429-7797, or Kiaya Nickens at kiaya.nickens@maryland.gov or 301-429-7809) for application details and guidance. State government agencies are automatically eligible. Other eligible applicants including local governments, non-profits, and CHDOs should contact DHCD with project proposals. HOME Special Reserve Fund applications are reviewed and allocated on a first-come, first-serve basis with priority given to CHDOs and non-profit organizations. Applications may be submitted as part of DHCD's existing housing program application process, or DHCD may propose HOME funds during project evaluation. Funds are allocated to program areas for up to eight months, after which unencumbered funds may be moved to meet additional demand or for special projects.

structured_extraction.program_name: Home Stretch - Affordable Housing Grant (Expanded Round - FY24)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants to municipal and nonprofit owners of public housing and internet service providers to install broadband-capable wiring and common area Wi-Fi to individual dwelling units and common areas, addressing digital equity gaps in affordable housing communities. Funding supports internal wiring upgrades, common area Wi-Fi installation, and external infrastructure improvements to enable high-speed broadband access for low-income residents.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants between $250,000 and $5,000,000 covering up to 95% of eligible project costs for broadband-capable wiring installation and common area Wi-Fi. Applicants must provide a minimum 5% match of eligible project costs. Total program funding: $26.9 million. Eligible uses include internal wiring upgrades (replacing outdated wiring with fiber optic or high-speed cabling, installing network switches and routers), common area Wi-Fi installation (free to residents), and external infrastructure work including up to 2 miles of fiber extension from nearest existing infrastructure. Ineligible uses include operational expenses, backhaul charges, ongoing data transport costs, customer support costs, and personal devices for residents.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Municipal and nonprofit owners of public housing and internet service providers serving low-income multi-dwelling units (MDUs)
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of broadband-capable wiring to individual dwelling units, installation or upgrade of robust Wi-Fi networks in common areas (free to residents), replacement of outdated wiring with fiber optic or high-speed cabling, installation of network switches and routers, external infrastructure improvements including fiber extension up to 2 miles, and engineering costs tied to funded capital assets. Common area Wi-Fi must provide high-speed internet access with security measures to protect resident data.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; all Maryland counties eligible. Projects must serve municipally owned or non-profit low-income multi-dwelling units (MDUs).
requirements_list: Applicant must be existing Internet Service Provider actively offering high-speed internet services over own physical network infrastructure to eligible municipally owned/non-profit low-income MDUs
Applicant must provide strong letter of support from property owner (municipal or non-profit)
MDU must be operated by municipally owned or non-profit organization with mission to provide affordable housing; non-profits must provide IRS 501(c)(3) or similar documentation
5% minimum match of eligible project costs required (up to 95% grant coverage)

Provide minimum speed of 100/100 Mbps with maximum latency of 50 milliseconds (or 100/20 Mbps if network is scalable to 100/100 symmetrical based on future technology advances; ISPs unable to achieve minimum must submit Certificate explaining circumstances related to geography, topography, or excessive cost)
Offer low-price/affordable internet plans specifically for low-income residents
Offer affordable pricing for different tiers of speed starting at 100/20 Mbps
Demonstrate technical expertise and capability to upgrade internal wiring and common area Wi-Fi infrastructure
Have track record of successfully completing similar projects
Demonstrate financial stability to ensure project completion and sustainability
Comply with all federal, state, and local regulations related to broadband services and grant funding, specifically Treasury CPF rules
Demonstrate excellent record of compliance with federal, state, and local regulations
Project budget must be justified and based on scope of work, project goals, and reasonable costs
Provide detailed line item capital construction budget
Provide sustainability plan outlining maintenance and long-term access to high-speed internet for residents

Provide financial information covering 3 years historical data and 3-5 years projected data including balance sheets, income statements, cash flow statements, funding sources, financial risks and mitigation plan, and long-term financial viability plan
Common area Wi-Fi must be free to use for all residents with sufficient coverage and security measures

Project must prioritize MDUs based on income levels of residents, current internet access quality, geographic location in underserved areas, vulnerable populations served, building condition and infrastructure needs, community engagement and support, and number of residents served
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications open October 31, 2024 and close January 31, 2025. Submit all completed applications and supporting documents via email to OSB.MD@Maryland.gov. Application must include: completed and signed application form, executive summary, statement of experience, letter of support from property owners, project proposal, MDU prioritization information with physical assessment results, detailed network design, engineering diagrams, community profile, subscriber cost information, potential barriers and risks with mitigation strategies, partners and local engagement details, project schedule, funding scope and budget, sustainability plan, financial information (3 years historical and 3-5 years projected data), IRS Form W-9, and Schedule F-2. Only complete applications at submission will be considered for funding. Funding announcements will be made on or before February 28, 2025. For feasible proposals scoring well in other categories, OSB may request revision of proposals to fix any technical issues before final consideration.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants to owners of public housing to install broadband-capable wiring to individual dwelling units, addressing digital equity gaps in low-income public housing communities. The program supports the installation of internal wiring infrastructure, wireless access points in common areas, and community engagement to promote broadband adoption.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants between $500,000 and $9,000,000 covering up to 95% of eligible project capital construction costs. Applicants must provide a minimum 5% cash match of actual capital construction costs. Match funds must come from eligible grant purposes and can include other state or federal funds. Non-capital administrative costs are capped at 1% of total project costs, with community engagement costs capped at 3% not to exceed $15,000. Grants reimburse eligible project expenses after review of project progress or completion reports and supporting documentation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local jurisdictions (county or municipal), including recognized jurisdictional housing authorities, that own and maintain a stock of publicly supported housing for low- and moderate-income households
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of broadband-capable wiring to individual dwelling units; installation of fiber optic facilities to serve public housing buildings; installation of wireless access points for free internet service in common areas; building modifications necessary for electronic equipment distribution; outreach to encourage broadband adoption including ACP registration assistance; all broadband networking equipment (hardware, software, wireless access points, modems, switches, routers, firewalls); low voltage contracting work including inside wiring installation; broadband network engineering and design documentation; installation and provisioning labor costs; taxes, shipping and insurance costs directly related to broadband network equipment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide - all Maryland counties eligible. Projects must serve publicly owned housing developments identified as having a need for additional broadband investment, including lack of access to connections reliably meeting minimum internet connectivity of 100 Mbps download and 20 Mbps upload speeds.
requirements_list: Applicant must be owner of publicly owned housing development (not publicly supported but not publicly owned)
5% minimum cash match of actual capital construction costs required
Projects must provide minimum internet connectivity of 100 Mbps download and 100 Mbps upload with maximum 50 milliseconds latency at each dwelling unit
Applicant must agree to maintain and secure project equipment for at least 5 years after project completion
Wireless access points required in public and common areas providing free broadband service
Community engagement strategies and ACP registration assistance required during project development
All equipment purchased must be new and non-depreciated
Network must be designed for open access use from cabinet to individual unit
Projects must be completed by June 30, 2026
Detailed project plan with timeline including construction, installation, provisioning, testing, and closeout required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must submit one electronic PDF copy of complete application to osb.md@maryland.gov by December 22, 2023. Application subject line must include 'Broadband for Public Housing', local jurisdiction name, and project name. Application must include: completed application form, executive summary, statement of experience, network design with diagram, community profile and engagement strategies, subscriber cost information if applicable, identification of potential barriers, list of partners and their involvement, project implementation schedule, funding scope and line-item capital construction budget using provided form. All required documentation must be submitted; incomplete applications will not be considered for approval. Applications will be scored on a 40-point scale based on project description, community need, experience and capacity, schedule feasibility, and budget reasonableness. Awards are anticipated in February 2024.

structured_extraction.program_name: Homeowner Assistance Fund (HAF) WholeHome Critical Home Repairs Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that helps eligible Maryland homeowners facing financial hardship due to the COVID-19 pandemic pay for critical repairs in their primary residences that could lead to displacement if not addressed. Repairs covered include heating and cooling systems, water heaters, electrical and plumbing or septic issues, roof repairs, mold and mildew remediation, lead paint and asbestos removal, and structural maintenance issues. Without addressing these critical repairs, homeowners would be involuntarily displaced from their properties.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant of up to $10,000 per homeowner for critical home repairs. In cases of extenuating circumstances, grants up to $15,000 may be awarded on a case-by-case basis with documentation of need. Grants are processed on a first-come, first-served basis. No deed of trust is recorded as this is grant assistance with no lien on the property. Applicants can choose between 33% deposit with 67% at completion or 0% deposit with 100% at completion payment options.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications Closed - April 2, 2026 (closed early because funds ran out)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners who own and live in their primary residence, experienced financial hardship after January 21, 2020, and have income at or below 150% of their county's area median income. This is one-time financial assistance per household.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Critical repairs to primary residences including non-functioning heating and cooling systems, water heaters, electrical and plumbing or septic repairs, roof repair or replacement, mold and mildew remediation, lead paint and asbestos removal, structural and maintenance issues, trip/slip hazard mitigation, and asbestos removal. Funds cannot be used for remodeling, general improvements, or reimbursement of work already completed or deposits already made.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide for homeowners with income at or below 150% of their county's area median income. Income limits vary by county and household size and are listed in the HAF 150% AMI Low Income Limits chart.
requirements_list: Experienced financial hardship due to COVID-19 after January 21, 2020
Income at or below 150% of County Area Median Income (AMI) based on household size
Must be a Maryland homeowner
Must reside in the primary residence and occupy the property
Must be named on the deed of trust
Critical repair must be one that would cause involuntary displacement if not addressed
Must provide a work proposal for the critical repair from a licensed and insured Maryland Home Improvement Contractor with photos or drawings
Work proposal estimate must be dated within the last 60 days
Contractor must be currently licensed as a Maryland Home Improvement Contractor or hold appropriate trade license (Electrical, Plumbing, HVAC, etc.)
Contractor must be in good standing with the State of Maryland
Contractor must provide active limited liability insurance with per occurrence limits equal to or greater than $1 million
If other individuals are named on the deed but do not occupy the property, proof must be provided that they live elsewhere
Payments or deposits made by homeowners for work or materials will NOT be reimbursed
This is one-time financial assistance per household
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Complete the WholeHome Homeowner Assistance Fund (HAF) application form. 2. Provide income documentation (paystubs, tax returns, award letters, or zero income statement). 3. Provide proof of COVID-19 financial hardship after January 21, 2020. 4. Obtain at least one detailed estimate from a licensed Maryland Home Improvement Contractor dated within the past 60 days that includes photographs documenting the critical repairs, contractor's phone number and email address, and scope of work. 5. Contractor must provide: copy of current MHIC or trade license, Certificate of Liability Insurance (COI) with per occurrence limits of $1 million or greater, Letter of Good Standing from Maryland, completed and signed W-9, and bid cover page. 6. Submit completed application and all required documentation via email to Rehab.HAFApplications@Maryland.gov or mail to Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, CDA Special Loan Programs- Rehab Homeowner Assistance Fund (HAF), 7800 Harkins Road, 3rd Floor, Lanham, MD 20706. 7. DHCD staff will review estimate to verify work meets health and safety requirements and contractor meets state requirements. 8. Once approved, applicant must sign commitment letter, grant agreement, rehabilitation contract, W-9 form, and final invoice from contractor. Applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis.

list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low- or no-interest loans provided through the Housing Innovation Fund to support new construction, acquisition, and rehabilitation of rental housing. Loans are available in two structures: (1) Short-term loans for 3-5 years at approximately 3% interest rate, or (2) Longer-term loans for 7-10 years at approximately 5.5% interest rate. Interest rates are subject to change. Loans are subordinate loans with positioning considered on a case-by-case basis. Maximum award per project is $2,500,000. Projects must provide mixed-income, cross-subsidized housing with at least 20% of units for households earning 50% or less of area median income, or at least 40% of units for households earning 60% or less of area median income. DHCD will select up to 3 projects to receive assistance with only 1 award per jurisdiction. $5 million in FY 2026 funds is available.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public housing authorities and county governments, optionally partnering with housing developers
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: New construction and acquisition or rehabilitation of rental housing including apartment buildings, townhouses, single-family homes, single room occupancy buildings, and shared housing facilities that provide mixed-income, cross-subsidized housing. Funds may be used to acquire existing private-sector housing to increase housing production.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland
requirements_list: Applicant must be a public housing authority or county government
County must partner with a local housing authority or housing developer, or sponsor must be a county in conjunction with a PHA or developer to acquire existing housing
Sponsors must have an ownership interest in the project's ownership entity, as demonstrated by an organizational chart and/or partnership agreement
Projects must provide mixed-income, cross-subsidized housing
At least 20% of units must be set aside for households earning 50% or less of area median income, OR at least 40% of units must be set aside for households earning 60% or less of area median income
Projects must be ready for occupancy within two years of the award selection date
Proposed projects must be in Maryland
Project types eligible include: new construction, acquisition and substantial renovation of multifamily properties, or acquisition of multifamily properties without major renovation
Eligible activities include new construction, acquisition, and rehabilitation of rental housing
Project must comply with DHCD Multifamily Policies regarding construction standards and individual unit health and safety requirements
Project must agree to ongoing compliance, asset management, and inspections
Applicants must comply with fair housing and equal opportunity laws
Applications must be complete with all required exhibits and certifications
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must submit a complete electronic application via Procorem WorkCenter. The process includes: (1) Request an electronic application folder using the Electronic Submission Package Request Form in the Multifamily Library; (2) Complete the Application Submission Kit including CDA Form 202 Worksheet, Certifications, Threshold Checklist, Applicant Self-Scoring, and Organizational Chart; (3) Submit all required attachments and exhibits clearly tabbed; (4) Pay application fee of $2,500 payable to Community Development Administration, submitted separately to Post Office Box 2524, Landover Hills, MD 20784, with a copy included in the application; (5) Submit complete electronic application by the deadline with electronic signatures accepted. Applicants should submit a pre-application meeting request form. Waiver requests for Project Threshold Criteria or Competitive Criteria must be submitted at least 15 days prior to the application deadline using the Waiver Request Form on the DHCD website (by May 4, 2026). A virtual information session is available on March 11, 2026 at 12:00 p.m. DHCD will review complete proposals for compliance, convene a scoring committee to score all complete proposals, rank proposals by score, and recommend the highest-scored proposal to the CDA Director for approval, then to the Secretary for final approval and allocation. If multiple applications are submitted from the same jurisdiction, DHCD will rank them by number of elements and total points achieved, with number of units as the tiebreaker.

structured_extraction.program_description: A Maryland state income tax credit program that provides financial assistance to eligible residents who are renovating or modifying their homes to improve accessibility and support independent living. DHCD reviews applications and issues tax credit certificates to approved recipients.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Applicants receive a Maryland state income tax credit certificate if approved. DHCD reviews applications and issues the certificate to approved recipients by August 31st.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 1st of the current calendar year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents and individuals seeking independent living modifications and home accessibility improvements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Home modifications and renovations to improve accessibility and support independent living.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed application and supporting documents online or on paper by the June 1st deadline. DHCD reviews applications by August 31st and notifies approved applicants of their tax credit certificate. DHCD may contact applicants if additional information is needed.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides loans to help homeowners install or repair indoor plumbing systems in single-family homes. Eligible improvements include wells, septic systems, public water and sewer connections, plumbing fixtures, and alternative water and septic systems.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans with interest rates ranging from 0% to 6% based on ability to pay and household income. Interest rates are 0%-4.5% for households at 60% of median income, and 4.5%-6.0% for households at 80% of median income. Maximum loan amount is $50,000. Maximum loan term is 30 years. Deferred loans with deferred principal and interest payments are available for borrowers with incomes at or below 50% of median income with no repayment capability. For borrowers with income below 30% of statewide median income, deferred loan amounts may be forgiven on an annual basis.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owner-occupants of single-family homes with income at or below 80 percent of statewide or Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income. Owners of rental properties with income-eligible tenants.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Wells, septic tanks and drain fields, piping from septic systems, public water or sewer connection expenses, plumbing fixtures and equipment including handicapped fixtures, additions and modifications for toilet and bath facilities, sand mound systems, purification systems, percolation testing, and alternative or innovative septic and water systems.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Loans are processed by local governments for properties within their jurisdiction. Income limits vary by household size and geography (Washington D.C. PMSA includes Calvert, Charles, Frederick, Montgomery, and Prince George's counties).
requirements_list: Single-family, owner-occupied house or primary residence
Inoperative, unsafe, or inadequate plumbing
Property must be structurally sound
Owner-occupant or rental property owner with income-eligible tenants
Household income at or below 80 percent of statewide or Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income
Homeowner's insurance required
Valid photo ID (driver's license, passport, military ID, etc.)
Proof of home ownership (deed and current mortgage statement)
Current property tax bill
Declaration page of homeowner's insurance policy
Contractor bid not more than 60 days old
Licensed and insured Maryland contractor with current MHIC or trade license, Certificate of Liability Insurance (COI) with $1M per occurrence limits, Letter of Good Standing, and completed W-9
Property photos documenting plumbing issues
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local housing office by county or call Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development Special Loan Programs at 301-429-7409 (Baltimore area), 877-218-8101, or 1-844-369-4150. Obtain bids from licensed Maryland contractors detailing the plumbing work needed, including photographs documenting the issues. Submit completed application with supporting documentation including income verification (paystubs, tax returns, bank statements), proof of home ownership, contractor bid with license and insurance documentation, and photos to DHCD.SLP_documentation@maryland.gov or mail to Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, CDA, Special Loan Programs, 7800 Harkins Road, 3rd Floor, Lanham, MD 20706. Loan requests are processed directly by local governments or their network of local administering agencies including county housing offices, nonprofit organizations, and local banks.

structured_extraction.program_name: Lead Hazard Reduction Grant and Loan Program
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant and loan program administered by DHCD, using funds from the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development, to assist homeowners and landlords lessen the risk of lead poisoning and preserve housing.

The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development issues tax-exempt bonds on behalf of counties, municipalities, and their agencies to finance infrastructure projects that serve the community. The program helps local governments access long-term capital financing for essential public infrastructure without having to issue bonds individually.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Community Development Administration issues tax-exempt bonds and loans the bond proceeds to local governments at interest rates determined by market conditions at the time of sale. Loan terms are set by the local government but cannot exceed the useful life of the project or 30 years, whichever is less. Local governments repay the debt and pay their share of the costs of issuance. The program reduces issuance costs through economies of scale and pooling of demand from multiple local governments.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland counties, municipalities, and their agencies that need long-term capital financing for infrastructure projects and do not routinely issue bonds or have limited resources to finance projects independently.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Street lighting, landscaping, sidewalks and public space improvements; public safety vehicles and equipment; water production, treatment, storage and distribution systems; storm water control and sewer collection and treatment facilities; government office and meeting facilities; police, fire, transportation, education, health, recreation, maintenance and other service-related facilities; and refinancing of existing debt for eligible projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland counties and municipalities are eligible.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland county, municipality, or their agency
Must have legal authority to construct, operate and maintain the proposed project
Must have legal authority to pledge security for and repay the proposed loan
Must have legal authority to pledge income tax payments and various other shared revenue from the State
Project must support an essential physical element of a municipality's public service system
Project must meet federal tax law requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The local government completes an application that elicits information similar to what a bond rating agency would require to evaluate credit worthiness. Applicants requesting technical assistance may submit an Expression of Interest form outlining the proposed project or specific questions. Timing of bond issuance depends on the volume and frequency of participation by local governments.

structured_extraction.program_name: Low Income Housing Tax Credit (LIHTC) Program
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal tax credit program that encourages private sector investment in the construction and rehabilitation of rental housing for low- and moderate-income families. States receive an annual tax credit allocation to award to qualifying projects.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a federal tax credit to encourage private sector investment in the construction and rehabilitation of rental housing for low- and moderate-income families.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible applicants include county governments, for-profit businesses, municipalities, and non-profit organizations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The tax credit supports the construction and rehabilitation of rental housing for low- and moderate-income families.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the program for additional information on how to apply.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program to further the state's digital inclusion efforts by enabling access to high-speed internet and expanding digital literacy. The program provides funding to local jurisdictions, nonprofit organizations (501(c) entities), and community-based anchor institutions for digital inclusion planning and program implementation activities that serve covered populations including low-income individuals, aging individuals, individuals with disabilities, individuals with language barriers, racial or ethnic minorities, and rural residents. Funded through American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) Coronavirus State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two funding tracks: (1) Digital Inclusion Planning provides financial assistance for up to 50% of the cost of developing a digital inclusion plan, with a maximum grant of $30,000 and minimum of $5,000. (2) Digital Inclusion Program Implementation provides up to 100% funding for implementing, expanding, or continuing digital inclusion programs, with a maximum grant of $75,000 and minimum of $10,000. Total program funding: $2 million (FY2022). Applicants are encouraged to identify other funding sources to leverage available grant funding. Individual grant amounts may be reduced based on the impact of the applicant's intended population and ability to deploy funds responsibly. All funded projects must comply with ARPA requirements and federal rules governing this funding. Projects must be completed by December 31, 2023.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments (counties and municipalities), nonprofits, foundations, corporations, institutions, associations, and coalitions with 501(c) nonprofit status, and community-based anchor institutions serving populations in Maryland. Priority given to individuals with income at or below 150 percent of federal poverty level, aging individuals, individuals with disabilities, individuals with language barriers, members of racial or ethnic minority groups, and individuals in rural areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Develop or implement digital inclusion plans and activities; enhance understanding of internet service; assist households with applications for internet service; provide training to residents in use of digital tools; enhance capacity of communities to access jurisdiction services and participate in civic matters; pursue educational opportunities; facilitate broadband adoption by covered populations for educational and employment opportunities; implement training programs covering basic, advanced, and applied skills or other workforce development programs; construct, upgrade, expand, or operate public access computing centers for covered populations through community anchor institutions; research and identify populations with low adoption rates for home internet and computers; further other qualifying digital inclusion or equity goals. Grant funds may not be used for construction of broadband infrastructure.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All communities in Maryland are eligible to be served, with priority given to covered populations (individuals with household income at or below 150% of federal poverty level, aging individuals, individuals with disabilities, individuals with language barriers including English learners and those with low literacy levels, members of racial or ethnic minority groups, and individuals primarily residing in rural areas).
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local government (county or municipality), nonprofit 501(c) entity, or community-based anchor institution
Applications must be fully complete at submission; any missing information may result in application being deemed ineligible

Executive summary required including project overview, population needs, funding contribution, potential barriers, partners and local engagement, intended outcomes and metrics, and statement of experience and past accomplishments
Scope of work and budget required with categories for operations, contracted services, travel, and other funding sources
Completed and signed application form with applicant legal name matching W-9
IRS Determination Letter of nonprofit status if applicable
Online verification of Certificate of Good Standing from Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation
IRS W-9 Request for Taxpayer Identification Number and Certification
Dun & Bradstreet DUNS Number for organization
Federal EIN Number
For digital inclusion planning applications: describe goals for plan, where applicant is in process, desired outcome, and how grant funds will be utilized
For digital inclusion program implementation applications: indicate how project fits into plan's goals or enhances digital inclusion, who will be served, desired outcome, and how it meets unmet needs
Statement of Experience must describe demonstrated capability and experience related to proposed project and include principal employees' relevant work experience

Partners and Local Engagement list including community partners and description of their involvement; applicants not from local jurisdictional agencies must indicate whom they are working with from local jurisdiction
Intended Outcomes and Metrics describing project outcomes and metrics and how success will be defined
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: NOFA released February 9, 2022. Application submission opens February 15, 2022 and closes March 31, 2022. Applications and all supporting documents must be submitted via email to OSB.MD@Maryland.gov with subject line 'MD-DIG: Name of Applying Organization'. Submit completed application form, executive summary, project budget, and IRS W-9 form. All awardees will be required to execute a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) outlining obligations of awardee and State to the project. The OSB reserves the right to conduct discussions, negotiations, and interviews as deemed necessary for evaluation. Funding announcements to be made on or before April 15, 2022, with intent to award funds beginning in May 2022.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program designed to help local jurisdictions, community-based organizations, non-profits, and anchor institutions build and deploy broadband networks that provide low-cost or free internet access to low and moderate income households and other underserved populations, addressing affordability challenges for households seeking to subscribe to internet service. Funded through American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) Coronavirus State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants between $25,000 and $250,000 covering up to 100% of project costs for construction, deployment, expansion, or continuation of community-based gap networks and community networks. Total program funding: $5 million. Funds support equipment, hardware, software, and digital network technology including optical line terminals, optical network terminals, routers, switches, firewalls, wireless equipment, antennas, access points, modems, and network shelters. Funding categories include: Operations (equipment, payroll, supplies, materials); Contracted services (payments to independent contractors, external organizations); and Travel (must be related to program deployment). Applicants are highly encouraged to identify other funding sources to leverage the available grant funding.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments (counties and municipalities), non-profit 501(c) entities, community-based anchor institutions, and other community-based organizations seeking to provide broadband access to covered populations including individuals living in households with income at or below 150% of federal poverty level, aging individuals, individuals with disabilities, individuals with language barriers (including English learners and those with low literacy levels), and individuals who are members of racial or ethnic minority groups.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Equipment, hardware, software, and digital network technology to build, upgrade, expand, or maintain broadband networks delivering service at low or no cost. Eligible items include optical line terminals (OLTs), optical network terminals (ONTs), routers, switches, firewalls, wireless radio equipment, antennas, access points, modems, and necessary equipment shelters. Funding can support building and deployment of new gap networks/community networks, upgrading or expanding existing gap networks/community networks, and operating and maintaining new or existing gap networks/community networks.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Must provide services within the State of Maryland (statewide eligibility). Project areas must be identified as having a need for additional broadband investment, including lack of access to a connection that reliably meets or exceeds symmetrical 100 Mbps download and upload speeds, lack of affordable access to broadband service, or lack of reliable broadband.
requirements_list: Be a local government (county or municipality), OR a non-profit 501(c) entity registered in Maryland, OR a community-based anchor institution, OR other community-based organization
Must be registered and in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation

Project must reliably provide minimum internet connectivity of 100 Mbps down and 100 Mbps up with a maximum latency of 50 milliseconds measured at the served subscribers' location (with limited exceptions for scalable networks achieving these speeds through future technology advances, related to geography, topography, or excessive cost)
Application must be fully complete at submission

Applicants must submit all required attachments including completed application form, project summary, IRS determination letter (if applicable), Certificate of Good Standing, W-9 form, and Dun & Bradstreet DUNS Number
Projects must be completed by December 31, 2023
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a complete application package via email to OSB.MD@Maryland.gov by March 31, 2022 with subject line 'MD-GAPS: Name of Applying Organization.' Package must include: (1) Completed application form with applicant information, federal EIN number, DUNS number, address, and contact information; (2) Project Summary addressing executive summary, statement of experience, network design, community profile, subscriber cost (if applicable), potential barriers, partners and local engagement, intended outcomes and sustainability, schedule, and funding scope/budget; (3) Project budget in categories of Operations, Contracted Services, Travel, and other funding sources; (4) IRS determination letter if nonprofit; (5) Certificate of Good Standing verification from Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation; (6) W-9 form; and (7) DUNS number. Only fully complete applications will be considered. The OSB intends to award funds beginning in May 2022. Successful applicants will be chosen based on qualifications and evaluation of responses, with possible interviews. All awardees will be required to execute a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) outlining obligations of the awardee and State to the project.

structured_extraction.program_name: MEER: Maryland Emergency Education Relief Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants to schools, libraries, and anchor institutions to close the digital divide by funding internet access and devices for K-12 students and school staff who lack necessary connectivity and technology to access classrooms.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants between $50,000 and $350,000 covering up to 100% of eligible program costs. Funding covers qualifying expenses and projects completed between September 1, 2021 and September 15, 2022. Total MEER program funding: $4,999,251.80 distributed across multiple Maryland jurisdictions to schools, libraries, and anchor institutions for broadband access and devices.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Program period ended; funding for projects completed between September 1, 2021 and September 15, 2022
structured_extraction.program_audience: Schools, libraries, anchor institutions, government agencies, and non-profit organizations serving K-12 students and school staff
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Internet access and devices for K-12 students and school staff to connect to classrooms, broadband infrastructure and digital connectivity in underserved communities
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide across all Maryland counties
requirements_list: Applicant must be a school, library, anchor institution, or eligible non-profit organization
Project must be completed between September 1, 2021 and September 15, 2022
Grant awards range from $50,000 to $350,000
Must address digital divide and provide broadband access or devices to K-12 students and school staff
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications were submitted to the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development Office of Statewide Broadband. Awards were made to eligible organizations demonstrating need and capacity to close the digital divide for K-12 students and school staff.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that provides operating assistance funding to designated and aspiring Main Street Maryland communities and Baltimore City's designated Main Street neighborhoods to help them build capacity and achieve community revitalization and economic development goals in Sustainable Community areas.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Designated Main Street Maryland Communities with full accreditation receive equal allocated amounts. Designated Main Street Maryland Communities with affiliate accreditation receive equal allocated amounts. Main Street Maryland Aspiring Communities receive equal allocated amounts. Funds support operating expenses only, including staff and consultant services, general operating expenses, market and business recruitment strategies, marketing and advertising, placemaking initiatives, and other projects identified in the applicant's work plan as key to Main Street efforts. All projects and activities must be completed within one year. No funding match is required. Awardees should draw down at least 50% of awarded funds within six months of award execution and must draw down all funds by the award agreement expiration date.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Designated and aspiring Main Street Maryland communities and Baltimore City's designated Main Street neighborhoods
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating expenses only, including staff and consultant services, general operating expenses, market and business recruitment strategies, marketing and advertising, placemaking initiatives, and other costs related to administering the Main Street program. Projects and activities must be completed within one year, align with the applicant's annual work plan, and contribute to the community's transformation strategy. Funds must be used for activities specifically detailed in the award agreement and are restricted to operating expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Designated and aspiring Main Street Maryland communities and Baltimore City's designated Main Street neighborhoods in Sustainable Community areas throughout the state. Additional consideration given to projects in ENOUGH areas and Just Communities.
requirements_list: Only designated and aspiring Main Street Maryland communities are eligible
All projects and activities must be completed within one year
Requested funds must support projects and activities that align with the applicant's annual work plan
Projects must contribute to the transformation strategy of the community
Organization profile must include all required documents before submitting application
No funding match required
Nonprofit applicants must submit evidence of nonprofit status (Bylaws, Articles of Incorporation, IRS Determination Letter)
Nonprofit applicants must submit evidence of good standing from Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation
Nonprofit applicants must submit evidence of charitable registration from Maryland Secretary of State
Current awardees must be in full compliance with all existing award agreements and reporting deadlines
Application must align with Main Street annual work plan
Site control documentation required at time of award agreement execution for projects involving acquisition, demolition, construction, or rehabilitation
Awardees must maintain all project-related records for minimum of three years after award close-out
Awardees must disclose any actual or potential conflicts of interest
Awardees must complete HB 1210 Corporate Diversity affidavit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application through the DHCD Project Portal at https://projectportal.dhcd.state.md.us/. Register as a new user and complete the registration request form (approval may take up to 72 hours). First-time applicants must contact the project manager for eligibility verification and system access. New organizations should request access and submit organizational documents at least two weeks before the application deadline to expedite processing. Ensure your organization profile includes all required nonprofit documentation (IRS Determination Letter, Articles of Incorporation, Bylaws, SDAT evidence of good standing, Secretary of State charitable registration) before submitting the application. Applications missing required documents may be disqualified. The application must align with your Main Street annual work plan. Virtual application training and individual technical assistance sessions are available through the Project Portal. For system access support, contact the project manager. Applications must be submitted by the stated deadline; late applications will not be accepted.

structured_extraction.program_description: An emergency loan program that provides financial assistance to small businesses affected by disasters. The program is activated by the Secretary of the Department of Housing and Community Development for specific disaster events.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Emergency loans to help small businesses recover from disasters. Funds can be used for renovations, repairs and replacement of furniture and equipment, inventory replacement, loss of revenues, operating and leasing expense assistance, and other recovery-related working capital needs.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Colleen Cord-Malone, Business Lending Programs, Manager II; Aisha K. Taylor, Business Lending Programs, Loan Underwriter
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland-based small businesses and nonprofit organizations located in commercial spaces that have been affected by qualifying disasters.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Renovations, repairs and replacement of furniture, fixtures and equipment, inventory replacement, loss of revenues, operating and leasing expense assistance, and other costs associated with recovery of a small business including working capital.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Business must be located in Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Howard County, Frederick County, or Washington County and show evidence of damage or loss associated with the May 2018 flooding events.
requirements_list: Business must be Maryland-based
Business must be located in a commercial space
Applicant must show proof of insurance status
Business must be located in Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Howard County, Frederick County, or Washington County
Business must show evidence of damage or loss associated with May 2018 flooding events

Ineligible business types include residential or transient living businesses, public facilities, adult bookstores, adult video shops, adult entertainment facilities, gambling facilities, gun shops, massage parlors, pawn shops, tanning salons, and tattoo parlors
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development for application procedures. The program is only available when activated by the Secretary for specific disasters.

structured_extraction.program_description: A credit enhancement program that helps small businesses access loans by establishing a loan loss reserve fund. Private lenders, borrowers, and the State of Maryland each contribute to the reserve, which protects lenders against loan defaults and enables them to make loans that might otherwise fall outside their normal credit guidelines.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program works through a reserve account funded by contributions from the lender, borrower, and the Maryland Capital Access Program. Typically, the borrower and lender each contribute 1.5 percent of the loan amount, and the state matches that contribution at 3 percent, for a total reserve of 6 percent of the original loan amount. Enrolled loan amounts range from $10,000 to $1,000,000. If a loan defaults, the lender can file a claim to draw from the reserve account to cover losses.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses located in Maryland's Priority Funding Areas, including nonprofit organizations
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Working capital, lines of credit, term loans, and business expansion projects. Proceeds cannot be used for passive real estate ownership, residential or transient living facilities, public facilities, adult entertainment, check cashing, gambling, liquor stores, massage parlors, pawn shops, gun shops, tanning salons, tattoo parlors, or sectarian religious instruction.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects financed by enrolled loans must be located in Priority Funding Areas as approved by the Maryland Department of Planning under the Smart Growth Act of 1997.
requirements_list: Business must be a small business located in Maryland
Business must be located in a Priority Funding Area
Nonprofit organizations are eligible
Loan amount must be between $10,000 and $1,000,000
Project cannot involve passive real estate ownership
Project cannot be residential or transient living facilities
Project cannot be public facilities like community halls, fire stations, hospitals, colleges, or universities
Project cannot be adult entertainment establishments, check cashing facilities, gambling facilities, liquor stores, massage parlors, pawn shops, gun shops, tanning salons, or tattoo parlors
Proceeds cannot be used for sectarian religious instruction
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: A small business applies to a participating lender. The lender reviews and enrolls the loan. The lender, borrower, and the Maryland Capital Access Program each deposit contributions into a reserve account based on a formula established by the program. The lender submits a one-page enrollment form with summary information to the Maryland Capital Access Program. If the loan defaults, the lender files a one-page claim form to draw from the reserve account.

structured_extraction.program_description: MEAP helps eligible Maryland households repair or replace heating, cooling, and water heating systems at no cost. The program operates year-round and is federally funded to make homes more comfortable. It also provides supplemental funding for critical repairs such as structural, electrical, water leaks, lead, and asbestos issues for homeowners.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides free repair or replacement of heating, cooling, and water heating systems for eligible households. For supplemental funding addressing critical repairs (structural, electrical, water leaks, lead, asbestos, etc.), homeowners can request up to $50,000, with a maximum initial deposit of 33% of the total project cost. Work eligibility is determined based on a home assessment and funding availability. Applicants are currently placed on a waitlist due to limited program funding and high demand.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible Maryland households with household income at or below 200% of the federal poverty level and a non-functioning heating, cooling, or water heating system. Homeowners may also apply for supplemental critical repair funding.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Repair or replacement of heating, cooling, and water heating systems. Supplemental funding for homeowners can address critical repairs including structural issues, electrical problems, water leaks, lead hazards, and asbestos.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland. Special flood assistance available for homes in Allegany or Garrett County affected by flooding. Applications should be mailed to: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, Attn: Weatherization, 7800 Harkins Road, Lanham, MD 20706.
requirements_list: Household income must be at or below 200% of the federal poverty level based on household size
Have a non-functioning heating, cooling, and/or water heating system

Automatically income-eligible if currently participating in: Utility Bill Pay Assistance through OHEP, Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF), Supplemental Security Income (SSI), or HUD housing assistance programs
Home must have power to the home

For homeowners applying for supplemental critical repairs funding: must provide lowest qualifying bid from licensed Maryland tradesperson/company with bid not more than 60 days old; grand total of bids should not exceed $50,000; bid must include photographs documenting critical repairs; contractor must provide current MHIC License or applicable trade license, Certificate of Liability Insurance with per occurrence limits of $1 million or greater, Letter of Good Standing, and completed W-9 form

For supplemental repair funding: applicants must provide proof of home ownership (deed and current mortgage statement or homeowners insurance declaration page), property tax bill, proof of flood insurance if applicable, and complete financial information for underwriting
If applicant has outstanding judgments, bankruptcy history, or foreclosure efforts within past 7 years, written explanation required for supplemental repair funding
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Complete the DHCD Energy & Repair Programs Application form with all required information (Client Information, Household Information, Energy Consent Form). 2. Submit complete application with all required documentation to: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, Attn: Weatherization, 7800 Harkins Road, Lanham, MD 20706. 3. Call intake line at 1-855-583-8976 to submit or for assistance. 4. For standard energy program applications, submit: copy of most recent electric utility bill, copy of benefit approval notice from programs checked if applicable, and proof of home ownership if mobile home. 5. For supplemental repair applications, provide additional documentation including: proof of last 30 days GROSS household income (bank statements not valid), copy of Social Security cards for all household members, photo ID for applicant, Zero Income Form for any household member 18+ claiming zero income, supplemental financial information, tax affidavit, credit pull consent, and repair contractor bid documentation. 6. Once eligibility is determined, a local agency will contact the household to schedule a home assessment. 7. Local agency evaluates service needs, discusses results with applicant, and schedules contractor to complete recommended work. 8. Incomplete applications and those missing documentation cannot be processed until complete.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides funding to local governments and community development organizations for programs to improve the exteriors of commercial properties located within Maryland's Sustainable Communities. The program supports communities seeking to create consistent, attractive designs for their commercial corridors in order to bolster economic vitality and stimulate new private investments.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MFIP awards funds to capitalize a local facade improvement program. Funds must be used for capital improvements to properties occupied by businesses. Eligible uses include: signage, exterior painting, storefront reconstruction, siding, exterior lighting, window and door upgrades, public-facing masonry or cornices, murals, removal of unattractive exterior finishes, and roofs. Individual business improvements must be between $1,000 and $50,000 of MFIP funding per award cycle. Ineligible uses include interior work, electric charging stations, solar panels, improvements outside Sustainable Communities, and predevelopment/operating expenses. Projects should prioritize aesthetic improvements over routine maintenance and focus on primary elevations of commercial properties.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Counties, municipalities, community development organizations, community development corporations, main street organizations, and downtown partnerships. Final recipients must be businesses located within Maryland's designated Sustainable Communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital improvements to exterior facades of commercial properties including signage, exterior painting, storefront reconstruction, siding, exterior lighting, window and door upgrades, public-facing masonry or cornices, murals, removal of unattractive exterior finishes, and roofs. Individual business improvements must range from $1,000 to $50,000 per award cycle.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Funding can only be used in areas designated as Maryland Sustainable Communities, which are geographic areas targeted for revitalization by local governments. Use the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper to determine geographic eligibility.
requirements_list: Project must capitalize on the strengths of a community while addressing its challenges to revitalization
Project should help achieve a local government's Sustainable Communities Action Plan
Projects must be located in designated Sustainable Communities
Applicant must submit evidence of site control (deed, purchase contract, or lease agreement)
Applicant must submit photographs showing existing conditions of the building
Applicant must obtain written consent from landlord and lessee as applicable
Applicant must submit project description with two cost estimates and detailed sketches
Applicant must provide screenshot from Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation showing business is in good standing
Individual business improvements must be between $1,000 and $50,000 of MFIP funding during a single award cycle
Work completed prior to receipt of letter of commitment is ineligible
Improvements must comply with all building codes, zoning ordinances, and Historic Preservation Commission requirements
All projects are subject to Federal Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation for properties over 50 years old
Applicant must maintain valid insurance coverage for property damage and personal injury
Applicant agrees to maintain property and improvements including removal of graffiti and regular sweeping
Applicant agrees to return pro-rated grant money if improvement is removed within two years
Changes to completed improvements that received MFIP funding within the last 12 months are ineligible
Improvements for businesses prohibited from receiving State Revitalization Programs funding are ineligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants complete the MFIP application form and attach all required documents including evidence of site control, photographs of existing conditions, written consent from landlord/lessee, project description with two cost estimates and detailed sketches, and proof of business good standing. Applications are subject to competitive review. Awardees will develop and enforce their own local program guidelines that comply with MFIP requirements and include criteria for rating and awarding grants to qualified businesses. DHCD provides model program documents following best practices. All proposed improvements must undergo historic preservation review by DHCD's Preservation Officer and potentially the Maryland Historical Trust before work begins. Work completed prior to historic preservation review will not be reimbursed.

structured_extraction.program_description: The program supports non-profit and local government organizations that provide housing counseling services and free or low-cost legal assistance. Awards are made annually on a competitive basis.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program awards grants annually on a competitive basis to provide operating support for housing counseling programs. Grantees are required to submit quarterly progress reports by the fifteenth of the month following the end of each quarter of the grant term.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Poverty Solutions Team, Division of Homeless Solutions
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations and local government agencies that provide housing counseling services and legal assistance.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating support for housing counseling programs including homebuyer education, pre-purchase counseling, foreclosure counseling, rental counseling, financial capability coaching, and legal services for homeowners concerned about foreclosure and renters concerned about eviction.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide
requirements_list: Applicant must be a non-profit organization or local government agency
Program must provide housing counseling services or free or low-cost legal assistance

Eligible activities include homebuyer education, pre-purchase counseling, foreclosure counseling, rental counseling, financial capability coaching, and legal services for foreclosure and eviction concerns
Grantees must submit quarterly progress reports by the fifteenth of the month following the end of each quarter
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted on a competitive basis annually. Specific application procedures and requirements are not detailed on this page.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Housing Rehabilitation Program (Homeowner Repair Loans)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Housing Rehabilitation Program provides affordable loan funding to help homeowners address critical health and safety issues in their homes and bring properties into compliance with applicable building codes and standards. It is part of a suite of special loan programs administered through DHCD's WholeHome initiative.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans with interest rates ranging from 0% to 6% based on household income and ability to repay. Generally, the maximum loan is $50,000, or up to 110% of the equity of the home, whichever is less. There is a minimum loan amount of $5,000. Loans in excess of $5,000 or with deferred payments are secured by a mortgage (deed of trust). Maximum loan term is 30 years. Loans serving families with incomes at or below 50 percent of the statewide or Washington, D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income may have deferred payments if necessary for project feasibility. Interest rates are tiered based on income: 4.5%-6.0% for households at 80% of median income; 0%-4.5% for households at 60% of median income. The maximum initial deposit is 33% of the total project cost.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owner-occupants of owner-occupied single-family homes with household income not exceeding 80 percent of the statewide or Washington, D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Critical health and safety repairs including mold remediation, gas leaks, roof repair, asbestos abatement, lead abatement, vermiculite removal, combustion appliance repair, chimney repair, water-proofing, radon mitigation, electrical hazards, knob and tube removal, electrical service upgrades, plumbing issues, water and well repairs, septic and sewer repairs, windows and doors for health and safety concerns, structural repair, accessibility improvements for disabled and seniors, fall prevention, ductwork upgrades, building shell stabilization, and pest treatments. Electrical upgrades for future home electrification (less than 100A to 200A upgrades). HVAC replacement for end of service life.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide (Maryland). Generally, all loan requests are processed directly by local governments for properties within their jurisdiction. Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area includes Calvert, Charles, Frederick, Montgomery, and Prince George's counties for income limit purposes.
requirements_list: Household income cannot exceed 80 percent of the statewide or Washington, D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income
Property must be an owner-occupied single-family home (duplexes, townhomes, condos, and manufactured homes excluded)
Work must address critical health and safety issues or building code violations
Contractor must be licensed and insured with current MHIC License or trade-specific license (Electrical, Plumbing, HVAC, etc.)
Applicant must provide at least one detailed work proposal from a licensed Maryland Home Improvement contractor or trade professional with photos documenting issues, dated within the past 60 days
Minimum loan amount of $5,000; maximum of $50,000 or 110% of home equity, whichever is less
Bid must not include remodeling or non-essential repairs
No active bankruptcy or foreclosure; both must be dismissed for minimum 2 years before eligibility
No minimum credit score required
If property built before 1978, applicant must acknowledge lead-based paint notification
Anyone on the deed but not occupying the property must provide proof of alternate residence
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Contact your local housing office or Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's Special Loan Programs at (301) 429-7409, (301) 429-7564, or 1-877-218-8101. 2. Obtain at least one detailed estimate (within past 60 days) from a licensed Maryland Home Improvement Contractor or trade professional for critical repairs with photos documenting the issues. 3. Complete the Maryland Housing Rehabilitation Program application with income documentation. 4. Provide contractor documentation including current license, certificate of liability insurance (minimum $1 million per occurrence), letter of good standing, and completed W-9 form. 5. Submit completed application and all supporting documentation to DHCD.SLP_documentation@maryland.gov or mail to Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, CDA, Special Loan Programs, 7800 Harkins Road, 3rd Floor, Lanham, MD 20706. 6. Staff will review the estimate to verify work meets health and safety requirements and contractor meets Maryland business requirements. 7. Upon approval, sign commitment letter, rehabilitation contract, construction agreement, and W-9 form. 8. Funds are disbursed by local administering agencies and participating mortgage lenders.

Investment size between $25,000 to $1,000,000

Lender must have 20% at risk

The program targets communities and areas with high need for economic development and small business support.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Town Manager Circuit Rider Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that helps small town and city governments build their administrative capacity by funding professional staff (called circuit riders) who work across multiple municipalities to assist with specific municipal functions and activities.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual competitive grant funding determined by General Assembly appropriation. Funds can only be used to pay salary and fringe benefits for circuit rider professional staff over a two-year period.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small municipalities with populations of 5,000 or less, as well as municipal governments, county governments, regional governmental organizations, or private organizations that want to sponsor a circuit consisting of two or more municipalities in reasonable proximity to each other.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Salary and fringe benefits for circuit rider professional staff who assist with specific municipal functions and activities over a two-year period.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Small municipalities with populations of 5,000 or less are eligible to participate. Circuit sponsors (municipal governments, county governments, regional governmental organizations, or private organizations) must assemble two or more municipalities that are in reasonable proximity to each other.
requirements_list: Municipality must have a population of 5,000 or less
Circuit sponsors must organize at least two municipalities in reasonable proximity to each other
Funds must be used only for salary and fringe benefits for circuit rider staff
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Funding is provided through a competitive process each year. Eligible governments are notified when the competition opens and when applications are due. Applications are evaluated based on need, proposed accomplishments, and financial commitment and support. Existing circuits are also evaluated on past performance. Technical assistance is available for interested governments and sponsors.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides flexible financing for starting up, rehabilitating, or expanding businesses and nonprofits that offer healthy food options, particularly those sourcing fresh food from Maryland farmers, in designated Food Desert Areas and Sustainable Communities.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
list_of_prioritized_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
list_of_relevant_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Flexible financing through the Neighborhood BusinessWorks program for start-up, rehabilitation, or expansion of eligible businesses and nonprofits offering healthy food options in food deserts and Sustainable Communities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses and nonprofits offering healthy food options, particularly those sourcing fresh food from Maryland farmers, located in designated Food Desert Areas or Sustainable Communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Start-up, rehabilitation, or expansion of businesses and nonprofits that provide fresh fruits, vegetables, and other healthy food options.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be located in a designated Food Desert Area or Sustainable Community. Food deserts are communities that lack easy access to healthy foods like fresh fruits and vegetables, typically lacking a supermarket or grocery store.
requirements_list: Located in a designated Food Desert Area or Sustainable Community
Offer healthy food options to residents
Preference for businesses sourcing fresh food from Maryland farmers
