structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants apply through intermediary lenders and partners selected by the department. Community-based lending intermediaries, including Community Development Financial Institutions, local governments, or quasi-public agencies, originate and administer loans and provide technical assistance to applicants.

structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program that expands opportunities for microenterprise development and creates new opportunities for small business development. It provides entrepreneurs with flexible financing for microenterprise start-ups and expansions within designated Sustainable Communities and Priority Funding Areas throughout Maryland. The program is administered through partnerships with community-based microlenders.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans up to $50,000 with interest rates up to 12% and loan terms not exceeding 5 years. Additional funds may be added to the project by the Intermediary. Collateral is required, which may include personal guarantees, liens on business assets, and pledges of accounts. No prepayment penalties.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Microentrepreneurs and small business owners seeking to start or expand their businesses in designated Sustainable Communities and Priority Funding Areas
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Working capital, marketing, planning and feasibility studies, real estate acquisition down payments, minor renovations, minor leasehold improvements, machinery and equipment, and other costs associated with opening or expanding a small business
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must be located in designated Sustainable Community areas or Priority Funding Areas throughout Maryland
requirements_list: Business must be a retail, manufacturing, goods and services related business
Business cannot exceed $500,000 in annual revenue
Business cannot have more than 5 employees at time of application
Business cannot be home-based

Business cannot be involved in residential or transient living, multifamily or single-family housing, nursing homes, assisted living facilities, crisis care centers, group homes, transitional housing, homeless shelters, community halls, fire stations, hospitals, colleges, universities, adult entertainment, gambling, gun shops, liquor stores, massage parlors, pawn shops, tanning salons, or tattoo parlors
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the intermediary microlender directly to receive an application. Five intermediary partners serve different regions of Maryland: Baltimore Community Lending (Baltimore City), Enterprise Development Group (Anne Arundel, Baltimore, Charles, Frederick, Howard, Montgomery, Prince George's, St. Mary's, and Baltimore City), Latino Economic Development Center (Anne Arundel, Baltimore, Charles, Frederick, Harford, Howard, Montgomery, Prince George's, and Baltimore City), Maryland Capital Enterprises, Inc. (Anne Arundel, Baltimore, Caroline, Dorchester, Kent, Queen Anne, Somerset, Talbot, Wicomico, Worcester, and Baltimore City), and Prince George's Financial Service Corporation (Prince George's County).

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides tax-exempt bonds and notes for construction and permanent financing of multifamily rental housing for families with limited incomes, supporting the development and preservation of affordable rental housing in priority funding areas. The program leverages federal Low-Income Housing Tax Credits to support new construction, acquisition, and rehabilitation of rental properties.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax-exempt bonds and notes provide construction and permanent financing for multifamily rental housing projects. Multiple financing options are available including: FHA-CDA Risk Sharing (40-year term), GNMA MBS (40-year term with 17-year balloon), Freddie Mac Tax Exempt Loans (17-year term), Cash Collateral/GNMA MBS (2-year short-term notes), and FNMA MBS Collateral (17-year term with immediate or forward start options). Interest rates vary by financing structure and credit enhancement method, ranging from approximately 4.3% to 6.7% estimated all-in rates based on current market conditions. Loan terms are generally 30 to 40 years for permanent financing, with construction periods of 20-24 months. A first lien position is generally required. All loans must be insured or have other forms of credit enhancement acceptable to the program. The Community Development Administration participates in the Federal Housing Administration/Housing Finance Agency Risk Sharing Program. Upfront costs and fees vary by financing option and loan amount. Applicants should consult with CDA loan underwriters for current rates, fees, and available financing structures.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit and nonprofit developers, and sponsors of affordable rental housing developments seeking to build or rehabilitate multifamily rental housing for low-income families.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction and permanent financing for new construction, acquisition, and rehabilitation of multifamily rental housing projects with a minimum of five units. Loans may also be provided to refinance existing high interest rate private loans if the refinance is in conjunction with rehabilitation of the housing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; projects financed with tax-exempt bonds must comply with the Maryland Qualified Allocation Plan. Priority funding areas preferred.
requirements_list: Minimum of five units in the project
Projects using tax-exempt bond financing must contain complete independent dwelling units
Projects must comply with the Maryland Qualified Allocation Plan to receive unallocated 4 percent Low Income Housing Tax Credits
All loans must be insured or have other forms of credit enhancement acceptable to the program
A first lien position is generally required for all bond loans
All loans funded with tax-exempt bonds must comply with federal requirements established for tax-exempt revenue bonds

Housing must be available to low-income households: either 20% of units available to households earning 50% or less of area median income, or 40% of units available to households earning 60% or less of area median income
For Tax/TE Financing structures: GNMA Loan must have HUD/GNMA credit enhancement via Section 221(d), 220, or other similar HUD programs; FHA Risk Sharing with CDA is not eligible for GNMA loans
A MAP Lender must be engaged by the borrower for GNMA loan structures
For unrated private placement bonds: the entity purchasing the Bonds must be approved by CDA and agree to retain the Bonds for the entire term without selling, pledging, or transferring ownership
For rated bond transactions: a bankruptcy opinion meeting rating agency requirements must be provided at borrower's expense
Bond proceeds must be sufficient to satisfy the 50% test for Tax Credits
Full amount of Bonds must be secured 100% by cash collateral (Letter of Credit is not sufficient)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Awards funding based on readiness to proceed. Applications accepted throughout the year on a rolling basis. Contact Housing Development Programs at dhcd.rentalhousing@maryland.gov or 301-429-7854 for application procedures and requirements. For Tax/TE Financing structures and TEFRA public hearing requirements, contact Benedict DuRant at benedict.durant@maryland.gov or 301-429-7823. Prospective borrowers may meet with CDA Multifamily staff to discuss financing options and structure. Multiple financing options are available; applicants should consult with CDA loan underwriters to determine the most suitable structure for their project.

structured_extraction.program_name: Multifamily Energy Efficiency and Housing Affordability (MEEHA) Program - EmPOWER
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.program_description: This program promotes energy efficiency and housing affordability in affordable multifamily rental housing developments by funding measures to reduce electric or gas consumption, including limited heating and cooling improvements. It aims to reduce greenhouse gases and keep housing affordable.
structured_extraction.program_audience: This program is for owners and developers of affordable multifamily rental properties. Eligible applicants include government bodies, for-profit companies, non-profit organizations, and individuals.

structured_extraction.program_name: Multifamily Energy Efficiency and Housing Affordability (MEEHA) Program - Greenhouse Gas Reduction Program (GHGRP)
structured_extraction.program_description: This program promotes energy efficiency and housing affordability in affordable multifamily rental housing developments by funding measures to reduce direct greenhouse gas emissions through replacing fossil fuel equipment with electric equipment and building energy conservation measures. Grants are provided to multifamily properties that are affordable or house low-income households.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: GHGRP provides grants only with no loans available. Funding offers up to $15,000 per dwelling unit with a project cap of $1.25 million. Funding allocation is $8.75 million in fiscal year 2024, and $5 million each in fiscal years 2025 and 2026. Funds support replacing fossil fuel equipment with electric equipment, building energy conservation and alternative energy generating systems such as solar photovoltaics, and incidental repairs necessary to change fossil fuel infrastructure to electric infrastructure. The broader MEEHA EmPower program also offers loans for energy efficiency improvements.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications are accepted on an ongoing basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of affordable multifamily rental housing developments with existing buildings of 35,000 gross square feet or more seeking to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and maintain housing affordability. Also includes multifamily property owners and developers with affordable or low-income serving properties. Projects must house at least 51% of tenants at or below 80% Area Median Income (AMI).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduce direct greenhouse gas emissions through replacing fossil fuel equipment with electric equipment. Building energy conservation and alternative energy generating systems such as solar photovoltaics. Energy efficiency improvements to multifamily properties. Incidental repairs required to allow installation of or protect program-funded energy saving measures.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. All counties eligible.
requirements_list: A minimum of 51% of households must be at 80% Area Median Income (AMI) or less for a minimum of 15 years

Existing buildings with 35,000 gross square feet of floor area or more, excluding parking garages, or two or more buildings with combined gross floor area of 35,000 square feet or more served by same electric or gas meter or same heating/cooling system (not a district energy system)
Project must work with a DHCD Qualified Energy Professional to complete an energy audit (for rehabilitation projects) or energy certification review (for new construction projects)
Project must demonstrate readiness to proceed, energy savings potential, and greenhouse gas reduction
Project must submit completed application and supporting documents including utility bills, property documentation, proof of affordability, W-9 form, and MBE commitment form
Gut Rehabilitation or Change of Use projects can receive new construction funding
Multifamily property must be affordable or house low income households
Property owner must authorize utility company to release energy use information to DHCD for evaluation purposes
If no existing regulatory agreement or tax covenant exists, DHCD will create a regulatory agreement to be recorded for projects awarded funds
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Property owner sets up Energy Star Portfolio Manager account and generates benchmarking report following MDE and/or EPA guidelines. 2. Owner submits completed MEEHA application with Portfolio Manager baseline report, third-party verification report, and other required documents to MultifamilyEnergy.dhcd@maryland.gov. 3. Owner engages a DHCD Qualified Energy Professional to perform energy audit and create energy audit report. 4. Qualified Energy Professional submits energy audit report and recommended scope of work to DHCD with greenhouse gas emissions reductions data and estimated costs. 5. DHCD reviews and provides feedback on funding request. 6. DHCD creates a grant agreement to be executed by all parties. 7. Construction phase begins with DHCD Project Manager conducting monthly meetings and visual inspections. 8. Project installs the funded greenhouse gas reduction measures. 9. DHCD releases funding on reimbursement basis through requisition process as work is completed and verified. 10. Project provides annual energy use benchmarking reports to DHCD for minimum of two years after construction completion. 11. Project enters the affordability period after construction is completed.

structured_extraction.program_description: Designed for Community Development Financial Institutions (CDFIs) to receive capital for relending to small businesses, particularly those owned and operated by socially and economically disadvantaged individuals (SEDI) and very small businesses (VSB) located in CDFI Investment Areas. Part of the SSBCI Neighborhood BusinessWorks program.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: DHCD provides SSBCI Loans to CDFIs for relending to qualifying small businesses. Loan size ranges from $2,000,000 to $15,000,000 based on CDFI capacity. SSBCI Loans bear interest at 0%-2% with terms up to 7 years and annual renewal options thereafter. Funds are relent to small businesses with targeted individual small business loans (SBLs) of up to $250,000 (unless prior written approval for higher amounts is granted). SBLs bear interest not to exceed 18%, with terms up to 5 years for general assets or longer terms for assets with longer useful lives. Combined origination fee and points capped at 1%, with application fees not exceeding $100. SSBCI funds (20% for non-SEDI/non-VSB businesses, 30% for SEDI/VSB businesses) are matched with private capital (80% and 70% respectively, with a target leverage goal of 10:1). SSBCI funds are in a top loss position on each SBL. CDFIs must have 20% at risk. Applications processed on a first-come, first-served basis.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community Development Financial Institutions (CDFIs) seeking capital to relend to small businesses, with priority given to socially and economically disadvantaged business owners (SEDI) and very small businesses (VSB) with fewer than 10 employees.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: CDFI Lenders relend SSBCI funds to qualifying small businesses for: working capital, marketing/planning/feasibility studies, real estate acquisition down payments, minor renovations, minor leasehold improvements, machinery and equipment acquisition, and other costs associated with opening or expanding a small business. Ineligible uses include residential/housing developments, facilities such as hospitals or universities, and businesses such as adult entertainment facilities, gambling facilities, gun shops, liquor stores, massage parlors, pawn shops, tanning salons, or tattoo parlors.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must be located in CDFI Investment Areas in Maryland. CDFIs may serve any Maryland counties.
requirements_list: CDFI certification and designation required
Financial stability and good standing with the State and Internal Revenue Service
Experience in administering small business loan programs including origination, credit and compliance underwriting, loan servicing, post-closing asset management, and compliance reporting
Ability to leverage eligible required private capital as a match to SSBCI funding
Capacity to comply with SSBCI Statutes, Regulations and Policies and DHCD requirements
Readiness to provide adequate resources and staff to begin making SBLs within 90 days of closing the SSBCI Loan
Ability to provide technical assistance to SBL Borrowers
Outreach capabilities to very small businesses (VSBs) and socially and economically disadvantaged individual-led businesses (SEDIs)
Proof of private capital match from qualified private source
Minimum 20% CDFI capital at risk
Minimum 1:1 private capital to SSBCI fund match (federal requirement)
Small business focus: SBL Borrowers must have fewer than 500 employees
Individual SBL not to exceed $250,000 unless prior written DHCD approval obtained
SBL interest rate not to exceed 18%
No prepayment penalties on SBLs
Monthly, quarterly, and annual reporting requirements
Annual audited financial statements required
Post-closing file access for DHCD asset management and federal auditors
Non-discrimination in lending based on race, color, religion, sex, handicap, familial status, or national origin
CDFI may not have equity interest, security interest, or be a stakeholder in SBL Borrowers
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: CDFIs submit the SSBCI NBW Loan to Lender Application (Appendix A) to DHCD at dhcd.ssbci@maryland.gov. The application must include organization information, proof of CDFI certification, explanation of capacity and experience in small business lending, projected annual loan production for a 6-year period, description of private capital leverage strategy, verification of financial stability and committed resources, detailed lending program description including demographic/geographic/industry targets, outreach capabilities to VSBs and SEDIs, loan product details, reporting and audit capability description, technical assistance plans, and any outstanding state liabilities. Required supporting documentation includes the organization's most recent Annual Report, Annual Financial Statement, 501(c)(3) Organizational documents, and last 3 years of Organization Tax Returns. Applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis. Once approved, the Lender receives a commitment letter reflecting total SSBCI Loan commitment, required private capital match, and proposed SBL funding timetable. SSBCI Loans must be closed according to terms and conditions provided by the Maryland Office of the Attorney General. Lenders are subject to quarterly and annual progress assessments by DHCD.

structured_extraction.program_description: Designed to fund and grow early-stage businesses in Maryland with high potential job growth that have already raised equity from early-stage investors and are seeking bridge financing to achieve milestones and reach their next equity raise. The program provides venture debt or convertible notes with SSBCI funds on a pari passu basis or better with private capital match.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Venture debt or convertible notes with SSBCI funds on a pari passu basis or better with private capital match. SSBCI funds must cause and result in the private capital match. Target SSBCI portion of venture debt ranges from $500,000 to $2,500,000. Typical bridge rounds are greater than $2,000,000. Repayment in principal and interest or convertible note structure. Aggregate funding round must be less than $20,000,000.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Early-stage businesses in Maryland with fewer than 500 employees and high potential for job growth that have already raised equity from early-stage investors. Existing paid-in capital exceeding $2,000,000 or revenues exceeding $1,000,000 required. Priority given to very small businesses with fewer than 10 employees and businesses owned and operated by socially and economically disadvantaged individuals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Bridge financing to support early-stage businesses in scaling operations and achieving milestones to reach the next equity raise.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses located in Maryland.
requirements_list: Less than 500 employees
Existing paid-in capital exceeding $2,000,000 or revenues exceeding $1,000,000
Minimum required private capital match to SSBCI funds ratio of 1:1
Target matching private capital to SSBCI funds ratio greater than 2:1
Businesses must have already raised equity from early-stage investors
High potential for job growth and positioned to scale
Aggregate funding round less than $20,000,000
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested businesses should email dhcd.ssbci@maryland.gov for more information and to express interest.

structured_extraction.program_name: National Capital Strategic Economic Development Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides competitive funds to support commercial and residential development activities in targeted revitalization areas. It focuses on neighborhoods where modest investment and coordinated strategy will have significant revitalization impact.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant funding forcommercial and residential development projectsincluding down payment assistance forhomebuyers, acquisition and rehabilitationof vacant properties, property improvements,energy efficiency upgrades, affordablehousing development, mixed-use development,community open space and publicinfrastructure enhancement, and strategicdemolition.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments and community development organizations in designated Sustainable Communities areas within Montgomery and Prince George's counties
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment assistance for homebuyers, acquisition or rehabilitation of vacant or dilapidated properties, improvement of existing residential and business properties, energy efficiency through weatherization and energy retrofits, affordable housing development, mixed-use projects combining housing retail and office space, community open space or public infrastructure development, and strategic demolition
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in Sustainable Communities in Prince George's County within the Interstate 495 boundary and District of Columbia area, or in Montgomery County within an Enterprise Zone or bounded by Prince George's County, Maryland Route 200, Interstate 270, Interstate 495 to the Maryland state line, and the District of Columbia.
requirements_list: Projects must support goals and objectives in the targeted area's Sustainable Communities Action Plan
Projects must be located in eligible Sustainable Communities areas
Applicants must be local governments or community development organizations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For application details and procedures, visit the State Revitalization Programs webpage. Contact your Regional Project Manager with questions about specific address eligibility. Use the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper to verify your jurisdiction's NED boundary.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal affordable housing production program that increases and preserves the supply of decent, safe, and sanitary affordable housing for extremely low-income and very low-income households. Provides financing for the development and preservation of affordable rental housing in priority funding areas. The program targets permanent rental housing for extremely low-income (ELI) households, defined as those with incomes at the greater of 30% of applicable Area Median Income (AMI) or at or below the poverty line.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: HTF funds may be used as broadly and flexibly as permitted by federal regulations to address unique underwriting needs of each project. Forms of assistance include: equity investments, interest-bearing loans or advances, non-interest bearing loans or advances, deferred payment loans, and grants. Ninety percent (90%) of the annual HTF allocation is used for production, preservation, and rehabilitation of affordable rental housing through acquisition, new construction, reconstruction, or rehabilitation of non-luxury housing with suitable amenities. Up to 10% may be retained for administrative and planning expenses. Operating cost assistance is permitted but limited to no more than one-third of the annual HTF allocation and must be fully utilized within 5 years of award. Assistance may take multiple forms including development hard costs, acquisition costs, related soft costs, relocation costs, and operating/rental assistance for rental housing.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis; funds awarded based on readiness to proceed
structured_extraction.program_audience: Developers, non-profit and for-profit sponsors, and housing organizations working to create or preserve affordable rental housing for extremely low-income and very low-income households, including homeless families.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Production and preservation of affordable rental housing for extremely low-income and very low-income households through acquisition, new construction, reconstruction, or rehabilitation of non-luxury housing with suitable amenities. HTF funds may support development hard costs, acquisition costs, related soft costs, relocation costs, and operating/rental assistance. Projects must serve ELI households and provide permanent rental housing with a minimum affordability period of 30 years.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland; priority funding areas. All projects involving new construction must be located in a Priority Funding Area (PFA) under Maryland's Smart Green and Growing Initiative, which includes incorporated municipalities, areas between Baltimore and Washington beltways, Sustainable Communities, enterprise zones, and certified heritage areas within locally designated growth areas.
requirements_list: Must serve extremely low-income or very low-income households defined as incomes at the greater of 30% AMI or at or below poverty line
Housing must be decent, safe, and sanitary
Projects must be located in priority funding areas for new construction
Must have site control extending at least 180 calendar days after application date
Must submit market assessment documenting housing needs of ELI individuals
Must submit Phase I Environmental Site Assessment for multifamily projects (more than 4 units); single family housing does not require Phase I ESA
Must provide evidence of utility availability (water, sewer, electric, gas, telephone, internet, cable)
Sites must be properly zoned for intended use; zoning changes must include documentation of status and timeline
Must submit Capital Needs Assessment for acquisition/rehabilitation projects showing remaining useful life exceeds affordability period
Must demonstrate developer experience with similar projects during past 5 years
Must provide financial statements for 3 fiscal years prior to application plus interim statements
All projects must be underwritten with minimum 5% vacancy rate
Annual operating expenses must be between $4,000-$7,000 per unit per year (waivers available for small projects up to 40 units or master-metered utilities)
Minimum $300 per unit per year reserves for replacement deposits
Operating reserves of 3-6 months underwritten operating expenses required
Minimum 1.15 debt service coverage ratio in first year of stabilized operations
Rents and revenue projected to increase no more than 2% annually
Operating expenses (including property taxes) projected to increase minimum 3% annually
Environmental assessment checklist or report must be included (not more than 1 year old at application)
For acquisition/rehabilitation projects, Phase I ESA must include lead-based paint and asbestos testing

Projects must comply with all HTF environmental provisions including historic preservation, farmland, airport zones, coastal barrier resources, coastal zone management, floodplains, wetlands, explosives/hazards, contamination, noise, endangered species, wild and scenic rivers, safe drinking water, and sole-source aquifers standards
Property must be free of hazardous materials, contamination, toxic chemicals and gases, and radioactive substances
Projects must avoid Superfund or CERCLIS sites within 0.25 miles without EPA/State agency clearance letter
Interior noise levels must not exceed 45 decibels; exterior noise standards vary by exposure level with mitigation requirements
Must meet Secretary of Interior Standards for Rehabilitation if property is listed or eligible for National Register of Historic Places
For rehabilitation projects, expansion of footprint into wetlands is not allowed
All rehabilitation projects must meet applicable HTF rehabilitation standards and requirements at 24 CFR §93.301(b)
Major systems must have remaining useful life of minimum 20 years upon completion
Developer/Owner must have demonstrated financial capacity with adequate working capital and net worth for guarantees
Recipient must provide certification of compliance with all HTF program requirements
Must demonstrate ability and financial capacity to undertake, comply, and manage eligible activity
Must demonstrate familiarity with other federal, state, or local housing programs used in conjunction with HTF
Must have demonstrated experience and capacity to own, construct, rehabilitate, manage and operate affordable multifamily rental housing
Section 3 requirements apply to projects with construction and total project cost over $200,000 in federal funds
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: HTF projects are selected by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development for funding consideration, subject to availability of funds. Applications are reviewed for eligibility and evaluated using threshold criteria. HTF funds are awarded to eligible projects through a non-competitive, first-ready first-served basis. Applications may be submitted by sponsors as part of a project application, or Department staff may propose HTF funds during project review and underwriting. Successful recipients receive a Notice of Award stating the Department's intent to award HTF funds. Applicants must complete an Application Submission Package that includes: market assessment, site control documentation, Capital Needs Assessment (if applicable), Phase I Environmental Site Assessment, utility availability evidence, zoning documentation, Anticipated Development Schedule, and all required financial and developer experience documentation. Projects are underwritten and evaluated based on developer capacity, project feasibility, readiness to proceed, geographic diversity, and alignment with state priorities. HTF funds may be requested as part of applications to other Department housing programs (RHFP, LIHTC, MBP, STHGP) or used independently. The Department requires all applications to contain a description of eligible activities to be conducted with HTF funds. Projects must comply with all federal HTF requirements, HUD interim rules, and state rehabilitation standards.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Development Administration issues bonds to fund loans for business projects. A business project is broadly defined and qualifies if it is located in a priority funding area and is acquired, owned, developed, constructed, reconstructed, rehabilitated or improved for the purposes of carrying on a business, whether or not for profit. Some qualified business projects are also located in traditionally underserved areas defined as Sustainable Communities. The program, known as Neighborhood BusinessWorks (NBW), has been financing small businesses in Maryland for over 20 years with a current loan portfolio of 158 loans with an aggregate outstanding principal balance in excess of $20 million. The delinquent loans represent less than 1% of the total outstanding legacy loan portfolio.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Bond-funded senior and/or subordinate loans for business projects located in priority funding areas or Sustainable Communities. For-profit borrowers must provide minimum 10% equity contribution with maximum 90% combined loan-to-value (CLTV) financing (senior loans with up to 30% top loss coverage) or maximum 100% CLTV with one senior loan (70% LTV) and one subordinate loan. Non-profit borrowers must provide minimum 5% equity with maximum 95% CLTV (senior loans with up to 30% top loss coverage) or maximum 100% CLTV with two-loan structure. All loans require minimum 1.50 debt service coverage ratio (DSCR) throughout loan life and 6-month debt service reserve. CDA earns interest override (minimum 0.60% for portfolio administration plus 0.40% loan servicing fee) and upfront financing fees (0.5%-1% plus $25,000 legal counsel fee plus closing costs). Project types include: (1) Commercial real estate construction and permanent financing for commercial and mixed-use projects; (2) Acquisition or refinance of stabilized commercial and mixed-use projects; (3) Non-profit facility loans for acquisition, rehabilitation and new construction of facilities for occupancy or use by qualified 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit businesses and 501(c)(3) non-profit organizations with projects in priority funding areas or Sustainable Communities seeking acquisition, development, construction, rehabilitation, or refinancing of commercial, mixed-use, or non-profit facility real estate
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition and permanent financing of commercial and mixed-use real estate; construction and permanent financing for commercial and mixed-use projects; refinance of stabilized commercial and mixed-use projects; non-profit facility loans for acquisition, rehabilitation and new construction of facilities for occupancy or use by qualified non-profit organizations
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in a priority funding area as defined in section 5-7B-02 of the State Finance and Procurement Article, or in Sustainable Communities as defined in section 6-205 of DHCD's Article, per Title 5, Subtitle 13 of the Economic Development Article, or per section 7-101 of the Transportation Article. All Maryland counties are eligible.
requirements_list: Project must be located in a priority funding area or Sustainable Communities
Project must be acquired, owned, developed, constructed, reconstructed, rehabilitated or improved for purposes of carrying on a business
For-profit borrowers: minimum 10% equity or total cost borrower contribution
Non-profit borrowers: minimum 5% equity or total cost borrower contribution
Minimum debt service coverage ratio (DSCR) of 1.50 throughout loan life for CDA-funded loans; 1.25 for credit-enhanced non-CDA loans
Loan debt service reserve equal to 6 months of maximum annual debt service
For-profit borrowers: maximum 90% combined loan-to-value (CLTV) or 100% with two-loan structure
Non-profit borrowers: maximum 95% combined loan-to-value (CLTV) or 100% with two-loan structure
Conservative loan-life pro-forma demonstrating adequate debt service coverage
Qualified professional and independent collateral valuation acceptable to CDA, MHF and debt investors
All CDA loans over $250,000 must be reviewed and recommended for approval by NBW Loan Review Committee
Industry-standard underwriting criteria including creditworthiness analysis, market position, adequacy of collateral, and soundness of business plan and management
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Online application process. All NBW projects are evaluated based on industry-standard underwriting criteria including analysis of borrower creditworthiness, market position of assisted businesses, adequacy of collateral, and soundness of business plan and management team. All projects are evaluated based on revitalization impact including elimination of blight, catalytic redevelopment stimulus and job retention/creation. Loans over $250,000 are reviewed by the 5-member NBW Loan Review Committee. CDA-funded business loans are subject to Housing Finance Review Committee (HFRC) approval. All CDA debt issuance supported by business loans requires Revenue Bond Advisory Board (RBAB) approval.

structured_extraction.program_description: Designed to assist small businesses with working capital and owner-occupied real estate acquisition or renovation by providing below-market-rate loans up to $5 million through a participating lender model. Part of the SSBCI Neighborhood BusinessWorks program, it helps small businesses operating in Maryland with fewer than 500 employees, with priority given to very small businesses with fewer than 10 employees and socially and economically disadvantaged individuals (SEDI).
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Senior or junior debt with SSBCI portion ranging from $350,000 to $5,000,000. Up to 30% program match. Interest rates based on underwriting analysis. Flexible loan terms up to 30 years depending on use and loan amount. Requires proof of private capital match (4:1 target for non-SEDI/VSB, 2.3:1 target for SEDI/VSB, minimum 1:1). Personal guarantees and collateral required. Prepayment lockout period may apply.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses operating in Maryland with less than 500 employees. Priority given to very small businesses with fewer than 10 employees and businesses owned and operated by socially and economically disadvantaged individuals (SEDI).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Owner-occupied real estate acquisition or renovation, mixed-use projects combining residential and commercial uses, working capital, machinery and equipment, and other costs associated with sustaining or expanding a small business in manufacturing, service, retail, office, or mixed-use sectors.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Business must be located or plan to locate in a CDFI Investment Area in Maryland.
requirements_list: Less than 500 employees
Proof of private capital match with target ratio of 4:1 (80-20) for non-SEDI/VSB or 2.3:1 (70-30) for SEDI/VSB
Minimum required private capital match of 1:1
Business located or to be located in a CDFI Investment Area
Demonstrated business viability and potential impact on neighborhood
Readiness to proceed with project
Adequate cash flow and collateral
Local governments are not eligible
Priority given to very small businesses with fewer than 10 employees
Priority given to socially and economically disadvantaged individuals (SEDI)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must complete an SSBCI Neighborhood BusinessWorks loan application package via the online application portal at https://apps.dhcd.state.md.us/nbwapplication. The application portal requires user registration and login. Upon approval, applicants receive a commitment letter. Loan approval requires meeting underwriting guidelines. Applicants must execute necessary legal documents prior to disbursement of loan proceeds.

structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program that provides flexible financing to new or expanding small businesses and nonprofit organizations for projects in targeted geographic areas that strengthen communities. The program supports businesses located in Priority Funding Areas and Sustainable Communities across the state. These loans provide direct, insured, or guaranteed financing to eligible businesses.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: This program provides direct, insured, or guaranteed loans to eligible businesses.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on rolling basis; contact for additional information
structured_extraction.program_audience: New or expanding small businesses and nonprofit organizations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is available to businesses in Priority Funding Areas and Sustainable Communities throughout the state.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should contact the program for more information on how to apply. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides funding to local jurisdictions and their internet service provider partners to extend existing broadband service to unserved areas within a community.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants between $50,000 and $500,000 paying for capital construction costs to extend broadband service to unserved areas. The grant covers 70% to 90% of eligible capital construction costs based on project density (determined by households per mile for wired projects or households per tower for wireless projects). Applicants must provide a match of 10% to 30% based on project density. For wired projects: fewer than 8 households per mile requires 10% match; 8 to fewer than 15 households per mile requires 20% match; 15 or more households per mile requires 30% match. For wireless projects: fewer than 40 households per tower requires 10% match; 40 to fewer than 70 households per tower requires 20% match; 70 or more households per tower requires 30% match. Match can be cash or in-kind (for ISP partners only). Eligible uses include construction of facilities to deploy service, middle mile infrastructure directly necessary to provide service, and electronics necessary to deliver service (OLTs, ONTs, routers, switches, firewalls, wireless equipment, modems, etc.).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local jurisdictions (counties or municipalities) and internet service provider partners seeking to expand broadband service to unserved areas
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital construction costs to extend existing broadband service to unserved areas, including construction of facilities, middle mile infrastructure directly necessary to provide service, and electronics necessary to deliver service such as optical line terminals, optical network terminals, routers, switches, firewalls, wireless radio equipment, antennae, access points, modems, and equipment shelters.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Unserved areas statewide defined as areas lacking terrestrial, fixed internet service at speeds above 25 Mbps download and/or 3 Mbps upload and/or with latency above 50 milliseconds. Areas having received state grant funding in the past are ineligible.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local jurisdiction (County or Municipality) with an ISP Partner
Service area must be unserved (lacking terrestrial, fixed internet service at speeds above 25 Mbps download and/or 3 Mbps upload and/or with latency above 50 milliseconds)
Areas having received state grant funding in the past are ineligible
Match requirement of 10% to 30% based on project density (determined by households per mile for wired or households per tower for wireless)

Projects must be able to provide minimum internet connectivity of 100 Mbps download and 100 Mbps upload with maximum latency of 50 milliseconds (with limited exceptions for up to 100 Mbps download and 20 Mbps upload if scalable)
All equipment must be new and non-depreciated
Costs incurred prior to submission of completed application are not eligible
Local jurisdiction must have entered into partnership with ISP Partner prior to funding agreement
Must comply with American Rescue Plan Act requirements and all federal rules regarding the funding
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit one electronic PDF copy of response to osb.md@maryland.gov on or before December 23, 2021 with subject line including 'Neighborhood Connect', local jurisdiction name, and project name. Application package must include: completed Grant Application Form, executive summary, partnership description, experience statement, network design and construction details, subscriber profile and demographic data, subscriber costs and service options, detailed line-item capital construction budget (as PDF and Excel spreadsheet), project schedule with key milestones, GIS files (shp, kmz, or kml format) showing PFSA properties and infrastructure, and all items combined into one zip file. All submissions reviewed for completeness and eligibility. Applications scored on 25-point scale based on need for service/project benefits (up to 5 points), match contribution source (up to 6 points), network delivery speed (up to 10 points), and subscriber options (up to 4 points). Awards made high to low score as funding permits. Projects must be completed by December 31, 2023.

structured_extraction.program_description: The state provides matching grants to support operating costs of certified Neighborhood Housing Services corporations that work to stabilize and improve the housing market in targeted low- and moderate-income neighborhoods. These organizations partner with residents, financial institutions, community organizations, local governments, and the state to provide homeownership opportunities, home rehabilitation, homebuyer education, and community organizing activities.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Each eligible Neighborhood Housing Services corporation may apply for a grant up to $50,000 that does not exceed one-third of its annual operating budget. Each eligible umbrella corporation may apply for a grant for each program under its supervision up to $50,000 that does not exceed one-third of the annual operating budget of that program. The state grant must be matched by funds from local governments, private businesses, and individual contributions.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Certified Neighborhood Housing Services corporations that are approved by the Neighborhood Reinvestment Corporation. Currently eligible organizations include Montgomery Housing Partnership Inc., NHS of Baltimore Inc., Salisbury NHS Inc., and St. Ambrose Housing Aid Center.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supporting operating costs of Neighborhood Housing Services corporations that provide homeownership opportunities through closing cost assistance and homebuyer education, home rehabilitation for ownership and rental, and community organizing activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Serves targeted low- and moderate-income neighborhoods in Maryland. NHS of Baltimore and St. Ambrose Housing Aid Center serve several neighborhoods in Baltimore City and Baltimore County. Salisbury NHS serves the West Side, Church Street, and Camden neighborhoods of Salisbury, Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Neighborhood Housing Services corporation approved and certified by the Neighborhood Reinvestment Corporation
Local political subdivision must agree to financially support the local NHS corporation and participate on its board of directors
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible NHS corporations submit grant applications for funding. Contact the Poverty Solutions Team at the Division of Neighborhood Revitalization for application procedures and guidelines.

structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.program_description: The Net Zero Loan Program provides low-interest construction financing to support the building of energy-efficient homes that produce as much or more energy than they use. This program also provides construction loans or helps improve existing loans for building low-energy or net-zero homes.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers low-interest direct loans and loan enhancements for construction of energy-efficient net-zero homes.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications are not currently being accepted
structured_extraction.program_audience: Builders and developers constructing low-energy or net-zero homes.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used for construction loans or to enhance existing loans for building low-energy or net-zero homes.

structured_extraction.program_description: A targeted investment that expands access to healthy and fresh foods in Maryland communities experiencing food insecurity by providing direct grants to eligible food retailers.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
list_of_relevant_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from $25,000 to $150,000 with up to $2 million in total funding available. A $250 processing fee is required for all applications and may be paid directly from awarded grant funds if approved. Funds support equipment purchases (e.g., refrigeration, shelving), buildout and facility upgrades, capital costs for inventory expansion, initial inventory costs, working capital for expansion or construction, and infrastructure and technology for SNAP/EBT acceptance. Applicants may also request supplemental loan funding through DHCD's Neighborhood BusinessWorks (NBW) program, which undergoes financial review to assess debt capacity. Selected recipients may also receive co-awards through the Maryland Market Money (MMM) program administered by the Maryland Department of Agriculture if SNAP-eligible.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit or nonprofit food retailers with a maximum of 500 employees, serving communities with a Maryland Community Business Compass Fresh Food Gap Score of 60% or higher.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Equipment purchases such as furniture, fixtures, refrigeration and shelving; renovation and build-out; facility upgrades; capital needs related to inventory expansion (non-prepared foods); working capital involved with expansion or renovations/construction; and infrastructure/technology for SNAP/EBT setup.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Retailers must serve a community with a Maryland Community Business Compass Fresh Food Gap Score of 60% or higher. Exceptions may be granted on an individual basis.
requirements_list: Serve a community with a Maryland Community Business Compass Fresh Food Gap Score of 60% or higher (exceptions may be granted on an individual basis)
Operate at least 5 days per week year-round (farmers markets and on-farm markets exempt from 5-day requirement but must operate year-round)
Employ a maximum of 500 workers
Be registered and in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
Currently or plan to offer fresh, frozen, or minimally processed healthy foods
Dedicate at least 20% of inventory or food-sales space to healthy food items (based on square footage or dollar value of inventory)
Provide documentation, photos, or store layout to confirm compliance with healthy food requirements
Submit one year of business tax returns or audited financial statements (or alternative documentation if operating less than one year)
Submit detailed written plan describing use of grant funds (not to exceed 2 pages)
Provide information demonstrating business meets or will meet healthy and fresh food criteria
Submit relocation and expansion documentation if applicable (lease agreement, letter of intent, or proof of site control)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted through an online portal. The application period opened January 20, 2026 at 12:00 p.m. EST and closed February 20, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. EST. Applicants can schedule an initial consultation before applying. Completed applications must include all required documentation at the time of submission; incomplete applications will not be reviewed until missing components are submitted and verified. Applications are evaluated on a competitive basis for completeness, impact, and alignment with program priorities. DHCD staff evaluate eligible applications and refer the final list to the Review Committee for determinations. Timeline: February-March application review; April funding recommendations finalized; May award announcements; June Board of Public Works approval and disbursements.

structured_extraction.program_name: Operating Assistance Grants - Technical Assistance Grant (TAG)
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.program_description: The Technical Assistance Grant program assists nonprofit organizations and local governments with operating costs associated with community and economic revitalization efforts. Funds support administrative expenses such as salaries, contracts for professional services, and technology costs. The program offers grants up to $50,000 with no matching funds requirement. Projects must be located in or serve residents of a Priority Funding Area and must be completed within one year.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers grants up to $50,000. There is no requirement for matching funds. The funds must be used for operating expenses.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations and local governments involved in community and economic revitalization activities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can only be used for operating expenses, including salaries, contracts for professional services, and technology expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in or serve residents of a Priority Funding Area.
requirements_list: No matching funds are required.
Projects must be completed within one year.
Funds cannot be used for capital project costs.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register through the online Application Portal by selecting 'New User?' and completing the form. Registration approval may take up to 72 hours. Once registered, you can access and submit the application.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides financial assistance to help small businesses buy or renovate commercial real estate that they can operate in and use to build wealth. Funded by the federal State Small Business Credit Initiative (SSBCI).
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Senior or subordinate loan positions available with flexible terms designed to maximize community benefit. Loans range from $500,000 to $5 million with up to 30-year terms. Interest rates are determined by underwriting analysis. Borrower must provide minimum 1:1 private capital match (one dollar from private source for every dollar of DHCD loan). Personal guarantees required from all owners with more than 20% equity. Adequate collateral required. Total project costs cannot exceed $20 million.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses with fewer than 500 employees seeking to purchase or renovate commercial real estate.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Costs to purchase, construct, or renovate commercial real estate. Eligible uses include: buying space for current operations, moving to new location, purchasing property for first-time buyers without storefronts (e-commerce, food trucks, etc.), or buying property for business expansion. Renovation projects must be at least 51% owner-occupied upon completion. New construction must be at least 60% owner-occupied upon completion.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland.
requirements_list: Business must have fewer than 500 employees
Project cannot be 100% residential (mixed-use projects may qualify)
Minimum 1:1 private capital match required
Loan amount must be at least $500,000 and no more than $5 million
Personal guarantees required from all owners with more than 20% equity
Adequate collateral required
Total project costs cannot exceed $20 million

Business type exclusions: adult entertainment facilities, check cashing facilities, gambling facilities, gun shops, liquor stores, massage parlors, pawn shops, tanning salons, tattoo parlors, cannabis businesses
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online using the application portal at https://apps.dhcd.state.md.us/nbwapplication. Schedule a consultation or contact DHCD for more information at dhcd.maryland.gov/Business/Pages/Own-Your-Future.aspx or email dhcd.businesslending@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that expands the supply of affordable rental housing for low-income households through partnerships between state and local governments, and provides financing for non-governmental entities to create housing for individuals with disabilities or special needs.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides loans for rental housing occupied by households with incomes at or below 50% of the statewide median income. Loan amounts are limited to $75,000 per unit for large projects and up to $2 million without a per-unit cap for small projects (40 units or fewer). For individuals with disabilities or special needs units, resident households must have gross income not exceeding 30% of Area Median Income. Loan repayment is generally deferred for up to 40 years as long as the local government entity continues to own the housing and rents it to income-eligible households.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Requests accepted on an ongoing basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, housing authorities, entities owned in part by local governments or housing authorities, and non-governmental entities creating housing for individuals with disabilities or special needs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: New construction and acquisition or rehabilitation of rental housing including apartment buildings, townhouses, single-family homes, single room occupancy buildings, and shared housing facilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Local government must make a contribution of the land or a contribution of equal value from non-state resources.
requirements_list: Local government or housing authority must apply or entity owned in part by local government or housing authority
Local participant must contribute land or equal value from non-state resources
Local participant must manage the project or arrange for another party to manage it
Resident households must have gross income not exceeding 50% of statewide median income adjusted for family size
Residents with disabilities or special needs units must have gross income not exceeding 30% of Area Median Income adjusted for household size
Occupants must provide tenant contributed services as detailed in statute and regulations (except for individuals with disabilities or special needs units)
Local government must continue to own housing and rent to income-eligible households to maintain loan deferral
Any profits from project sale must be used for other low-income housing purposes
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Requests for funding are accepted on an ongoing basis and evaluated based on meeting the program purpose, readiness to proceed, and availability of funding. If Partnership Rental Housing Program funding is requested with other department funds, the application requirements and deadlines of the other funding must be met.

structured_extraction.program_name: Project CORE Phase I – Demolition of Blighted Properties
structured_extraction.program_description: The state invests funding to demolish city blocks of blight in Baltimore City. The Maryland Stadium Authority serves as project manager, working with the Baltimore City Department of Housing to identify properties for demolition, and then grading, seeding, and fencing demolished sites. Phase I includes demolition of blighted properties across recommended clusters in Baltimore City, followed by redevelopment and stabilization projects.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The state invests $75 million over four years, with an additional $18.5 million from Baltimore City. The city provides in-kind services valued at $0.25 for every $1 in state funding. FY17 Phase I awards totaled $15,860,000 distributed across 30 projects with estimated total project costs of $300,582,276, including demolition, redevelopment, site preparation, and stabilization initiatives.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City agencies and nonprofit community development organizations working on property demolition and urban revitalization
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Demolition of blighted properties, site grading, seeding, fencing, redevelopment, site preparation, stabilization, and community revitalization projects
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City only, focused on identified Year 1 demolition clusters with varying blight density levels

structured_extraction.program_name: Project CORE Phase II – Revitalization Through Redevelopment
structured_extraction.program_description: The state leverages Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development programs to encourage new investment in blighted communities that have been cleared through Phase I demolition.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The state leverages an estimated $600 million through existing Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development programs to encourage new investment in revitalized communities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public, private, and nonprofit development partners investing in Baltimore City communities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: New investment and redevelopment in blighted communities
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that activates vacant buildings and storefronts, supports small businesses, creates jobs, improves commercial corridors, and increases local economic activity by providing grant funding to place-based economic development organizations working to improve the vitality of Maryland's commercial corridors. Organizations in designated Sustainable Communities and Main Street areas receive grants to subgrant to businesses for rental assistance, renovation, and equipment costs to activate vacant spaces.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $300,000 per applicant in grants to place-based economic development entities, Main Streets, and Arts and Entertainment Districts. For FY2024, $8.0 million was available to be awarded. Organizations then subgrant funds to businesses for rental assistance, renovation, and equipment to activate vacant storefronts and buildings in business districts. Sub-grantees (small businesses) can use Project Restore funds for rent, interior/exterior renovation, furniture, fixtures, and equipment only. Grant term is from execution of award agreement through December 31, 2025. Awarded organizations can request up to 15% of their grant for operating costs including staff, professional services, marketing, and promotion directly related to Project Restore 2.0. Funding for operations is direct deposited after award agreement execution. Funding for project activities at awarded properties is disbursed upon approval of Request for Payment, which occurs before construction/purchasing begins.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: FY2024 Application deadline was Wednesday, April 24, 2024 at 5pm EST. Application is closed; uncertain if another round will be offered
structured_extraction.program_audience: Place-based economic development organizations, Main Streets, Arts and Entertainment Districts, local governments (Town, City, or County), and other designated economic development organizations working to improve commercial corridors in Maryland. Small businesses are not eligible to apply directly but receive funding as sub-grantees through awarded organizations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Financial support to activate vacant buildings and storefronts, support small businesses, create jobs, improve commercial corridors, and increase local economic activity. Subgrants to businesses cover rental assistance, renovation, and equipment costs. Sub-grantees can use funds for rent, interior/exterior renovation, furniture, fixtures, and equipment to activate vacant commercial spaces. Funds cannot be used for acquisition, new construction, vehicles, operating costs for businesses, or projects in indoor shopping malls, industrial parks, or office parks. Funds must support street-level retail in walkable business districts in downtown and historic commercial corridors.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide; all awarded properties must be located in a DHCD-designated Sustainable Community. Priority consideration given to designated Sustainable Communities and Main Street areas.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a place-based economic development organization, local government entity (Town, City, or County), Main Street program, or Arts and Entertainment District
Applicant must have IRS-determined non-profit status (501c3 status specifically not required) or be a local government entity at time of application
Applicant must have at least 0.5 FTE staff at time of application
Small businesses are not eligible to apply directly
All awarded properties must be vacant at time of application (no executed lease with tenant at time of application)
Located in or serving a designated Sustainable Community at time of application
Focus on vacant storefronts or buildings in local business districts
Property must be activated and business operational by December 31, 2025
Each entity can only submit one application per funding round
Past Project Restore awardees (FY22, FY23) cannot receive funds for same property location; expansion to new locations may be eligible if other requirements met
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit applications through Maryland OneStop system. Applications must include specific vacant property addresses (1-3 properties recommended), property condition reports with photos, organizational capacity documentation, equity and inclusion strategy, alignment with organizational strategy, timeline for project completion, executed lease, sub-grant agreement templates, and budget with sources and uses of funds. All applications are reviewed after the submission deadline; no rolling review. Applications are first reviewed for threshold eligibility, then scored by DHCD staff on organizational readiness (0-100 points), equitable process creation, project alignment with strategy, and advancement of program goals. Selected organizations identify priority vacant storefronts/buildings and subgrant funds to eligible businesses. Following award, grantees submit Request for Payment (RFP) for each property before funds are spent, with pre-populated information, sub-grantee details, business plan, executed lease, project budget with sources/uses, service provider details, cost estimates, executed sub-grant agreement, and project timeline. Upon property completion, grantees submit Completion Report by property with opening date, Use & Occupancy permit, interior/exterior photos, Maryland Historic Trust determination, and paid receipts/invoices. One Final Report is submitted per organization within 30 days of grant term end with operating funds documentation, operational status confirmation, and program impact narrative. The program is currently closed and no new applications are being accepted.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Rental Housing Program provides financing to rehabilitate or create rental housing. The program aims to increase the supply of affordable rental housing for low-income residents through loans that can be combined with federal HOME funds, tax-exempt or taxable bond financing, low-income housing tax credits, and other private or public funds.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Most Rental Housing Fund loans have a term of up to 40 years, bear interest at a rate of 2 percent per annum, and are repayable from cash flow. The maximum loan amount does not exceed $2 million. Loans may be used for acquisition, construction, rehabilitation, and development costs, including lender fees, architectural and engineering fees, market studies, appraisals, legal fees, and other costs directly related to the development of the housing.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications are accepted at designated times during the year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit, limited profit, or nonprofit developers, nonprofit organizations, county governments, municipalities, or local housing authorities seeking to develop rental housing for low-income residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Loans may be used for acquisition, construction, rehabilitation, and development costs. Development costs include lender fees, architectural and engineering fees, market studies, appraisals, legal fees, and other costs directly related to the development of the housing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All new construction projects must be located in Priority Funding Areas.
requirements_list: Eligible residents must have incomes of no more than 60 percent of the area median income
The owner must reserve the same proportion of units for low-income tenants as the Rental Housing Program Funds are to the total financing
Eligible types of housing include newly constructed or rehabilitated rental housing, congregate housing, single-room occupancy, emergency shelters, and shared living facilities
Projects may be restricted to elderly residents
In some cases, small commercial rehabilitation housing projects may be considered
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted at designated times during the year and are evaluated against criteria established by the Department. Priority is given to projects that restrict units to tenants with incomes below 60 percent of median income, restrict units to low-income tenants for more than 40 years, provide tenant service packages, use non-State funds in addition to State funds, provide quality housing in a good location, and are sponsored by teams with demonstrated development and management ability.

structured_extraction.program_description: Rental Housing Works provides subordinate gap financing to support the creation and preservation of affordable rental housing. The program works in conjunction with the state's Multifamily Bond Program and 4% Low Income Housing Tax Credits to strengthen the Maryland economy and create jobs.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Subordinate loans funded from state general obligation bonds. Loans are structured with a 40-year term at 2% simple interest, due on sale, refinancing, or transfer of the property. Repayment is limited to 75% of annual cash flow. The loan features no regular interest during construction, with contingent interest payable from surplus cash or upon capital events. Maximum loan amount is $2.5 million per project, waivable under certain circumstances. Contingent interest equals a percentage of Surplus Cash or Borrower Net Proceeds (the greater of the percentage that the Loan comprises of Total Project Costs or 20%), up to a maximum aggregate amount equal to annual simple interest at 4% on the outstanding principal balance. During the Permanent Loan Period, the Applicable Surplus Cash Percentage is paid annually (typically 50% until Developer Fee is paid, then a specified percentage) toward principal reduction. After full repayment of principal, contingent interest payments continue from available Surplus Cash. Upon a Capital Event (sale, refinancing, or transfer), payment is due equal to the lesser of the Contingent Interest Percentage of Borrower Net Proceeds or outstanding Indebtedness plus Contingent Interest (not to exceed Maximum Contingent Interest Amount).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Affordable rental housing developers and sponsors seeking gap financing to support projects financed through the Multifamily Bond Program and 4% Low Income Housing Tax Credits.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Gap financing for the creation and preservation of affordable rental housing projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Projects must be financed using the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's Multifamily Bond Program and 4% Low Income Housing Tax Credits
Required zoning for use and density of development must be in place at application with proper documentation (letter from local zoning office or approved PUD resolution)
Award of competitive public and private funding sources necessary for financial feasibility must have been made prior to or concurrent with RHW application
Project's projected Full Time Equivalent (FTE) jobs must be documented using the Rental Housing Works Full Time Equivalent Job Calculator (FTE equals 2,080 hours per year)
Board of Public Works must approve all Rental Housing Works funding awards
Projects must meet the scoring criteria for bond loans as outlined in the Guide
Maximum state loans per project of $2.5 million (unless waived under certain circumstances)
Development or site plan approval is not required at application, but conditional use or special exception approval must be obtained before closing
Applicant must complete CDA Form 202 clearly identifying RHW funds requested and conforming to RHW limitations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted on an ongoing basis in conjunction with Multifamily Bond Program and 4% Low Income Housing Tax Credits applications. Applicants must submit a separate RHW application (available at http://www.mdhousing.org/website/Programs/rhw/application.aspx) along with a completed standard Application Submission Package and the following required documentation: completed CDA Form 202 with RHW funds clearly identified; written zoning documentation; certification that competitive funding awards have been made; completed FTE Job Calculator; and signed certification to RHW Application Submission Package. The department tracks applications by receipt date and reviews them alongside Multifamily Bond Program applications. Applications that meet threshold criteria are scored using evaluation criteria outlined in the program guide. After scoring, kick-off meetings are scheduled with a timeline and critical path schedule. Projects are funded on a first-ready, first-served basis. All RHW funding awards must be approved by the Board of Public Works.

structured_extraction.program_name: Request for Interest: Federal Funding Application Assistance
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides up to $125,000 in grants to local jurisdictions or their internet service provider partners to cover costs of preparing federal funding applications for broadband expansion to unserved rural areas. Eligible costs include market studies, engineering, legal, financial, and other approved consulting services.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 100% grant covering up to a maximum of $125,000 for costs associated with preparing federal funding applications for broadband expansion to unserved areas. Eligible costs include engineering consultants, financial consultants, marketing studies, legal consultants, and other approved services. Reimbursement is provided for properly contracted services required for the application. Costs will only be reimbursed for projects that submit a completed application for the federal funding program and meet the terms and conditions of the federal funding program.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No fixed deadline; rolling basis depending on federal funding opportunities and available state funding
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local jurisdictions and internet service provider partners seeking federal broadband funding to serve unserved rural residents and businesses
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Costs associated with preparing federal funding applications for broadband expansion to unserved areas, including engineering consultants, financial consultants, marketing studies, legal consultants, and other approved consulting services necessary for federal funding application preparation
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; projects must target unserved areas as defined by federal programs or areas without internet service at 25 Mbps down and 3 Mbps up; must comply with federal program requirements regarding areas that have not received prior federal broadband investments
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local jurisdiction or ISP partner
Project must target unserved areas meeting federal program requirements or OSB definition of unserved (25 Mbps down, 3 Mbps up minimum)
Project must be able to provide minimum internet connectivity of 1000 Mbps down and 1000 Mbps up with maximum latency of 50 milliseconds, unless federal program is more restrictive
Applicant must submit completed application for federal funding program
