Project must meet terms and conditions of the federal funding program
Applicant must submit one electronic copy of response to OSB.MD@maryland.gov

Response must include cover letter with authorized representative contact information, completed application form signed by both local jurisdiction and ISP partner, business model summary, experience statement, network design and construction description, customer profile, and implementation schedule
Technology must be capable of meeting speed and latency requirements (technology neutral approach)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested applicants should contact the Office of Statewide Broadband to discuss their project and determine if an application can be funded. Applicants must submit one electronic copy of their response to OSB.MD@maryland.gov with the applicant name and 'Federal Funding Assistance RFP response' in the subject line. Response must include: (1) cover letter with local jurisdiction and partner contact information, (2) completed and signed application form, (3) business model summary, (4) experience statement of project team, (5) network design and construction description, (6) customer profile and competitive service assessment, and (7) implementation schedule with key milestones. The OSB will evaluate responses based on qualifications and ability to fulfill requirements. A successful applicant may be selected based on submittals and possible interview. Questions should be submitted in writing to OSB.MD@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.program_description: Section 811 Project Rental Assistance expands affordable housing for low-income adults with disabilities. The program helps eligible residents live in stable housing with access to supportive services. This federally funded grant provides project-based rental assistance for adults with disabilities who are between 18 and 61 years old. The program is a partnership with the Maryland Department of Disabilities and the Maryland Department of Health.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides project-based rental assistance for housing units.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on rolling basis; contact for additional information
structured_extraction.program_audience: This program helps for-profit and non-profit sponsors of affordable rental housing developments, as well as low-income adults with disabilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds provide project-based rental assistance for non-elderly adults with disabilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in priority funding areas.

structured_extraction.program_name: Seed Community Development Anchor Institution Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: The program provides competitive grants and loans to anchor institutions (colleges, universities, and hospitals) for community development projects that generate jobs, strengthen partnerships between institutions and the state, and create safer, healthier, and more attractive communities in underinvested areas.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants and loans are provided to anchor institutions for capital improvement projects. Applicants must provide matching funds equal to the amount of financial assistance received (1:1 match requirement).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Anchor institutions including institutions of higher education and hospital institutions in Maryland that meet specific organizational criteria.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital improvement projects in eligible locations such as Sustainable Communities or underinvested areas of the state that generate jobs and strengthen community partnerships.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Funds can only be used in Sustainable Communities or areas of the state that have not received prior investment. Geographic eligibility can be determined using the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper tool.
requirements_list: Must be an anchor institution (institution of higher education or hospital institution in Maryland)
Hospital institutions must have at least five physicians organized as a medical staff
Hospital institutions must maintain facilities to provide diagnostic and treatment services for two or more unrelated individuals under medical staff supervision
Hospital institutions must admit or retain individuals for overnight care
Maryland Hospital and Higher Education Institution Departments, Foundations, and Other Entities of the Institution are eligible applicants
Must provide matching funds equal to the amount of financial assistance received (1:1 match)
Projects must be located in Sustainable Communities or underinvested areas
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For application instructions and more information, visit the State Revitalization Programs webpage.

structured_extraction.program_name: Shelter and Transitional Housing Facilities Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants to improve, create, or acquire transitional housing and emergency shelters that serve homeless or at-risk households and individuals. The program aims to reduce homelessness in Maryland by providing capital financing for emergency shelters and transitional housing facilities that provide housing and support services to prevent homelessness and assist households to live independently.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants for new construction, acquisition, rehabilitation of housing, and purchase of capital equipment for transitional housing and emergency shelters with supportive services. Grant funds may cover up to 50 percent of total project costs, or up to 75 percent under certain conditions. Eligible project activities include: cost of acquiring land and buildings; necessary studies, surveys, plans, specifications, appraisals, compaction tests, test borings, construction cost estimates and environmental impact reports; site preparation; cost of labor and materials for construction, rehabilitation, and installation of improvements; acquisition of necessary machinery, equipment, and furnishings installed at the project; and fees and premiums normally incurred in real estate development including indemnity and surety bonds, hazard and liability insurance during construction. Recipients must maintain the project as transitional housing or emergency shelter for 15 years; if use is discontinued earlier, the grant must be repaid. Program funds may not be used for refinancing existing debt, financing costs of building portions that do not provide homeless housing, financial transaction costs associated with tax credit syndication, replacing furnishings in existing facilities, or providing operating assistance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations with 501(c)(3) tax-exempt status and local governments seeking to create or improve transitional housing or emergency shelters for homeless and at-risk individuals and families
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: New construction, acquisition, rehabilitation of housing, and purchase of capital equipment for transitional housing facilities and emergency shelters that provide supportive services. Eligible uses include: real property acquisition; architectural and engineering services; construction (additions, alterations, conversions, relocations, renovations, replacements, restorations); site development and improvements; utilities; and equipment and furnishings with a life expectancy of at least 15 years that are of durable construction, not elaborate or extravagant, and necessary to accommodate the functions for which the structure is intended.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. All projects involving new construction must be located in a Priority Funding Area (PFA), which includes all incorporated municipalities (including Baltimore City with some exceptions), all areas between the Baltimore beltway and Baltimore City limits and the Washington DC beltway and DC boundary, all areas designated as Sustainable Communities, Federal and State enterprise zones, all areas designated by county governments as PFAs (including rural villages designated in county comprehensive plans as of July 1, 1998), and certified heritage areas within locally designated growth areas. Local government letters of support are required for all projects, and a letter from local government certifying PFA location is required for projects involving new construction.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization or local government

Housing must serve homeless or at-risk households and individuals (homeless defined as a household without permanent housing and lacking resources to obtain permanent housing, in imminent danger of homelessness)

Project must include supportive services for residents that are specifically oriented to meeting the needs of the homeless target population; service providers must be identified and commitment letters, agreements or other documents identifying funding sources for services must be submitted

Applicants must identify the homeless target population they expect to serve (e.g., families, women and children, single males, victims of domestic violence) and continue serving the designated population throughout the 15-year funding term
Recipient must agree to maintain the project as transitional housing or emergency shelter for 15 years
If use is discontinued before 15 years, the grant becomes repayable
Local government letter of support is required for all projects
A letter from local government certifying the project is located in a Priority Funding Area (PFA) is required for projects involving new construction
Project must comply with Maryland Historical Trust requirements; the Trust must complete its review and issue a letter of no objection before funds are disbursed
Any roof purchased with State funds must have at least a 20-year, no-dollar-limit warranty; for new construction, proper roofing system must be determined based on 60-year life cycle cost analysis
Projects involving new construction or substantial rehabilitation are subject to thorough review of all construction-related items by the Department's Construction Management staff
Minority Business Enterprises (MBEs) participation is strongly encouraged with a State goal of at least 29% certified MBE participation
Applicants must use Maryland resident businesses where possible (businesses with Maryland address, registered to do business in State, employing Maryland residents)
LEED green building technologies are encouraged
All contractors must be checked against the debarment list; no State funds may be spent on debarred or suspended individuals or firms
Project must comply with Forest Conservation Program requirements if construction activities occur on land greater than 40,000 square feet
Funds may not be used for sectarian religious instruction or sectarian religious buildings or programs; Affidavit Not to Use Funds for Religious Purposes may be required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application with required forms (Forms 212 and 215 for cost estimates), local government letter of support, and letter from local government certifying PFA location (for new construction projects) to Housing Development Programs at the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development. Applications must include a complete description of supportive services to be offered and a plan outlining funding sources for services and operating expenses during the project term. The Department will review applications for threshold requirements and may request assistance from the Maryland Department of Human Resources' Office of Transitional Services or the Department of Health Office of Health Care Quality to review the adequacy of proposed supportive services. The Department will evaluate applicant's experience in operating facilities for the homeless and previous success in providing services. Processing time and underwriting procedures are described in the program guidelines.

structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program designed to preserve and improve single-family properties by bringing them up to applicable building codes and standards or a minimum housing quality standard. Funds may be used to address critical health and safety issues including mold remediation, roof repairs, lead abatement, electrical hazards, plumbing issues, structural repairs, and other critical infrastructure repairs.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Zero to six percent interest loans with terms up to 30 years. Generally, the maximum loan is $50,000. Loans are secured by a mortgage if the loan exceeds $5,000 or has deferred payments. Loans that serve families with incomes at or below 50 percent of the statewide or Washington, D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income may have fully deferred payments if necessary for project feasibility. Interest rates range from 0% to 6% based on the applicant's ability to pay.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owner-occupants of single-family homes with low to moderate household incomes seeking to address critical health and safety repairs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rehabilitation of owner-occupied single-family homes to address critical health and safety issues including but not limited to: mold remediation, gas leaks, roof repair and replacement, asbestos and lead abatement, chimney repair, foundation waterproofing, radon mitigation, electrical hazards and upgrades, plumbing issues, water and well repairs, septic and sewer work, window and door repairs for water intrusion or security, structural repairs, accessibility modifications for disabled and seniors, fall prevention measures, ductwork upgrades, building shell stabilization, and pest treatments.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Generally not available in Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Harford County, Howard County, Prince George's County, or Montgomery County. Available in other Maryland jurisdictions. All properties must be within the applicant's local jurisdiction.
requirements_list: Household income of owner-occupants cannot exceed 80 percent of the statewide or Washington, D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income (50 percent for deferred payment eligibility)
Property must be an owner-occupied single-family home
Property must be the applicant's primary residence
Property must be within the applicant's local jurisdiction
Property title must include the applicant(s)
Applicant must provide proof of homeownership including deed and current mortgage statement
Applicant must provide a bid from a licensed Maryland contractor identifying critical repairs not to exceed $50,000
Contractor must provide current MHIC or trade license, Certificate of Liability Insurance with per occurrence limits of at least $1 million, Letter of Good Standing, and completed W-9 form
Bid should not be more than 60 days old
Applicant must provide documentation of critical repairs including photographs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Complete the Maryland Home Rehabilitation Program application form. 2. Gather required documentation including proof of homeownership, income verification (paystubs, tax returns, bank statements, award letters), property tax bill, homeowners insurance declaration page, and photo ID. 3. Obtain bids from licensed Maryland contractors with detailed scope of work and photographs documenting critical repairs. 4. Ensure contractor provides current license, Certificate of Liability Insurance, Letter of Good Standing, and W-9 form. 5. Submit completed application with all supporting documentation via email to DHCD.SLP_documentation@maryland.gov or mail to Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, CDA, Special Loan Programs, 7800 Harkins Road, 3rd Floor, Lanham, MD 20706. 6. All loan requests will be processed directly by local governments for properties within their jurisdiction.

structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.program_description: The Strategic Demolition Fund seeks to catalyze activities that accelerate economic development and job production in existing Maryland communities. The fund aims to improve the economic viability of existing communities through strategic demolition and related activities.

The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's Sustainable Communities Program provides a specific geographic designation to local areas to support community development, revitalization, and sustainability through coordinated strategies. It gives local governments resources to improve older communities and promote growth that is environmentally, economically, and socially responsible. The program combines resources for historic preservation, housing, and economic development under a single designation, focusing on infrastructure improvements, multimodal transportation, and development that strengthens existing communities.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a geographic designation that makes communities eligible for certain state programs and resources. Once approved, the Sustainable Communities designation is valid for five years. The designation qualifies applicants for funding through related programs including Community Legacy, Neighborhood BusinessWorks, Strategic Demolition Fund, Operating Assistance Grants, National Capital Strategic Economic Development Fund, Seed Community Development Anchor Institution Program, Main Street Maryland Program, Baltimore Regional Neighborhood Initiative (BRNI), Maryland Façade Improvement Program (MFIP), Job Creation Tax Credit (enhanced from $3,000 to $5,000 per job and reduced job creation threshold from 60 to 25 jobs), Low Income Housing Tax Credit (LIHTC), Enhanced Local Tax Increment Financing (TIF) Authority, Sustainable Maryland Certified program, Water Quality Financing Administration Programs, State Highway Administration (SHA) programs, Sidewalk Retrofit Program, and Kim Lamphier Bikeways Network Program. Designated communities also receive access to a revitalization toolbox created by various state agencies showing how agencies prioritize investment in Sustainable Communities.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing; new designations valid for five years upon approval.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments (municipal or county) seeking to designate and revitalize communities through coordinated state investment and sustainable development practices.

structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All proposed communities must be entirely within a Priority Funding Area and must be within or near a town center or transportation center. Proposed community must be within or near a town center or transportation center

Must demonstrate financial need for local revitalization including support for nonprofit organizations, strengthening older commercial districts and residential communities, and improving public amenities
Must include a defined geographic area with existing built environment that needs revitalization or additional state investment
Must include a Sustainable Community Action Plan summarizing key initiatives and projects
Must provide a local government resolution supporting both the boundary designation and Action Plan
For new designations, a meeting with program staff is required before applying
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Request an application template by emailing Tynan Stevenson at tynan.stevenson@maryland.gov with subject line 'Sustainable Communities [New Designation or Renewal] Application – [Community Name] - [Sponsoring Jurisdiction]'. For new designations, a meeting with program staff is required before applying. Step 2: Submit application including defined geographic area, Sustainable Community Action Plan, and local government resolution. Step 3: An interagency panel led by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development reviews the application. Step 4: The panel presents the application to the Governor's Smart Growth Subcabinet for final approval. Step 5: Upon approval, the designation is valid for five years. Step 6: Communities seeking Baltimore Regional Neighborhood Initiative (BRNI) designation must submit a separate revitalization plan to become eligible for additional funding.

structured_extraction.program_name: UPLIFT (Utilizing Progressive Lending Investments to Finance Transformation)
structured_extraction.program_description: A homeownership production program that increases property values and provides wealth-building homeownership opportunities for targeted households by accelerating the pace of development, construction, and sale of quality affordable housing in low-income census tracts and designated Sustainable Communities. The program helps close the appraisal gap—the difference between the cost to develop a property and what it can sell for on the market—which is common in neighborhoods affected by redlining and disinvestment.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The State covers the difference between the cost to build and the sale price (the appraisal gap) through UPLIFT funding via a soft promissory note with the Department. Selected qualified development teams acquire, develop, build, and sell quality affordable housing in targeted neighborhoods using a combination of public and private financing. Homebuyers acquire fee simple title using down payment, down payment assistance, first mortgage loan (Maryland Mortgage Program or other source), and the Department's soft promissory note. Development loans are provided to builders/developers for the construction phase. A $1,000 non-refundable application fee is required per project. Additional fees include a 1% origination fee of the loan amount (paid at initial closing).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications are accepted on a rolling basis as long as funding is available
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit and for-profit developers and builders, local jurisdictions, community-based organizations, and public housing authorities engaged in revitalization efforts seeking to develop and sell quality affordable housing in targeted low-income neighborhoods.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition, development, construction, and sale of quality affordable housing in low-income census tracts and designated Sustainable Communities. Funding covers the appraisal gap (difference between development cost and market sale price) to make housing development financially feasible in historically redlined and disinvested communities. Projects must involve new construction or substantial rehabilitation of vacant structures.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in low-income census tracts (where 50% of households have incomes below 60% Area Median Income or poverty rate is 25% or more) AND designated as Maryland Sustainable Communities. New construction projects cannot be located in FEMA Flood Zone A or AE areas. Projects in Zone C, Zone X, or within 100-year or 500-year floodplains may request waivers with appropriate documentation or flood mitigation plans. Applicants should consult the UPLIFT Qualified Areas Map to determine eligibility.
requirements_list: Projects must be located in both a low-income census tract and a designated Sustainable Community
Projects must consist of newly constructed or substantially rehabilitated (formerly vacant) structures
Development team must have relevant experience as significant participants in comparably-scaled projects
All development team members (developer, builder, architect, neighborhood engagement facilitator, marketing/sales entity) must demonstrate required experience
Development team must meet acceptable credit history and current financial capacity requirements
Applicants must attend and complete a pre-application meeting before submitting formal application
Projects must meet design and construction standards set by DHCD
Projects must comply with cost limits for new construction or rehabilitation
Site must have proper control documentation
Environmental assessment required identifying hazardous materials and site conditions
Projects must include neighborhood engagement and affirmative fair housing marketing plan
Developer fees must comply with formula-based limits
A $1,000 non-refundable application fee required per project
Applications must be submitted with two complete copies (one hard copy, one electronic)
All required exhibits and documentation must be included and meet specified criteria
Due diligence reports must be current (typically less than 12 months old)
Projects must demonstrate readiness to proceed with adequate financing commitments
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 0: Review the UPLIFT Program Guide and compile project details, timelines, plans, and logistics. Schedule and complete a Pre-Application Meeting and submit required pre-application materials at least two business days before scheduled meeting date. Step 1: After pre-application meeting, complete the UPLIFT Electronic Application Submission Request Form. Upon DHCD internal review, receive access to a private Dropbox folder for application submission. Step 2: Download the Application Documents Package from the UPLIFT website. Step 3: Complete all application sections (Parts 1-7) including narratives, certifications, development information, and financials using the provided Excel forms and Word documents. Prepare two copies of complete application: one electronic (via Dropbox) and one hard copy. Step 4: Pay the $1,000 non-refundable application fee by ACH or check and include proof of payment. Mail check to Accounts Receivable or use provided ACH information. Step 5: Upload all electronic files to Dropbox in correct subfolders. Complete and submit the Final Submission Checklist. Deliver hard copy to DHCD Operations & Administration Office at 7800 Harkins Road, Lanham, MD 20706. Step 6: DHCD conducts threshold review to verify compliance with all threshold criteria and material completeness. Applications that are materially incomplete will not be evaluated. Step 7: Applications passing threshold review are scored against evaluative criteria in five areas: Development Team Capacity, Project Impact, Leveraging Resources, Readiness to Proceed, and Development Quality. Step 8: UPLIFT Loan Committee reviews and recommends eligible projects to the Secretary of DHCD for approval. Step 9: If approved, applicants receive a commitment letter. Step 10: Project enters underwriting pipeline with Project Kick-off Meeting generally held 45-60 days after complete application submission. Step 11: Prepare Final Underwriting Submission (FUS) updating all financing, design, construction, and marketing elements. Step 12: Upon underwriting approval, Secretary authorizes commitment and investment of resources. Step 13: Initial financing closing occurs with Attorney General's office review and closing checklist completion. Step 14: Construction Kick-off Meeting held to coordinate construction, marketing, and occupancy requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's largest residential energy conservation program that assists income-eligible homeowners and renters by reducing heating and cooling costs through energy-conservation measures while addressing health and safety issues in their homes.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides free energy conservation services to eligible households through local weatherization agencies. Services include comprehensive home energy audits and improvements such as blower door air infiltration reduction, insulation in attics/floors/walls, hot water system improvements, lighting retrofits, furnace cleaning/tune-ups, safety repairs, burner retrofits or replacements, and health and safety repairs. Services are delivered at no cost to eligible participants. Work follows the Standard Work Specifications (SWS) aligned Maryland Field Guide and includes quality control inspections on 100% of completed units. For the 2024-2025 program year, the average cost per unit is approximately $7,496 for DOE Formula Funds and $6,000 for Bipartisan Infrastructure Law (BIL) funds. Program also offers emergency heating and cooling system repairs/replacements (MEAP), maintenance and education services (MEET), and health and safety improvements.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Income-eligible homeowners and renters in Maryland. Priority given to households with members over age 60, people with disabilities, households with children, households with high energy usage, and households with high energy burden.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy conservation improvements including air infiltration reduction, insulation, hot water system upgrades, lighting retrofits, furnace repairs and replacements, health and safety repairs, HVAC system replacements, and water heater replacements. Funding can also support emergency heating/cooling repairs and maintenance services for previously weatherized homes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide through local weatherization agencies serving each territory. Local Weatherization Agencies serve the following counties and regions: Allegany County (Allegany County HRDC), Anne Arundel, Baltimore County and Baltimore City (Baltimore Community Action Council of Howard County or Baltimore City DHCD), Calvert, Caroline, Carroll, Cecil, Charles (Housing Authority of St. Mary's County), Dorchester (Shore Up!), Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Howard, Kent, Montgomery, Prince George's (Housing Authority of St. Mary's County), Queen Anne's, Somerset, St. Mary's, Talbot, Washington, Wicomico, and Worcester. Some geographical areas have certain eligibility restrictions.
requirements_list: Household income at or below 60% of State Median Income (SMI) or 200% of Federal Poverty Level (FPL)
Applicants currently receiving benefits from Utility Bill Pay Assistance, SNAP, TANF, SSI, or HUD housing assistance programs automatically qualify as income-eligible
Application must be submitted to local weatherization agency serving the service area
Dwelling must be in condition suitable for energy improvements
Primary residence must be owner-occupied or rental property where owner consents to weatherization
Homeowners and renters must meet income eligibility requirements
Households must apply through designated Local Weatherization Agency (LWA)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Contact your Local Weatherization Agency (LWA) serving your county or area to submit an application. 2. Complete application and income verification process. 3. LWA staff will determine eligibility based on income and other factors. 4. If eligible, LWA will schedule a comprehensive energy audit of your home. 5. Energy auditor will assess the home and identify cost-effective energy improvements. 6. If home qualifies, LWA will develop a work plan for approved energy improvements. 7. LWA will schedule and complete approved weatherization work. 8. Quality control inspection will be performed on 100% of completed work. 9. Occupant education will be provided on installed measures and energy-saving behaviors. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis as funding is available. Wait lists may be used when demand exceeds available funds.

structured_extraction.program_description: This grant provides funds for National School Lunch Program operators to purchase equipment to serve healthier school meals, improve food safety, and expand access to school meals. structured_extraction.assistance_description: Funds to purchase equipment (new, renovated, or replacement) valued at greater than $1,000 per item to support school food service operations. Priority given to high-needs schools where 50 percent or more of enrolled students are eligible for free or reduced-price meals, schools with opportunities for meaningful nutrition impacts, schools with aging food service equipment, and schools that have not previously received an NSLP Equipment Grant. The 2022 total funding available is $954,126. Grant operates in two phases: Phase 1 (October 1, 2022 through June 30, 2024) and Phase 2 reallocation (July 1, 2024 through September 30, 2024). Awards are made within 30 days of the application deadline.

structured_extraction.program_name: Accreditation Support Fund – Maryland Program Accreditation
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides financial assistance to licensed child care centers and school-age only programs to help cover the cost of non-consumable learning materials needed to pursue Maryland Program Accreditation. Support funds are available to child care programs seeking to obtain or maintain Maryland Accreditation through the Maryland EXCELS quality rating and improvement system.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides grants/subsidies to reimburse child care centers and school-age only programs for non-consumable learning materials purchased in pursuit of Maryland Program Accreditation. Maximum reimbursement is $2,500 per accreditation cycle for programs serving 100 or fewer children, or $3,000 per accreditation cycle for programs serving more than 100 children. Eligible materials include curricula, classroom technology, outdoor play equipment, science and sensory materials, books, and literacy activities. Funds cannot be used for accreditation fees, facility improvements, association membership fees, staff training, costs paid through another funding source, or costs exceeding the fee charged by the accreditation organization. Reimbursement covers items purchased within 12 months before the application date.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed child care centers and school-age only programs seeking to pursue, obtain, or maintain Maryland Program Accreditation
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Non-consumable learning materials including curricula, classroom technology, outdoor play equipment, science and sensory materials, books, and literacy activities purchased in pursuit of accreditation. Cannot be used for accreditation fees, facility improvements, association membership fees, staff training, costs paid through other funding sources, or fees exceeding the accreditation organization's charge.

Must be currently Maryland Accredited or have completed the Initial Self-Appraisal as part of the Maryland Accreditation process
Purchases must be non-consumable learning materials
Purchases must be from within 12 months before the application date

Approvals and requests for further information are sent through the Maryland Onestop portal.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: The fund covers required application fees for national accreditation from MSDE-recognized accrediting organizations, including initial application fees, renewal application fees, and annual update fees charged by the accrediting organization. Recognized accrediting organizations include: American Montessori Society (AMS), Association Montessori International/USA (AMI/USA), Association of Independent Maryland Schools (AIMS), Association of Waldorf Schools of North America (AWSNA), Cognia Early Learning Accreditation, Council on Accreditation – After-School Accreditation (COA/ASA), Lumen Accreditation, Maryland Accreditation (MSDE), Middle States Association of Colleges and Schools Commission on Elementary and Secondary Schools (MSA-CESS), National Accreditation Commission (NAC), National Association for the Education of Young Children (NAEYC), National Association for Family Child Care (NAFCC), and National Early Childhood Program Accreditation (NECPA). Awards are paid directly to the accrediting organization on behalf of the applicant. Funds cannot exceed the fee charged by the accreditation organization and cannot be used for facility improvements, association membership fees, staff training, or costs already covered by other funding sources.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program that provides financial reimbursement to help schools and organizations serve nutritious snacks or suppers to children in afterschool care programs. The program operates under either the National School Lunch Program (NSLP) or the Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP). The NSLP Afterschool Snack Service is a federally-assisted snack service that provides cash reimbursement to encourage schools in serving snacks to children after the regular school day. The afterschool snack component helps children fully engage in afterschool programming by filling the hunger gap many children face in the afternoon and early evening.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The USDA provides financial reimbursement to school districts, non-profit organizations, and school-based programs for serving snacks or suppers to children in afterschool care settings. Afterschool snacks are available through the NSLP for participating school districts. Afterschool meals (snacks and/or suppers) are available through CACFP for school-based, non-profit, and non-school-based organizations that are area-eligible. Reimbursement is provided on a per-meal basis for snacks meeting USDA nutritional standards. Children participating in an approved afterschool care program age 18 and under, and participating children who turn 19 during the school year, are eligible to receive reimbursable snacks through the NSLP.
structured_extraction.program_audience: School districts participating in the NSLP, non-profit organizations, and school-based or non-school-based organizations offering afterschool care programs that provide educational or enrichment activities in a supervised environment. Children age 18 and under participating in approved afterschool care programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Financial reimbursement for serving healthy snacks or suppers to children in afterschool care programs. Snacks must meet USDA NSLP Afterschool Snack or CACFP meal pattern requirements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Programs must be area-eligible to participate in the Child and Adult Care Food Program component. Statewide availability through Maryland public schools for NSLP component. The SFA (School Food Authority) must participate in the NSLP lunch component in order for a site operated by the SFA to operate the NSLP Afterschool Snack Service.
requirements_list: School districts must be participating in the National School Lunch Program (NSLP)
The SFA (School Food Authority) must participate in the NSLP lunch component
Afterschool programs must provide educational or enrichment activities in a supervised environment
For NSLP component: site must sponsor or operate an approved afterschool care program
For CACFP component: programs must be area-eligible
For CACFP component: meals must meet USDA CACFP Meal Patterns
Afterschool care program must primarily provide care for children after school
Program must have organized, regularly scheduled activities in a structured and supervised environment
Eligible education or enrichment activities include homework assistance, tutoring, supervised drop-in athletic programs, extended day programs, drama activities, and arts and crafts programs
Organized interscholastic programs or community-level competitive sports are not eligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: School districts and organizations should contact their local school system or the Maryland State Department of Education for information on how to participate in the program. The SFA must work with state agencies to establish participation agreements. State agencies administer the program through agreements with local school food authorities. Refer to USDA Food and Nutrition Service resources and state guidelines for specific application procedures and requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: Registered apprenticeship program offering students paid opportunities to join the workforce while in school through on-the-job training and related technical instruction, aligned with industry credentials.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: 450 hours of paid on-the-job training and 144 hours of related technical instruction. Apprenticeship placements and schedules are set by the employer and student and can occur during the school day, after school, over the summer, or on weekends. Approved by the Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Council and delivered in partnership with local school districts.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students seeking paid workforce experience while in school, and adult apprentices pursuing career development.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Paid on-the-job training and related technical instruction in registered apprenticeship positions across various industries.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland through local school districts.
requirements_list: Approved by the Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Council
Delivered in partnership with local school districts
Must be registered apprenticeship position
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Students and families should talk to their school's apprenticeship or career-connected learning coordinator to explore opportunities, eligibility, and scheduling. The coordinator will help match students with employers based on career interests and availability. Employers can partner with a Maryland Department of Labor Navigator to learn how to register positions and host student apprentices.

structured_extraction.program_description: DORS Rehabilitation Technology Services provides customized assessments and training to help people with disabilities find and use assistive technology (AT) to support their employment and educational goals. Assistive technology may include video magnifiers, note-taking devices, specialized software like voice recognition and screen readers, and mobile devices for organization. Training classes cover software like JAWS screen reading and ZoomText magnification.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: DORS RTS staff provides customized assessments to identify appropriate assistive technology for individuals with disabilities pursuing employment or educational goals. The program offers training and technical support on AT hardware and software use, including desktop or portable video magnifiers, note-taking devices, voice recognition software, screen readers, and mobile devices for organization and time management. Assessments and training are available at the Workforce Technology Center (WTC) in Baltimore or in the individual's community.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Job seekers and students with disabilities who are DORS consumers with an employment or educational goal.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Assessment and training for assistive technology devices and software to improve employment and educational capabilities.
requirements_list: Must be a DORS consumer with an employment or educational goal.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your DORS Counselor or local office to request a customized AT assessment. Assessments and training can be arranged at the Workforce Technology Center (WTC) campus in Baltimore or in the individual's community.

structured_extraction.program_description: A 16-week training course that prepares job seekers with disabilities to work in the automotive industry as entry-level General Service Technicians. The program covers vehicle diagnosis and repair, inspection, tire and lubrication services, and uses state-of-the-art equipment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides 16 weeks of training in automotive general service technician skills at the DORS Workforce & Technology Center campus in Baltimore. Training includes customer service, shop safety, automotive maintenance and repair, and hands-on experience with equipment such as tire balancing machines, 4-wheel alignment systems, lifts, and hand tools. The program covers lubrication and fluid changes, tire changing and balancing, battery and starting system testing and charging, battery replacement, tune-ups, vehicle inspections, and brake repair.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Job seekers with disabilities who want to work as entry-level automotive general service technicians.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The program provides training in automotive general service technician skills, including lubrication and fluid changes, tire changing and balancing, battery and starting system testing and charging, battery replacement, tune-ups, vehicle inspections, and brake repair.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is provided at the DORS Workforce & Technology Center campus in Baltimore.
requirements_list: Valid driver's license with no more than 2 points
Ability to lift 50 pounds
Ability to squat, stoop, and kneel
3rd grade reading level and basic math skills
No disqualifying criminal background
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your DORS Counselor or local office for more information or request DORS Services.

structured_extraction.program_description: A free online course required by the Maryland State Department of Education for all child care providers. The course covers essential health and safety information needed for child care providers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides free online self-paced training course required by the Maryland State Department of Education for all child care providers. The Office of Early Learning and Instruction supports confirmation of registrants and provides troubleshooting support.
structured_extraction.program_audience: All child care providers in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Health and safety training for child care providers
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide program required for all child care providers in Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a child care provider in Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Child care providers register online for the self-paced course. The Office of Early Learning and Instruction confirms registrations and provides troubleshooting support as needed.

structured_extraction.program_name: Broadening Options and Opportunities for Students Today (BOOST) Scholarship Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The BOOST Scholarship Program provides scholarship awards to help eligible students attend participating nonpublic schools. Students must qualify for free or reduced-price school meals and be accepted to a participating nonpublic school.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Scholarship awards are provided in the form of checks sent to the participating nonpublic school. Award amounts depend on household income, academic level of the student, school-provided financial assistance, and available funding. The scholarship amount is capped at the student's tuition owed after accounting for school discounts. Award amounts are determined by the BOOST Advisory Board in summer for the upcoming school year. For the 2026-2027 school year, approximately $9,000,000 in funding is available (plus carry-over from prior year) to provide an estimated 2,500 scholarship awards. The scholarship check is sent to the school, and the parent/guardian must come to the school to endorse the back of the check. Funds can only be used for tuition and required fees for enrollment; they cannot be used for transportation or meals. If the scholarship award exceeds the tuition owed to the school (after accounting for school discounts), the award will be reduced to match the tuition owed. Individual awards cannot be split or transferred to other students.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Parent applications: March 9 - May 8, 2026; Nonpublic school applications: March 6, 2026
structured_extraction.contact_name: Allison Sanborn, BOOST Program Manager; James Clark, Administrative Support
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students in kindergarten through 12th grade whose families qualify for free or reduced-price school meals and who are accepted to participating nonpublic schools in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Scholarship funds are used to help pay tuition and required fees at participating nonpublic schools. Funds must be deposited by the school and applied to the student's tuition account and cannot be used for transportation or meals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is available statewide in Maryland for students attending eligible participating nonpublic schools. Participating nonpublic schools are located in 19 jurisdictions across Maryland.
requirements_list: Student must qualify for free and reduced-price meals (FARMs) based on household income and size
Student must be enrolled or accepted at a participating nonpublic school for the 2026-2027 school year
Student must be entering grades kindergarten through 12th grade (pre-K students are not eligible)
The nonpublic school must hold a certificate of approval from or be registered with the State Board of Education
The nonpublic school must be approved to participate in the Nonpublic Textbook Program
The nonpublic school must provide more than only pre-K and K programs (at least a 1st grade full-day education)
Parents must submit the online BOOST Scholarship application through Submittable and upload their 2025 Federal 1040 tax returns for income verification
Child's full name as it appears on birth certificate must be provided
Information on current school enrollment and nonpublic school intended for 2026-2027 enrollment must be provided
Information on whether child has learning disability and receives special education services must be disclosed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Parents complete the online BOOST Scholarship application through Submittable between March 9 and May 8, 2026, and upload their 2025 Federal 1040 tax returns for income verification. Applications are reviewed for eligibility and completeness on a rolling basis. Applications are ranked by priority and as a percentage of the federal poverty index. Priority rankings are: (1) Students who received a BOOST award during 2025-2026 school year and their siblings; (2) New applicants from public schools qualifying for free meals; (3) New applicants from public schools qualifying for reduced-price meals; (4) Applicants currently at nonpublic schools qualifying for free meals; (5) Applicants currently at nonpublic schools qualifying for reduced-price meals. After May 30, 2026, all application data is shared with the BOOST Advisory Board. The BOOST Advisory Board convenes in summer 2026 to determine award amounts based on available funding, total applicants, and priority status. Award notifications are sent via email to parents/guardians by August 2026, and parents must accept or decline by the deadline stated in their notification. Participating schools must confirm student enrollment and submit special education documentation if applicable. Scholarship checks are mailed to schools between September and December 2026. As parents decline awards, funds become available and are offered to the next eligible applicants. No new awards are offered after December 11, 2026. Parents may attend customer service support sessions on March 10, March 12 (with Spanish interpreter), and weekly Wednesdays from March 18 through May 6, 2026 from 12-1 pm.

structured_extraction.program_description: A partnership with CVS Health and Community College of Baltimore County that prepares job seekers with disabilities to become Certified Pharmacy Technicians by providing classroom instruction, mock pharmacy practice, and on-the-job externships in CVS pharmacies. Participants are prepared to take the national Pharmacy Technician Certifying Board (PTCB) test.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides 14 weeks of classroom instruction held at the DORS WTC location, followed by 6 weeks of clinical on-the-job training in CVS pharmacies located in the participant's local community. Training covers CVS programs and procedures, inventory management, and prescription medication measurements. The program prepares participants to take the national Pharmacy Technician Certifying Board (PTCB) test to become Certified Pharmacy Technicians. There is no tuition cost to participants.
structured_extraction.contact_email: DORS Counselor or local DORS office
structured_extraction.program_audience: Job seekers with disabilities who are at least 18 years old and interested in becoming Certified Pharmacy Technicians. Pharmacy Technicians assist pharmacists in hospitals or retail pharmacies, serving customers, processing insurance claims, maintaining inventory, and filling prescriptions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and certification preparation for pharmacy technician positions, including classroom instruction and on-the-job clinical training.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland. Externships occur in CVS pharmacies located in the participant's local community.
requirements_list: Be 18 years of age and possess a high school diploma or GED
Desire to work in a retail environment with ability to provide excellent customer service to the public
Have a 9th-grade reading comprehension level and 9th-grade math skills
Be detail oriented and able to switch between tasks while working accurately and quickly
Have efficient computer, telephone, and study skills
Pass a drug screen and background check prior to program start
Able to lift up to 30 pounds and bend, stoop, and stand for long periods of time
Have close visual acuity
COVID-19 vaccination required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your DORS Counselor or local DORS office for more information or to request DORS services.

structured_extraction.program_name: Child Care Career and Professional Development Fund (CCCPDF)
structured_extraction.program_description: A program providing financial assistance to child care providers and staff for career and professional development activities and education, including scholarship funding to pursue college degrees in early childhood education, child development, elementary education, or special education. Payments for degree programs are made directly to the accredited college or university rather than reimbursed to participants.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides funding to support career and professional development activities for child care providers, including scholarship funding for associate or bachelor's degree programs in Early Childhood Education, Child Development, Elementary Education, or Special Education. Payments are made directly to accredited colleges or universities recognized by the U.S. Department of Education.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individual child care providers and staff in Maryland participating in the Maryland Child Care Credentialing Program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Career development and professional development activities and education, including college degree tuition and fees in Early Childhood Education, Child Development, Elementary Education, or Special Education at accredited institutions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide; participating institutions located throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Participant must be a child care provider or staff member
Participant must be enrolled in the Maryland Child Care Credentialing Program
Degree must be pursued at an accredited college or university recognized by the U.S. Department of Education
Degree program must be in Early Childhood Education, Child Development, Elementary Education, or Special Education
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants work with participating institutions (marked with an asterisk in the program listings) to apply for scholarship funding. MSDE will notify applicants of fund approval status. See also: http://earlychildhood.marylandpublicschools.org/degree-programs

structured_extraction.program_description: A 16-week training course in partnership with the Community College of Baltimore County that prepares job seekers with disabilities for certification to work as childcare providers. The program combines classroom instruction with a nine-week internship at a licensed childcare facility. Internships are offered at select locations throughout the state.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A 16-week training course including classroom instruction at DORS' WTC campus in Northeast Baltimore and a nine-week community-based internship at an approved, licensed childcare facility at select locations throughout the state. Training covers child growth and development, activity organization and management, communication skills for child care, group care of infants and toddlers, school-age child care, First Aid and CPR certification, and hands-on internship experience. The program is offered in partnership with the Community College of Baltimore County.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Job seekers with disabilities who are at least 18 years old and interested in becoming certified childcare providers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and certification in childcare provision, including classroom instruction, First Aid and CPR certification, and paid or unpaid internship experience at approved and licensed childcare facilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is offered at DORS' WTC campus in Northeast Baltimore with internships at approved and licensed childcare facilities at select locations throughout the state.
requirements_list: At least 18 years of age
Background check and health clearance
6th grade reading comprehension level and basic math skills
High school diploma, GED, or certificate
Basic computer knowledge
Ability to lift and move children up to 30 pounds or more
Ability to see details at close range
Ability to hear and give verbal instructions in noisy conditions
Ability to change from one task to another
Ability to supervise children independently
Job seeker with a disability (must be eligible for DORS services)

structured_extraction.program_name: Child Care Quality Incentive Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that provides financial incentives to licensed child care providers — including child care centers and family child care homes — to improve and enhance the quality of care and children's school readiness. The program awards funds to help providers acquire training, supplies, materials, and equipment to create stimulating learning environments for children aged zero through sixteen. The program emphasizes educational curricula and activities in literacy, math, science, social studies, physical development, arts and crafts, dramatic play, and active play. The program is governed by COMAR 13A.14.11 regulations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants awarded to eligible child care providers to purchase approved supplies, materials, and equipment that support quality improvement and children's school readiness. Eligible expenses include curriculum materials, books, educational media, computers for child care, active play equipment, arts and crafts supplies, dramatic play props, literacy materials, manipulatives, math materials, science and nature equipment, and special needs equipment for children aged zero through sixteen.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Not yet announced — program under review
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed child care centers and family child care homes operating in Maryland that implement curricula aligned with Kindergarten Readiness and Early Learning Assessment (ELA) guidelines.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of approved supplies, materials, and equipment to improve child care quality and implement knowledge gained through training and education in early childhood development. Eligible categories include: curriculum materials, books, educational media, computers for child care use, active play equipment, arts and crafts supplies, dramatic play props, literacy materials, manipulatives, math materials, science and nature equipment, and special needs equipment for children aged zero through sixteen.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide — all Maryland counties eligible.
requirements_list: Possess a current license or letter of compliance
Currently operate a child care center or family child care home
Implement a curriculum aligned with Kindergarten Readiness and Early Learning Assessment (ELA) guidelines
Meet additional specific requirements based on provider type (child care center or family child care home)
All materials must be age appropriate for children aged zero through sixteen
Expenses must enhance the quality of child care by improving children's developmental skills
MSDE-approved curriculum guides must include title, author, and publisher
Educational and resource books must include title, author, and publisher
Educational media must include title and manufacturer
Computers must be for child care use
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Application procedures and requirements are set forth in COMAR 13A.14.11 regulations. Applications will be made available through the IMPACT and Tidbits newsletter and on the MSDE website once the revised Grant Information Guide and Application process is approved. Applicants must demonstrate how approved materials will be used to implement knowledge gained through training and enhance child care quality.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program providing financial relief to child care providers to help them recover from impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Relief grant funding ranging from $2,400 to $60,000 depending on the licensed capacity of the child care facility. Grant funds must be spent by December 31, 2021. Recipients must maintain financial documentation for 5 years and may be subject to random audits. Funds are subject to offset for any state of Maryland tax debts owed, though such funds are automatically released the following day. Federal tax debts must be resolved directly with the IRS. Recipients will receive a Form 1099-G for grant amounts above $600.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed child care providers in Maryland, including non-profit and for-profit providers. Before and after school providers are eligible if they operate on March 3, 2021 and maintain their license.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To provide relief and recovery support for child care provider operations. Grant funds may be used for provider facility costs and other operational expenses to support recovery from COVID-19 impacts.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland-wide.
requirements_list: Must be a licensed child care provider in Maryland
Must be operating on March 3, 2021 and maintain license
Each facility location with its own license number requires a separate application
Provider ID required (found on inspection report)
May be randomly selected for audit requiring receipts and financial documentation
Recipients receive Form 1099-G for amounts above $600
Grant funds must be spent by December 31, 2021
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications were completed online through the relief grant webpage. Applicants entered their Provider ID, facility cost information including rent or mortgage and property taxes, and number of days closed due to COVID-19. A confirmation screen appears upon submission. Applicants can verify receipt of their application by searching for their Licensing Number in the 'Received Applications' list (Excel spreadsheet) on the relief grant webpage. Application changes could be submitted via a change form before the March 3, 2021 deadline. Grant processing began after March 3, 2021 with funds expected within 4-6 weeks of application closure.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Child Care Scholarship (CCS) Program helps eligible families in Maryland pay for high-quality child care and early education programs. Families who qualify receive scholarships (vouchers/subsidies) that cover part of their child care costs at participating Maryland EXCELS registered family homes, licensed child care centers, or through informal child care by relatives or non-relatives in the child's home. Eligible families receive a temporary 60-day scholarship while their full 52-week application is processed. The program also provides assistance to families experiencing homelessness or at risk of homelessness to ensure children have access to safe, quality child care while families work toward housing stability. Due to high demand, the program temporarily stopped issuing scholarships to new families starting May 1, 2025, though families meeting certain criteria (TANF, TCA, SSI recipients) are exempt from the freeze and can still receive scholarships immediately. Other families can still apply and be added to a waitlist. Child care providers who enroll children receiving scholarships must be Maryland EXCELS participants and use the Child Care Provider Portal to manage attendance, invoicing, and scholarship requests.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible families receive payment scholarships from the state to cover part of their child care costs. A temporary 60-day scholarship provides immediate assistance while the full application is processed; a full scholarship lasts 52 weeks (two years for new applications determined eligible). Families pay a state-assigned co-payment (ranging from $0 to $3 per week) plus any amount not covered by the scholarship. Families receiving Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) or Supplemental Security Income (SSI) have a $0 co-payment. Family co-payments decrease if families are receiving scholarships for more than one child. Families meeting homelessness or other criteria under HB 1121 may qualify for co-payment waivers. Child care providers are paid in advance based on enrollment and attendance, with payments processed by the 1st and 15th of each month. Advance payments are calculated on the last Friday of each month if providers submit all required forms at least 5 days before that date. Providers receiving direct deposit can anticipate payment from the Comptroller's Office within 7 days after payment processing completion. The state pays for up to 60 days of absences per calendar year. As of May 1, 2025, new families are subject to an enrollment freeze due to budget capacity being reached; families receiving TANF, TCA, or SSI are exempt and receive scholarships immediately upon approval. Other approved families are placed on a waitlist. Existing enrolled families continue to receive scholarships as long as they remain eligible and submit renewal forms on time. Families can add new children to existing scholarships without being subject to the freeze. Income guidelines vary by family size (Initial Income Scale for new applications and Continuation Income Scale for renewals/changes). Fast-Track scholarships are processed within 3 business days; Full Application determinations take up to 30 calendar days or 5 business days of receipt of all required documentation.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Starting May 1, 2025, the program temporarily stopped issuing scholarships to new families (enrollment freeze). Applications are still accepted; approved families are added to a waitlist. TANF/TCA/SSI recipients are exempt from the freeze. Fast-Track applications are not processed during the freeze; families must complete full applications to be determined eligible for the frozen status list.
structured_extraction.contact_phone: 877-227-0125 (press 3 for families; office hours 8:00 am – 5:00 pm); After-hours: 855-435-7410 (Tue–Thu 5–9 pm, Sat 9 am–12 pm)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible families in Maryland with children under age 13 (or ages 13–19 with a qualifying disability) who are working, in an approved training program, or attending school, and need help paying for child care. Also includes families receiving TCA or SSI, families referred by Head Start, and families experiencing or at risk of homelessness. Licensed child care centers, letter of compliance facilities, military centers, registered family child care providers, and informal child care providers who wish to enroll children whose families receive Child Care Scholarships.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Payment for child care and early education services at participating Maryland EXCELS registered family homes, licensed child care centers, informal child care by relatives or non-relatives in the child's home, and before and after school child care programs. Funds support children ages birth to 12 or ages 13-19 with qualifying disabilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Applicants must be Maryland residents.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident who is working/employed, in an approved training program, or attending school. For families where both parents live in the same household, both parents must meet all eligibility requirements.
Must be a recipient of Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) or Supplemental Security Income (SSI), or have family income within CCS income guidelines (varies by family size).
Child must be under age 13, or ages 13–19 with a qualifying disability.
Child must be a U.S. citizen or qualified alien (birth certificate or citizenship documentation required). Parents are not required to be U.S. citizens.
Willing to have child immunized to Maryland state standards or provide documentation supporting exemption from immunization.
Must provide proof of identity for all household members; head of household must provide a Photo ID.
Must provide proof of residency (utility bill, lease, etc.).
Must provide proof of income (most recent four weeks of consecutive pay stubs and all other household income).
Must provide proof of approved activity (employment, school, or job training enrollment).
Families experiencing homelessness must meet income and eligibility requirements and may apply with a homelessness application coversheet.
Some applicants require referral from DHS/MORA, Head Start, or other approved agencies.
Families may be eligible for co-payment waivers under HB 1121 if experiencing homelessness or meeting other specified criteria.
Families receiving TANF, TCA, or SSI are exempt from the May 1, 2025 enrollment freeze and can receive scholarships immediately upon approval.
During the enrollment freeze, approved families (not exempt) are added to a waitlist.
Existing enrolled families must submit renewal forms on time to continue receiving scholarships.
Families can add new children to existing scholarships without being subject to the freeze.

Child care providers must be Maryland EXCELS participants, register and use the Child Care Provider Portal, track and submit accurate attendance records, submit invoices through the portal for reimbursement, and comply with licensing or letter of compliance requirements.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Families apply online through the Child Care Scholarship Family Portal at https://family.childcareportals.org. Step 1: Register and create an account on the portal. Step 2: Complete the Fast-Track application and submit three documents: proof of employment/training/school enrollment, proof of residency, and proof of income (most recent 4 weeks of consecutive pay stubs). Step 3: Application is processed within three business days by CCS Central 2. Step 4: If eligible, a temporary 60-day scholarship is issued (or families are added to a waitlist if the enrollment freeze applies). Note: During the enrollment freeze (as of May 1, 2025), Fast-Track applications will not be processed; families must complete the full application instead. Step 5: To receive a full 52-week scholarship, submit additional documentation within 15 days of fast-track approval. The full application includes all household member information, detailed income documentation, proof of citizenship for each child, and other supporting documents. Full Application determinations take up to 30 calendar days from submission date or within 5 business days of receipt of all required documentation. Step 6: At redetermination, 45 days before the end of current eligibility period, submit a Redetermination Application with all required updated documents. Families receiving TANF, TCA, or SSI who are approved receive scholarships immediately (exempt from freeze). Redetermination Applications must be submitted at least 15 days before the current scholarship end date to allow processing time and avoid payment breaks to providers. For questions, complete an inquiry form at money4childcare.com or call CCS Central 2 at 877-227-0125 (press 3) during office hours (8:00 am – 5:00 pm) or after-hours support at 855-435-7410 (Tue–Thu 5–9 pm, Sat 9 am–12 pm). Open Office Hours with CCS Central 2 are held monthly from 12:00 to 1:00 PM on dates posted at money4childcare.com. Child care providers must become Maryland EXCELS participants, then register with the Child Care Provider Portal at https://provider.childcareportals.org to accept scholarship requests, track attendance, submit monthly invoices, and manage payments.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program designed to ensure quality of professional development offered to child care professionals in Maryland. The program approves individuals and organizations that meet requirements, provides technical assistance to applicants and approved trainers, and oversees statewide review, approval, renewal, and monitoring of trainers and training proposals for birth through age 8 education covering Core of Knowledge, Pre-Service, and Continued training.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides approval and oversight of professional development training for child care professionals. Approved trainers can offer training to child care staff. Technical assistance is provided to applicants and approved trainers. Quarterly trainer meetings are facilitated.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care professionals, trainers, and organizations offering professional development in early childhood education
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and professional development for child care professionals in Maryland
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide program serving all of Maryland
requirements_list: Applicants must meet requirements identified in COMAR 13A.14.08
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals and organizations apply for approval in accordance with COMAR 13A.14.08 requirements. The Office of Early Learning and Instruction leads the statewide review, approval, renewal, and monitoring process.

structured_extraction.program_name: Child Care and Development Fund (CCDF – Federal Block Grant)
structured_extraction.program_description: A program that assists low-income families in obtaining child care so they can work or attend training and education, while also promoting quality in child care and coordination among early childhood development and afterschool programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides assistance to low-income families to help them obtain child care services while they work or attend training and education programs. Also supports quality improvements and coordination among early childhood and afterschool programs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income families needing child care to work or pursue education or training
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Child care services
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland

structured_extraction.program_name: Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP)
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides reimbursements for nutritionally balanced meals and snacks to eligible children (including infants) enrolled at participating childcare centers, daycare homes, afterschool care programs, and emergency shelters, as well as to adults over 60 or living with disabilities in adult daycare facilities. Meals comply with USDA nutrition standards and the Dietary Guidelines for Americans. Over 300 agencies participate statewide. Child care centers that participate receive reimbursement for food costs to help ensure young children are well fed, particularly in low-income families.
