structured_extraction.program_description: A federal grant program that requires local education agencies identified as having significant racial or ethnic disproportionality in special education identification, placement, or discipline to reserve 15 percent of their IDEA Part B funding to implement proactive and responsive actions addressing root causes of overidentification. The program supports educational and behavioral evaluations, services, professional development, and systemic organizational change to promote equity.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Local education agencies (LEAs) identified by the state as having significant disproportionality must reserve 15 percent of IDEA Part B Section 611 and Section 619 combined funds to implement CCEIS. Funds must be calculated based on both Part B 611 and Part B 619 total combined passthrough funds, with full flexibility regarding whether the reservation is made with 611 funds, 619 funds, or both. Part B 619 funds reserved for this purpose may be expended for any approved CCEIS activity and are not limited to services for students ages 3-5. Funds support: (1) educational and behavioral evaluations, services, and supports including evidence-based literacy instruction; (2) professional development and coaching for staff capacity-building; (3) self-assessment and root cause analysis processes; (4) stakeholder engagement and systemic awareness building; (5) implementation drivers including staffing, training, and professional learning experiences; (6) staff performance evaluation; (7) data systems and progress monitoring; and (8) comprehensive evaluation of plan outcomes. Allowable costs include: coaches/mentors (who may not provide instruction unless appropriately licensed); extended contracts/hours for staff delivering interventions; general education teacher salaries for providing academic/behavioral interventions and professional development; guidance counselor salaries for behavioral interventions and progress monitoring; professional development services; school psychologist salaries for implementing behavioral interventions; RTI/MTSS coordinator salaries for coordinating intervention delivery; school social worker salaries for progress monitoring and behavioral interventions; substitute teacher salaries; staff travel for professional development; tutoring services; computing devices for delivery of interventions; instructional materials for struggling students; and instructional software exclusively for intervention delivery. Unallowable costs include: alternative education replacing core programming; student transportation; core curriculum activities; furniture; special education eligibility evaluations; occupational/physical therapist services (except for students determined to need Tier 2 or 3 interventions); rent/occupancy costs; universal screening costs; and child find activities. Funding is mandatory for identified LEAs and tied to federal special education appropriations.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling/Ongoing - identified LEAs submit SFY 2025 Plan by specified deadline; subsequent interim reports due January 31, 2025 and January 31, 2026; final report due November 30, 2026
structured_extraction.contact_name: Gary W. Richardson, MBA (Branch Chief) and Demetria White (Interagency Specialist)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local education agencies (LEAs) identified by Maryland as having significant disproportionality in special education identification, placement, or disciplinary actions based on race or ethnicity for two or more consecutive years. An LEA is identified when it has one or more student subgroups with a risk ratio greater than 2.0 for two or more consecutive years, unless the risk ratio declines by .15 (if less than 4.0) or .5 (if 4.0 or greater) from one year to the next, demonstrating reasonable progress.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational and behavioral evaluations, services and support including evidence-based literacy instruction; professional development and coaching; self-assessment and data review; root cause analysis; leadership and stakeholder engagement; systemic awareness building; professional learning experiences; implementation drivers including staffing and training; coaching and consultation; staff performance evaluation; data systems; progress monitoring; and evaluation of plan outcomes. Funds may serve children ages 3-21 who are not currently identified as requiring special education but who need additional academic and behavioral support to succeed in general education, as well as children currently identified as requiring special education (though funds may not be used exclusively for this group). CCEIS may not be used for core curriculum activities intended for all students, alternative programming that replaces core instruction, special education eligibility evaluations, child find activities, student transportation, or office equipment/furniture.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applies statewide to identified local education agencies in Maryland that meet the criteria of having one or more student subgroups with a risk ratio greater than 2.0 for two or more consecutive years in identification, placement, or discipline categories. Identification is based on Maryland's standard methodology for analyzing significant disproportionality, which compares the risk of each racial or ethnic group to all other groups within the LEA using 14 categories of analysis across identification, placement, and discipline.
requirements_list: LEA must be identified by the state as having significant disproportionality in special education based on risk ratios
Risk ratio must be greater than 2.0 for one or more student subgroups for two or more consecutive years
Unless risk ratio declines by .15 (if less than 4.0) or .5 (if 4.0 or greater) from one year to the next, demonstrating reasonable progress
Must reserve 15 percent of IDEA Part B Section 611 and Section 619 combined funds for CCEIS
Must address root cause factors contributing to disproportionality through comprehensive data analysis
Must address and review policies, practices, or procedures identified as contributing to overidentification or inappropriate identification
Must establish diverse stakeholder group representative of affected populations and general/special education staff

Must engage in self-assessment and root cause analysis using MSDE-recommended tool (IDEA Data Center Equity Rubric, Addressing Root Causes of Disparities in School Discipline guide, or Assessing and Improving Special Education Program Review Tool)
Must plan proactive and responsive actions targeting identified root causes
Must build systemic awareness and leadership supports for organizational change
Must establish job-embedded professional learning for staff capacity-building
Must develop comprehensive evaluation system for monitoring and assessing plan outcomes and implementation
Must align projected expenditures with specific Planned Response Actions addressing identified root causes
Must conduct annual review of policies, practices, and procedures
Must submit CCEIS Plan using SFY 2025 Plan Template including root cause analysis, stakeholder engagement, action planning, and budget alignment
Must submit standard fiscal budget forms (C-1-25) with budget detail
May submit programmatic and fiscal amendments as needed
Must track progress using CCEIS Progress Report Template with interim reports and final report
Must ensure non-supplant requirement - funds supplement but do not replace state, local, or other federal funds
Must publicly report on revisions to policies, practices, and procedures
Compliance with IDEA regulations 34 CFR §300.646 and §300.647
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: (1) Identification Phase: State identifies LEAs with significant disproportionality using standard risk ratio methodology comparing each racial/ethnic group to all others across 14 categories of analysis (identification, placement, discipline). MSDE issues Letter of Significant Disproportionality to identified LEAs. (2) Planning Phase: Identified LEA forms diverse Implementation Team including administrators, general/special educators, instructional specialists, parents, and community members. Team conducts comprehensive self-assessment using one of three MSDE-recommended tools: IDEA Data Center Equity Rubric, Addressing Root Causes of Disparities in School Discipline guide, or Assessing and Improving Special Education Program Review Tool. Team analyzes data from multiple sources (school/district/regional comparison data, process fidelity data, prior intervention impacts, student-level data by race/ethnicity) to identify root causes. Team completes SFY 2025 CCEIS Plan Template including: (a) identification of categories of analysis and at-risk areas to address; (b) narrative describing self-assessment process, data findings, and root cause factors; (c) school/feeder pattern analysis identifying schools most significantly disproportionate; and (d) Planned Response Actions (PRAs) addressing root causes. (3) PRA Development: For each identified root cause, LEA develops separate PRAs that include: measurable outcomes with goals and interim benchmarks aligned to reporting periods; data sources/methods for evaluating progress; and focus areas addressing: (i) review and/or adjustment to policies, procedures, practices (required for each identified area); (ii) academic or behavioral interventions; and/or (iii) professional learning. Each PRA includes detailed budget using Excel budget templates for Part B 611 and Part B 619 funds. (4) Submission: LEA submits complete CCEIS Plan package including: SFY 2025 CCEIS Plan Template, MSDE Grant Budget C-1-25 forms (separate for each funding source if not combined), Budget Detail Forms, self-assessment tool results, and supporting fiscal documents. All designated local officials (Director of Special Education, Chief Academic Officer, Finance Officer, Superintendent) must sign plan for submission to MSDE. (5) Review and Approval: MSDE DEI/SES Equity Specialist, Programmatic Liaison, Fiscal Liaison, and Resource Management and Monitoring Branch Chief review and approve plans. Upon approval, revised allocation sheet issued if LEA changed distribution of Part B 611 and 619 allocations. (6) Implementation and Monitoring: LEA implements approved PRAs. MSDE and LEA monitoring teams collect and analyze data on implementation and outcomes at defined intervals. (7) Progress Reporting: LEA submits CCEIS Interim Progress/Cumulative Variance Report #1 by January 31, 2025 (for period July 1, 2024 - December 31, 2024), Interim Report #2 by January 31, 2026 (for period January 1, 2025 - December 31, 2025), and Final Progress/Cumulative Variance Report and Final Financial Report by November 30, 2026. Grant Amendment Requests accepted by August 15, 2026. (8) Ongoing: LEAs may submit programmatic and fiscal amendments as needed based on data and implementation progress. Amendments require updated C-1-25, C-1-25 A, C-1-25 B, Budget Detail, and signatures from all required officials and MSDE liaisons. Contact MSDE Resource Management and Monitoring Branch for specific submission deadlines and procedures.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides consultation, assessment, and support services to help people with disabilities explore, access, and participate in registered apprenticeship programs across Maryland. Services include apprenticeship consultation, academic assessment, exploration of opportunities, academic instruction, pre-apprenticeship support, registered apprenticeship support, and youth apprenticeship support.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: D ORS provides no-cost consultation and support services to individuals with disabilities interested in apprenticeships. Services include apprenticeship consultation to identify opportunities, academic assessment to determine current skill levels, in-depth exploration of various apprenticeship opportunities, academic instruction to improve academic levels, pre-apprenticeship program support, registered apprenticeship program support, and youth apprenticeship tracking and support. All services are delivered by DORS staff including an Apprenticeship Coordinator and Academic Instructor. Registered apprenticeships are paid jobs where apprentices work full-time while receiving on-the-job training from skilled craftspeople and related classroom instruction, earning progressive wages as they gain skills.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Marylanders with disabilities seeking to pursue apprenticeships and develop skilled trades while earning a wage.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services support exploration, preparation, and participation in registered apprenticeship programs. Apprentices work full-time while receiving classroom instruction and on-the-job training from skilled craftspeople, earning progressive wages as they gain skills. Individuals can visit occupations.mdapprenticeship.com to view available occupations and connect with an apprenticeship navigator.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout the state of Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a DORS consumer (individual with a disability receiving DORS services)
Interest in exploring or participating in registered apprenticeship opportunities
Must be 18 years of age
Must have a high school diploma (by means of high school graduation, GED, or NEDP)
Must be physically able to perform required tasks
Must be drug free
Must have transportation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Apprenticeship Coordinator to begin. Initial consultation involves identifying apprenticeship interests and determining which assessment or support services are needed. Services are customized based on individual needs and readiness level. To become an apprentice: (1) Visit occupations.mdapprenticeship.com to see available occupations; (2) Call (410) 767-2246 or email info@mdapprenticeship.com to connect with an apprenticeship navigator; (3) Apply directly to the program sponsor or employer.

Students receive classroom and practical training in floor care, cleaning, sanitation, and related workplace skills at the Workforce & Technology Center campus in Baltimore.

structured_extraction.program_description: A vocational training program that prepares individuals with disabilities for careers in food services through classroom instruction and hands-on experience. The program combines seven weeks of classroom and cafeteria training with a seven-week internship at a local business. Training is offered in partnership with the Community College of Baltimore County at the DORS Workforce & Technology Center (WTC) campus in northeast Baltimore.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides seven weeks of classroom instruction at the Workforce Training Center and hands-on experience in the WTC cafeteria, followed by a seven-week internship at a local business. Training covers food handling and preparation, kitchen safety, equipment operation, recipe reading, food portions and nutrition, weighing and measuring, customer service, point of sale operations, and ServSafe principles. The program is designed for job seekers with disabilities and is offered in partnership with the Community College of Baltimore County.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training in food handling and preparation, kitchen safety, equipment operation, recipe reading, food portions and nutrition, weighing and measuring, customer service, point of sale operations, and ServSafe principles.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program helps individuals who are 55 or older and are blind or have a vision impairment to live independently in their homes and communities. The program teaches people with vision loss how to become independent through independent living skills training, including safe cooking techniques and managing personal care and household tasks. ILOB rehabilitation specialists will come to your home to provide assessment and training.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Services and training to help individuals age 55 and older who are blind or have vision impairments live independently in their homes and communities. Examples of services include: training in managing personal care and household tasks; labeling and organizing personal care items, clothing, appliances and medications; safe cooking techniques; orientation and mobility training; Braille instruction; use of assistive technology; referral to community peer support groups and other services; and introduction to community resources such as NFB-NEWSLINE and resources at the Maryland State Library for the Blind and Print Disabled. ILOB rehabilitation specialists provide in-home assessment and training, and work as a team with ophthalmologists, low vision professionals and community partners to provide personalized service.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Independent living support services and skills training to help people become independent in their homes and communities, including training in personal care and household management, safe cooking, orientation and mobility, Braille instruction, assistive technology use, and community resource connections.

structured_extraction.program_name: Infant and Early Childhood Mental Health Support Services (IECMHSS) Program Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide grant program that supports positive mental and behavioral health practices for young children from birth through age 5 who have developmental, social, emotional, or behavioral issues. The program funds non-profit and public agencies to provide consultation, referrals, and mental health services for children, families, teachers, and caregivers. Consultants deliver training, coaching, and mentoring to child care staff and teachers to build confidence and competence in managing challenging behaviors, improve classroom environments, and connect children and families to more intensive mental health services when needed. The program builds the capacity of early care and education providers and family members to promote healthy social-emotional development for young children. It operates in partnership with community resources including Judy Centers, Head Start Centers, health departments, Child Find, and Maryland Infants & Toddlers Program, across all 12 statewide child care licensing regions.
list_of_relevant_industries: Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding to non-profit and public agencies licensed in Maryland to provide infant and early childhood mental health services, including consultation, training, coaching, and mentoring to child care staff and teachers. Eligible organizations must be non-profit or public agencies licensed to do business in Maryland with proven capacity to provide these services and must operate 12 months per year except for federal holidays.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit and public agencies licensed in Maryland that provide infant and early childhood mental health services; child care providers, teachers, program directors, and families of children birth through 5 years old, particularly those in licensed child care facilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To provide consultation, referrals, and mental health services for children, families, teachers, and caregivers; to train and coach child care staff on handling challenging behaviors; to improve classroom environments; to refer children and families to appropriate mental health services; and to build the capacity of early care and education providers to promote healthy social-emotional development for young children.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: State of Maryland — available across all 12 statewide child care licensing regions, having expanded from an initial pilot in Baltimore City and the Eastern Shore.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a non-profit or public agency
Applicant must be licensed to do business within the State of Maryland
Applicant must have proven capacity to provide Infant and Early Childhood Mental Health Services
Applicant must operate 12 months per year except for federal holidays
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the Infant and Early Childhood Mental Health Support Services Program Application form by the deadline. Customer service support sessions are offered to provide an overview of the program, requirements, and proposal.

structured_extraction.program_name: Licensing Compliance Grant for Family Child Care Providers (LCGFCCP)
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that helps registered family child care providers offset costs of opening their child care programs and achieving compliance with family child care licensing regulations. Formerly known as the Family Child Care Provider Grant Program, the program reimburses eligible registered family child care providers who meet income eligibility requirements for up to $1,000 in costs related to meeting state family child care regulatory requirements.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimbursement grants of up to $1,000 for registered family child care providers who meet income eligibility requirements, covering costs related to meeting the requirements of the family child care regulations and opening their child care programs. Eligible expenses include safety supplies, provider medical examination fees, criminal background check fees, small household repairs in approved child care areas, approved child care training course fees, expenses related to local water/sewer/fire/health requirements, and program materials and equipment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Registered family child care providers in Maryland with annual income not exceeding 60% of Maryland's current State Median Income (SMI) for their family size.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Costs associated with opening child care programs and achieving or maintaining compliance with family child care regulations, including safety supplies, provider medical examination fees, criminal background check fees, household repairs in child care areas, training course fees, expenses related to local requirements, and program materials and equipment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a registered family child care provider
Annual income must not exceed 60% of Maryland's State Median Income (SMI) for the applicant's family size
Must be seeking to achieve or maintain compliance with family child care regulations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are processed according to regulations set forth at COMAR 13A.14.07, which specify eligibility requirements, application procedures, and award methods. Contact the Office of Child Care Regional Licensing Office for application procedures.

structured_extraction.program_name: Local Early Childhood Advisory Council System Improvement Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: Grants that support Local Early Childhood Advisory Councils (ECACs) in coordinating early childhood services at the local level. Activities include establishing school readiness benchmarks, conducting needs assessments of early childhood education programs and services, developing action plans to increase program participation and quality, coordinating early childhood initiatives and reforms, and reporting progress to the Governor's State Advisory Council. Funded through PDG B-5 and administered by the MSDE Division of Early Childhood.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding provided to Local ECACs to support coordination of early childhood services at the local level. Funded activities include: (1) establishing annual benchmarks of school readiness skills for children entering kindergarten; (2) conducting periodic local needs assessments concerning quality and availability of early childhood education and development programs and services; (3) identifying opportunities for and barriers to collaboration and coordination among federally funded and state-funded child development, child care, and early childhood education programs; (4) developing action plans for increasing overall participation of children in existing programs with outreach to underrepresented and special populations, and for elevating program quality; (5) developing recommendations regarding local professional development and career advancement plans for early childhood educators; (6) aligning local family engagement practices with the State Family Engagement Coalition; (7) coordinating Race to the Top Early Learning Challenge projects and other early childhood initiatives and reforms at the local level; and (8) reporting progress to the Governor's State Advisory Council on Early Childhood Education and Care, including quarterly submission of attendance rosters, meeting minutes, and annual reports on local council action plans.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local Early Childhood Advisory Councils (ECACs) throughout Maryland, which include multidisciplinary members representing local government executives, school superintendents, early learning coordinators, special education directors, child care providers and directors, Head Start agencies, health department representatives, family support organizations, higher education institutions, parent representatives, library representatives, business leaders, social services agencies, school principals, home visiting programs, and community action agencies.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Service delivery coordination at the local level; establishing annual benchmarks of school readiness skills; conducting periodic needs assessments of early childhood education programs and services; developing action plans to increase program participation with outreach to underrepresented and special populations and to elevate program quality; developing recommendations for professional development and career advancement for early childhood educators; aligning local family engagement practices with the State Family Engagement Coalition; coordinating early childhood initiatives and reforms including Race to the Top Early Learning Challenge goals and objectives; and reporting progress to the Governor's State Advisory Council on Early Childhood Education and Care.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide through Maryland's Local ECACs serving all 24 Maryland counties and Baltimore City. ECACs are established in accordance with H.R. 1429, Public Law 110-134 (The Improving Head Start for School Readiness Act of 2007, Section 642(b)) and the Federal Race to the Top: Early Learning Challenge Grant. Each ECAC operates under a formal Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) submitted to the Maryland State Department of Education, Division of Early Childhood Development, for approval.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Local ECAC established in accordance with H.R. 1429, Public Law 110-134 and the Federal Race to the Top: Early Learning Challenge Grant
Local ECAC must have executed a formal Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) with MSDE Division of Early Childhood Development

Council membership must conform to Executive Order 01.01.2008.09 and include representatives from local government, schools, early learning programs, health, social services, family engagement, and business

Council must include voting members per bylaws requirements (up to 37 members including county executive or designee, school superintendent or designee, early learning coordinator, special education director, child care representatives, Head Start representatives, health representatives, family representatives, library representatives, business representatives, and others)
Council must meet at least four times per calendar year with open public meetings
Council must maintain attendance rosters and meeting minutes for all meetings
Council members must comply with conflict of interest provisions
Council must submit quarterly rosters and meeting minutes to the Governor's State Advisory Council on Early Childhood Education and Care
Council must submit annual reports on local council action plans to the Governor's State Advisory Council
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Local ECACs apply through a process managed by the MSDE Division of Early Childhood via the MSDE Grants website. The application process includes submission of a formal Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) to MSDE Division of Early Childhood Development for approval. Upon MOA approval, MSDE will provide funding as specified. Local ECACs must establish bylaws consistent with recommended ECAC bylaws and ensure compliance with governance, membership, meeting, and reporting requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: A quality certification program for licensed child care centers and public pre-kindergarten programs to demonstrate their commitment to providing high-quality early learning. Programs work through a 24-month process using Maryland Accreditation Standards, self-appraisals, program improvement plans, technical assistance (virtual and onsite), and validation visits to achieve accreditation status, which is valid for five years. Once accredited, programs become eligible for Maryland EXCELS Quality Rating 5, higher EXCELS payments, and access to Accreditation Support Funds for purchasing instructional materials.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Programs receive technical assistance support through virtual sessions (phone calls with validators discussing program administration and home/community partnerships) and onsite visits (observation and feedback on program operations across all classrooms). Accredited programs become eligible for higher Maryland EXCELS payments and access to Accreditation Support Funds for purchasing instructional materials. Technical assistance is optional and can be requested once after completing initial self-appraisals. Virtual and onsite TA sessions each consist of one opportunity per accreditation cycle.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing; rolling admissions. Applications accepted at any time. Within 12 months of completing the Maryland Accreditation Orientation, programs must select 'Begin Accreditation' in the online system.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed child care centers and public pre-kindergarten programs in Maryland. Family child care programs are not currently eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Accreditation Support Fund monies can be used for purchasing instructional materials to support program improvements. Technical assistance supports program improvement across administration, operations, and community partnerships.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; all Maryland counties.
requirements_list: Program must be a licensed child care center or public pre-kindergarten program
Family child care programs are not eligible
Program must complete the self-paced Maryland Accreditation Orientation
Program must complete and submit an application to participate in Maryland Accreditation
Program must form a Self-Appraisal Team
Program must complete Initial Self-Appraisals with input from staff and enrolled families and submit comments and required documentation for each indicator within 12 months of beginning accreditation
Program must develop and submit a Program Improvement Plan based on indicators rated Partially Met or Not Met
Program must apply for Maryland Accreditation Support Funds (optional)
Program may request optional Virtual or Onsite Technical Assistance
Program must complete Final Self-Appraisal reviewing program improvements and submit comments and required documentation for each indicator
Program must request a Validation Visit at least 90 days before accreditation expiration
Program must participate in a Validation Visit with observation and feedback at least 30 days before accreditation expiration
Program must upload comments, required documents, and pictures in response to validator ratings within 3 days of binder reopening

For staff qualifications - Licensed Child Care/Head Start teachers must have Associate's degree in Early Childhood Education/Child Development or related field and Maryland Child Care Credential Level 5 or higher (or Administrator Credential Level 2 or higher, or Bachelor's degree in Early Childhood Education/Child Development, or current Maryland teaching certificate for early childhood); Assistant Teachers must have high school diploma and Maryland Child Care Credential Level 2 or higher (or CDA Certificate, or 90 hours certification)

For staff qualifications - Public School teachers must have Bachelor's degree in Early Childhood Education/Child Development or related field and meet Maryland State Certification requirements; Assistant Teachers/Paraprofessionals must have high school diploma and meet Maryland ParaPro requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Complete the self-paced Maryland Accreditation Orientation. 2. Submit an application to participate in Maryland Accreditation. 3. Within 12 months of finishing orientation, select 'Begin Accreditation' in the Maryland Accreditation online system. 4. Form a Self-Appraisal Team and complete Initial Self-Appraisals with submissions of comments and required documentation for each indicator. 5. Apply for Maryland Accreditation Support Funds. 6. Develop and submit a Program Improvement Plan for indicators needing improvement. 7. Optionally request and complete Virtual Technical Assistance (phone consultation on Program Administration and Home and Community Partnerships sections) or Onsite Technical Assistance (validator observation of indoor/outdoor environments and feedback on Program Operation section). 8. Complete Final Self-Appraisal with submissions of comments and required documentation for each indicator. 9. Request a Validation Visit at least 90 days before accreditation expiration. 10. Host the Validation Visit at least 30 days before expiration. 11. Within 3 days of binder reopening, upload comments, required evidence, and pictures in response to validator ratings. 12. Receive Accreditation Decision from MSDE. 13. While accredited (Years 1-3), submit Annual Updates up to 60 days before due dates. 14. Beginning 24 months before accreditation expiration (Years 4-5), begin the re-accreditation process.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Assistive Technology (MTAP) loan program helps Maryland residents with disabilities and their families qualify for low-interest loans to buy assistive technology equipment, devices, adapted and non-adapted vehicles in order to live, work, and learn more independently and to support various employment goals.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest loans are available from $500 to $60,000 to purchase assistive technology equipment and devices for Maryland residents with disabilities. Applicants approved on their own merit by the lender receive a preferred/discounted interest rate through the ATLP process. If declined by the lender, the ATLP Board of Directors will consider the application for a loan guarantee. Approval time is typically 30-45 days.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents with disabilities and their families
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To purchase assistive technology equipment, devices, adapted and non-adapted vehicles to help people live, work, and learn more independently and support employment goals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Maryland resident with a disability or a family member of a person with a disability
Must intend to use the loan to buy assistive technology for a Maryland resident with a disability
Must have a good likelihood of repaying the loan
Photo ID (passport, driver's license, or state-issued ID) required for application submission
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Click 'Apply Now' and log in or register for a OneStop account. 2. Complete the online application form. 3. Upload a photo or scan of your photo ID (passport, driver's license, or state-issued ID). 4. Submit the application to ATLP staff for review. ATLP staff will review for completeness and verify the loan is for assistive technology. 5. Application is submitted to the lender for review. If approved on its own merit, the lender determines your interest rate and you can close the loan at a branch office or by mail. If declined by the lender, ATLP submits your request to the ATLP Board of Directors for consideration of a loan guarantee. 6. If the Board declines a loan guarantee, you have the right to appeal the decision in writing or alternative format to the ATLP office address provided.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Business Enterprise Program for the Blind (BEP)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Business Enterprise Program for the Blind is authorized by the Federally mandated Randolph-Sheppard Act and prepares individuals whose primary disability is vision loss to operate successful retail concession, food service, and vending operations in Federal, Military, DOD and State property and at business partner locations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides three-phase training consisting of: (1) an eight-week New Manager Training course conducted by BEP staff at DORS' Workforce & Technology Center in Northeast Baltimore; (2) formal food service training with certified instructors and chefs leading to National Restaurant Association food service sanitation certification; and (3) on-the-job training consisting of three to six months of extended internship at various BEP facilities under an experienced manager. The program also provides licensing and oversight to manage vending facilities operations.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Maryland Business Enterprise Program for the Blind
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals whose primary disability is vision loss who are interested in becoming licensed business managers for retail concession and food service operations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and preparation to operate retail concession, food service, and vending operations in public facilities including State office buildings, federal agencies, and military installations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Federal, Military, DOD and State property and business partner locations throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Primary disability is blindness or vision loss
Be a legally blind U.S. Citizen
Have at minimum a high school diploma or GED equivalent
Have an aptitude for business management
Have practical skills and meet the legal criteria for operating a business supported by federal law
Be referred by a DORS OBVS counselor
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals can request services by going to dors.maryland.gov and selecting Request DORS Services. The form can be completed by the job seeker, a family member, a medical provider, a social worker, or other representative. After submission, the individual will be contacted to set up an intake meeting where a DORS counselor will gather and provide information regarding eligibility for DORS services and discuss BEP opportunities. If already working with a DORS counselor, applicants can ask their counselor directly about BEP.

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary professional development system that recognizes and rewards child care professionals—including registered family child care providers, licensed child care center operators, directors, teachers, and aides—who exceed state licensing and registration requirements. The program guides participants through seven credential levels for staff and four levels for administrators, based on approved training, work experience, and professional activities. It helps develop a professional workforce, improves provider compensation, recognizes professional learning and ongoing education, and provides a structure for career growth. Participants earn achievement bonuses ranging from $200 to $1,500 upon achieving a credential level, receive up to $400 per year in training vouchers and reimbursements (for Level 2 and above), and are eligible for tuition assistance through the Child Care Career and Professional Development Fund (CCCPDF) for approved college or university programs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants earn achievement bonuses upon achieving credential levels: Staff Credential Levels 2, 3, and 4 receive one-time bonuses of $200, $300, and $500 respectively; Staff Credential Levels 4+, 5, and 6 receive annual bonuses of $600, $750, and $1,000 respectively. Administrator Credential Level 1 receives a one-time bonus of $600; Administrator Credential Levels 2, 3, and 4 receive annual bonuses of $750, $1,000, and $1,500 respectively. Participants with credential Level 2 or higher receive up to $400 per year in training vouchers and reimbursements (as funds are available) for pre-service training, conferences, and college coursework. All participants are eligible for tuition assistance through the Child Care Career and Professional Development Fund (CCCPDF) for enrolling in approved college or university programs to earn an Associate's, Bachelor's, or Master's degree.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Renewal applications open periodically; check program website for updates. Requests reviewed and processed within 60 days of receipt.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Registered family child care providers and operators, directors, teachers, assistant teachers, and aides (working part-time or full-time) in licensed child care centers or programs with a Letter of Compliance in Maryland who want to advance professionally beyond state licensing requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Achievement bonuses for reaching credential levels; training vouchers and reimbursements for pre-service training, conferences, and college coursework; tuition assistance for approved college or university programs related to child care and early childhood education.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide program serving all of Maryland. Participants must work in a registered family child care home, licensed child care center, or Letter of Compliance program in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a registered family child care provider or an operator, director, or staff member (teacher, assistant teacher, or aide) in a licensed child care center or Letter of Compliance program in Maryland
Cannot be a substitute or volunteer in a child care program
Cannot be a child care center employee who does not work directly with children on a daily basis (e.g., regional/district manager, administrative, maintenance, food service, transportation staff)
Cannot have been sanctioned by the Office of Child Care
Must complete approved Core of Knowledge (COK) training in six key areas: Child Development, Curriculum, Health Safety and Nutrition, Special Needs, Professionalism, and Community
Must meet work experience requirements specific to each credential level (ranging from none for Level 1 to five years for Administrator Level 4)

Must participate in Professional Activity Units (PAUs) related to the child care profession, such as professional association membership, accreditation participation, mentoring, or community involvement
Must continue working in a child care setting for at least one year after acceptance into the program

Credentials are issued for a 12-month period and may be renewed if continuing to work in a registered or licensed child care program, completing continued training, and participating in professional activities
All criteria must be met to qualify for each credential level
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Providers apply through the Workforce Advancement Branch (formerly Credentialing Branch) of the Office of Early Learning and Quality Improvement to participate in the voluntary credential program. Participants must map out a professional development plan in consultation with the program to ensure selected training applies toward credential goals. Applicants must submit documentation of completed Core of Knowledge training, work experience, and Professional Activity Units. Applications for renewals are accepted on a rolling basis; interested providers should contact the program or monitor the website for updates. PAU activities not listed on the standard matrix can be submitted using the Professional Activity Unit Approval Form for individual review, with decisions made within 60 days of receipt.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Child Care Resource Network (MCCRN) Technical Assistance
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Child Care Resource Network provides technical assistance to help child care providers start, expand, and operate child care centers or become family child care providers. Services include support with licensing and compliance, behavioral issues, special needs support, and credential and program accreditation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Technical assistance services covering licensing and compliance issues, behavioral issues, children with special needs, and support for credential and program accreditation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Existing and potential center-based and family child care providers, Head Start programs, nursery schools, cooperatives, drop-in centers and playgroups, community and non-profit organizations, community groups, employers, and public agencies committed to expanding child care resources.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Technical assistance for starting, expanding, and operating child care services, including licensing compliance, behavioral support, special needs accommodations, and program accreditation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide - available throughout Maryland

structured_extraction.program_description: A Quality Rating and Improvement System that awards child care and early education programs quality ratings from 1 to 5 based on meeting standards in areas like developmentally-appropriate practice, professional development, and family engagement. Participating providers receive guidance, training, and incentives to improve their practices.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Providers receive a road map, training, and incentives to improve quality. Support includes guidance from a regional Quality Assurance Specialist and opportunities to learn from other providers. Participating providers publish and improve their Quality Rating by uploading evidence of meeting Maryland EXCELS Standards into an online system. Regional Quality Assurance Specialists provide direct assistance with increasing quality ratings and connect providers to available training, work groups, and resources.
structured_extraction.contact_email: Various by region (lisa.smith1@maryland.gov, ashley.hensley@maryland.gov, patricia.aburn@maryland.gov, audreyc.green@maryland.gov, rosemary.lober@maryland.gov, monique.dawkins@maryland.gov, yvonne.bell@maryland.gov, petrea.hicks@maryland.gov, maryb.johnson@maryland.gov, theadora.quible@maryland.gov, urceal.cook@maryland.gov, vickie.disanto@maryland.gov, meghan.leach@maryland.gov, lornya.bowie@maryland.gov)
structured_extraction.contact_phone: Various by region; see attachment for county-specific contacts
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care and early education programs seeking to improve quality and maintain participation in the Quality Rating and Improvement System
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable; this is a quality improvement and rating system rather than a direct funding program
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Regional Quality Assurance Specialists serve specific counties: Baltimore County, Baltimore City, Cecil & Harford, Carroll & Howard, Montgomery, Allegany, Frederick, Garrett & Washington, The Eastern Shore (Caroline, Dorchester, Kent, Queen Anne's, Somerset, Talbot, Wicomico, Worcester), Anne Arundel, Calvert, Charles, St. Mary's, and Prince George's.
requirements_list: Meet Maryland EXCELS Standards in developmentally-appropriate practice, professional development, and family engagement
Participate in publishing and improving Quality Rating
Work with a regional Quality Assurance Specialist
Upload evidence of meeting Standards into the online system
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Providers sign up to participate in Maryland EXCELS and contact their regional Quality Assurance Specialist for assistance. A Quality Assurance Specialist supports the provider in creating and uploading evidence of meeting Standards into an online system. Evidence is reviewed by Maryland EXCELS staff, and the provider receives a rating for each Standard area as well as an overall rating from 1 to 5. Specialists are available by region to provide training, connect providers to work groups, and help providers access available resources.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland State Department of Education distributes bonuses to child care programs participating in Maryland EXCELS to support quality improvement. Programs receive bonuses ranging from $1,000 to $13,500 based on program type, quality rating level, and capacity.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Bonuses are distributed as flat payments ranging from $1,000 to $13,500 based on program type, capacity, and quality rating level. Child care centers with capacity 1-50 receive $1,000 to $4,500; centers with capacity 51-100 receive $1,000 to $9,000; centers with capacity 101 or more receive $1,000 to $13,500. Family child care homes receive $1,000 to $4,300, and large family homes receive $1,000 to $4,500. Bonuses are paid by check or direct deposit without application required. Payments are made within 60 days of quality rating publication.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care programs participating in Maryland EXCELS, including child care centers and family child care homes
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Bonuses may be spent at the discretion of the program for quality improvements, including learning materials, furniture, staff salary increases, accreditation efforts, and other program enhancements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to all eligible programs statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Program must be participating in Maryland EXCELS
Program must be in compliance with all Maryland EXCELS regulations
Program must participate in scheduled Continuous Quality Improvement visits
Program must publish a quality rating for the first time, or re-publish a quality rating of 4 or 5 between July 1, 2025 and June 30, 2026
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: No application is required. Eligible programs automatically receive bonus payments by check or direct deposit within 60 days of their quality rating being published. Program directors can check payment status on the General Accounting Division website. Contact your regional Quality Assurance Specialist for assistance with increasing your quality rating and to learn more about available training, work groups, and resources.

structured_extraction.program_description: A quality-based reimbursement program that rewards child care providers for offering high-quality services to families using the Child Care Scholarship program. Providers at Maryland EXCELS Quality Rating levels 3, 4, and 5 receive increased reimbursement amounts ranging from 10% to 44% depending on the child's age, type of care, and the program's quality rating. Payments are automatically applied and shown as 'EXCELS' payments on the Invoice Detail Report.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Increased reimbursement payments to child care providers based on their Maryland EXCELS Quality Rating. Family child care homes receive 10–29% increased reimbursement for children under 2 years and 10–28% for children 2 years and over. Child care centers receive 22–44% increased reimbursement for children under 2 years and 10–26% for children 2 years and over. The specific percentage depends on the provider's quality rating level (3, 4, or 5). Payments are automatically applied and shown as 'EXCELS' payments on the Invoice Detail Report.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care providers (family child care homes and child care centers) participating in the Maryland EXCELS quality rating system and serving families eligible for the Child Care Scholarship program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Increased reimbursement for providing high-quality child care services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Program must be participating in Maryland EXCELS
Program must have achieved and maintain a Maryland EXCELS Quality Rating of at least Level 3
Provider must be serving families using the Child Care Scholarship program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Providers participating in Maryland EXCELS and the Child Care Scholarship program automatically receive the increased reimbursement payments based on their quality rating level. No separate application is required beyond initial enrollment in both programs.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Economic Development Assistance Authority and Fund (MEDAAF) - Child Care Facility Loans
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides special purpose loans to construct, expand, or improve child care facilities in Maryland. Available to non-profit organizations, for-profit businesses, and individuals operating or planning to operate a child care facility.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Special purpose loans are available to finance the construction, expansion, or improvement of child care facilities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care facility operators and developers seeking to construct, expand, or improve their facilities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction, expansion, or improvement of child care facilities
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Must be operating or planning to operate a child care facility
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Maryland Department of Business and Economic Development for loan application procedures and requirements.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Hearing Aid and Language & Communication Video Loan Bank
structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide resource that allows families of deaf or hard of hearing children to borrow hearing aids for up to one year at no cost. The program also provides videos and resources to help families learn communication methods such as American Sign Language, Cued Speech, and spoken language development strategies.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Families may borrow hearing aids for up to one year at no cost. The program also provides DVDs and other educational materials about language and communication options for deaf and hard of hearing children. All resources are provided at no cost to eligible families.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Zella Shabasson, Au.D. and Dr. Paige Bradford
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland families of children who are deaf or hard of hearing from birth to age 21 who have not yet graduated from high school.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Hearing aids for deaf or hard of hearing children. Educational videos and materials about language and communication development options including American Sign Language, Cued Speech, and spoken language strategies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland residents only.
requirements_list: Child must be diagnosed by an audiologist or other medical professional as deaf or hard of hearing
Child must be from birth to age 21 and not yet have graduated from high school
Family must be Maryland residents

For hearing aids: applicant must not have insurance coverage for hearing aids, be experiencing delays or difficulties acquiring or replacing hearing aids, and/or need a hearing aid trial before purchasing personal aids or receiving a cochlear implant
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Families can request materials through online links for hearing aids, language and communication videos, or other resources for families of deaf and hard of hearing children. Contact information is provided for the Audiologist or Section Chief in the Division of Special Education.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Infants & Toddlers Program (MITP) Consolidated Local Implementation Grant (CLIG)
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant mechanism through which local jurisdictions receive federal and state funds to implement local early intervention programs for infants and toddlers with disabilities and their families. The program provides formula and project grants to local jurisdictions to support the creation and operation of early intervention services for infants and toddlers with disabilities.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides formula and project grants to local jurisdictions. This financial aid supports early intervention services for infants and toddlers with disabilities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments and non-profit organizations that provide services to infants and toddlers with disabilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support the creation and operation of local early intervention services for infants and toddlers with disabilities.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland Meals for Achievement (MMFA) is a state-funded program that supplements federal meal reimbursements to allow participating schools to offer free breakfast in the classroom to all students. The program ensures all children in participating schools have access to nutritious breakfast at the start of each school day. Participating schools must meet economically disadvantaged criteria. MMFA is credited with improving students' test scores, behavior, attendance, and well-being. Currently 581 schools in Maryland participate in MMFA.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides state funds to supplement federal meal reimbursements, allowing participating schools to offer free breakfast in the classroom to all students at those schools.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students in participating schools in Maryland; schools must meet economically disadvantaged criteria to participate
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Providing free breakfast in the classroom for all students at participating schools
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland counties; currently 581 schools in Maryland participate in MMFA
requirements_list: Schools must meet economically disadvantaged criteria
Schools must participate in the MMFA program and apply to receive state funding
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Schools apply to participate in MMFA to receive state funding to supplement federal meal reimbursements

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Medicaid Home and Community-Based Services Waiver for Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder (Autism Waiver)
structured_extraction.program_description: A Medicaid waiver program that provides community-based, long-term, person-centered therapeutic services and support to eligible children and youth with Autism Spectrum Disorder to enable them to live in their home and community as an alternative to institutional care.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The waiver provides funding for seven types of services: Intensive Individual Support Services (one-on-one assistance based on the child's need for interventions and support to help children acquire, retain, and improve self-help, socialization, communication, daily living, functional living, behavior management, and adaptive skills); Therapeutic Integration - Regular or Intensive (structured programs outside school hours providing therapeutic activities and expressive therapies for children with socialization, isolation, hyperactivity, impulse control, and behavior issues); Respite Care (short-term supervision and assistance with activities of daily living); Environmental Accessibility Adaptations (funding for physical adaptations to the home necessary to ensure health, welfare, and safety); Family Consultation (individualized consultation and training provided to the child's family); Adult Life Planning (family-centered support in accessing adult community services); and Residential Habilitation - Regular or Intensive (community-based residential placement for children who cannot live at home). Participants also receive Service Coordination and targeted case management. Eligible participants qualify for full Medical Assistance benefits including health insurance, prescription coverage, dental care, physician and hospital care, home health, laboratory services, disposable medical supplies, durable medical equipment, and mental health services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children and youth with Autism Spectrum Disorder who meet eligibility criteria and their families.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services include intensive individual support services, therapeutic integration programs, respite care, environmental accessibility adaptations for the home, family consultation and training, adult life planning, and residential habilitation in community settings. Medical Assistance benefits also cover health insurance, prescription drugs, dental care, hospital services, home health, medical supplies, durable medical equipment, and mental health services. Participants must use at least 5 hours of Autism Waiver services per month to maintain eligibility.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Eligible individuals must reside in Maryland. The program serves children ages 1 through the end of the school semester when the child turns 21 years old. Military Exception: Dependents of US Military Service members invited to apply to the Autism Waiver while the family is out of the state for military services shall be offered an opportunity to apply upon request when they return to Maryland and meet all technical eligibility requirements.
requirements_list: Be a resident of Maryland
Be between the age of 1 and 21
Have a current educational classification of Autism or a diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder

Receive early intervention or special education services through an Individual Family Service Plan (IFSP) (ages 1-5), an Individual Education Program (IEP) in an early childhood or Kindergarten setting (ages 3-5), or an IEP with 15 or more hours of special education and related services and/or 1:1 adult supports per week (first grade through exit from high school)
Meet an institutional Level of Care for Intermediate Care Facilities for Individuals with Intellectual Disabilities (ICF-IID) and choose to receive Autism Waiver services as an alternative
Be able to be served and safely maintained in the home and community with Autism Waiver services
Meet financial eligibility for Medical Assistance with monthly income not exceeding 300 percent of Supplemental Security Income (SSI) benefits and countable assets not exceeding $2,000
Choose the Autism Waiver as the waiver that best meets the child's needs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Call the Autism Waiver Registry Helpline at 1-866-417-3480 to register interest. Parents must provide child's name, date of birth, address, county of residence, contact information, and confirm the child has a diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder and an IFSP or IEP with at least 15 hours of special education/related services per week. 2. An MDH vendor conducts initial screening during the intake call based on parent self-report. 3. If technical eligibility criteria are met during the intake call, the child's name is added to the Registry and the family receives a confirmation letter. 4. MSDE verifies technical eligibility (resident of MD, under age 21, Autism Spectrum Disorder diagnosis, IFSP or IEP with 15 hours of special education/health-related services). 5. Child is added to the Autism Waiver Waitlist. Application for enrollment is based on chronological order from the time the child's name is placed on the Waitlist. 6. When the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) identifies a vacancy, an application letter is sent to the family inviting them to apply and giving a 45-day deadline to accept the invitation, establish contact with the Autism Waiver Contact at the local education agency (LEA), complete the technical eligibility checklist, and submit a financial application. 7. Family works with the Autism Waiver Contact to confirm technical, financial, and medical eligibility and complete a Level of Care assessment. 8. Receive notification of eligibility from the State. If eligible, the letter includes a start date to begin Autism Waiver services. 9. Attend a multidisciplinary team meeting to develop a Plan of Care. 10. Maintain eligibility by using at least 5 hours of Autism Waiver services per month.

structured_extraction.program_description: A national recognition program that rewards and inspires excellence in education by honoring top educators with financial awards.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Awards of $25,000 unrestricted funds to recognized educators.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Outstanding educators and teachers who demonstrate excellence in education.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Unrestricted use by award recipients.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: National program; Maryland educators are eligible.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides nutritious lunches and snacks to students in Maryland public and private nonprofit schools and residential childcare institutions. Over 900,000 students have access to these meals each day.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Schools receive reimbursement for providing USDA-approved nutritious lunches and snacks to students. All 24 Maryland public school systems and 22 nonprofit private schools participate.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students in participating Maryland public schools, nonprofit private schools, and residential childcare institutions
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reimbursement for nutritious lunches and snacks that meet USDA nutrition guidelines and Dietary Guidelines for Americans
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland counties where participating schools are located
requirements_list: Must be a public school system, nonprofit private school, or residential childcare institution
Must serve USDA-approved nutritious meals meeting federal nutrition standards

structured_extraction.program_description: OBVS oversees programs and services for individuals whose disability is vision loss. OBVS is part of the Maryland State Department of Education's Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS). OBVS teachers, counselors, and technical specialists are specially trained to help individuals who are blind, vision impaired, or deaf-blind. OBVS offers four service areas: Employment or vocational rehabilitation services, Transition services for Students with Disabilities, Independent Living Older Blind (ILOB) programs, and Maryland Business Enterprise Program for the Blind (BEP).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: OBVS provides four main service areas: (1) Employment or vocational rehabilitation (VR) services to help people with disabilities obtain competitive employment; (2) Transition services for Students with Disabilities to prepare students to move from school to post-school life; (3) Independent Living Older Blind (ILOB) programs for individuals age 55 and over to become independent in their homes and communities; (4) Maryland Business Enterprise Program for the Blind (BEP) to prepare individuals whose primary disability is vision loss to operate successful retail concession, food service, and vending operations in federal and State of Maryland facilities. Services include career guidance and exploration, assistive technology such as screen reading software, magnifiers, and low vision aids, career training or academic education, independent living skills training such as safe cooking techniques and managing personal care and household tasks, orientation and mobility instruction in safe travel or use of a long white cane, and job placement services.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals whose disability is vision loss, including those who are blind, vision impaired, or deaf-blind. Services are available for students with disabilities transitioning from school to post-school life, individuals seeking employment, and older individuals age 55 and over seeking independent living training.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Career guidance and exploration, assistive technology, career training or academic education, independent living skills training, orientation and mobility instruction, job placement, and support for operating retail concession, food service, and vending operations.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To request DORS services, go to dors.maryland.gov and select 'Request DORS Services.' You will be contacted to set up an intake meeting where a DORS counselor will gather and provide information regarding eligibility. You may also contact your local DORS office directly to request services. OBVS staff are located in DORS offices throughout Maryland, and you will be assigned a counselor or teacher who works in your community.

Students enroll in credit/certificate classes at community colleges and register with the Disability Support Services office. A DORS Pathways coordinator works with students, families, DORS counselors, and college staff.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational support, career development services, and skills training at community colleges

Families with children from birth through age three

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides instruction in self-advocacy and social skills training to Pre-ETS (Pre-Employment Transition Services) students with Autism. Students participate in activities that help develop soft skills needed to obtain and maintain employment, and are introduced to education, training and employment options available after high school, including apprenticeships, career training, job placement, and college. Includes participation in college tours.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Provides classroom and other activities offering instruction in self-advocacy and social skills training focused on soft skills needed to obtain and maintain employment. Students also participate in Counseling on Post-Secondary Education Opportunities (CPSEO) activities that introduce them to education, training and employment options available after high school, such as apprenticeships, career training, job placement, and college, including college tours.
structured_extraction.contact_phone: Contact your DORS Counselor or local office for more information

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Self-advocacy and social skills training for employment; counseling on post-secondary education opportunities
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available through DORS
requirements_list: Enrollment in Pre-Employment Transition Services
Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder

Currently enrolled in high school (including home school or alternative secondary education program), post-high school education program (such as college), or another recognized educational program (such as trade school)
At least 14 years old but less than 22
