structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Students enroll through the Pre-Employment Transition Services program. Contact your DORS Counselor or local office for more information or request DORS Services via QR code.

structured_extraction.program_description: Pre-Employment Transition Services (Pre-ETS) provides five specific services designed to help students with disabilities identify their career interests and enhance their awareness of the world of work. Services include: (1) job exploration counseling, (2) instruction in self-advocacy, (3) counseling on post-secondary education opportunities (CPSEO), (4) workplace readiness training, and (5) work-based learning experiences. Services are generally short-term and introductory in nature, and are available statewide through local DORS offices. Specialized services are available for students who are blind or visually impaired at the DORS Workforce & Technology Center campus. CPSEO services are also provided to Pre-ETS students with Autism, exposing them to post-secondary options such as apprenticeships, job training, direct job placement, and college, including college tours. The Pre-Employment Autism Support (PEAS) program provides instruction in self-advocacy and social skills training to Pre-ETS students with Autism.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free training and counseling services provided to eligible students. Services include: job exploration counseling to explore skills and interests (including interest inventories, learning about the labor market, and information about specific in-demand occupations); instruction in self-advocacy covering communication, rights, responsibilities, problem solving, and self-awareness (including sessions like the Youth Leadership Forum); counseling on post-secondary education opportunities (CPSEO) providing awareness of career pathways and post-secondary skill development options, including apprenticeships, job training, direct job placement, and college with college tours; workplace readiness training on employee skills, workplace behavior, interaction with supervisors and coworkers, strategies to get to work on time, and appropriate dress and behavior on the job; and work-based learning experiences through work opportunities with participating employers outside the traditional school setting. Specialized services are provided for students who are blind or visually impaired at the DORS Workforce & Technology Center campus. Pre-Employment Autism Support (PEAS) program provides instruction in self-advocacy and social skills training to Pre-ETS students with Autism, with participation in CPSEO activities.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Jessica Markum, Staff Specialist for Students and Transitioning Youth; Muttasim Fadl, Employment Services Specialist for Students with Blindness or Vision Impairments; MSDE Division of Rehabilitation Services Headquarters
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students with disabilities who are at least 14 and less than 22 years old, currently enrolled in secondary school (including home school or other alternative secondary education program), post-secondary education program, or other recognized educational program, and have a documented disability (on an IEP or 504 plan, or with medical documentation). Specialized services also available for students who are blind or have low vision, and for Pre-ETS students with Autism.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Job exploration counseling (interest inventories, labor market information, in-demand occupations), self-advocacy training (communication, rights, responsibilities, problem solving), workplace readiness training (employee skills, workplace behavior, supervisor interaction, timeliness, dress and behavior), post-secondary education counseling (including college tours), and work-based learning experiences with participating employers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through more than 20 local DORS offices in Maryland; services available virtually and in-person. Specialized services for students who are blind or visually impaired also provided at the DORS Workforce & Technology Center campus in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be at least 14 years old and less than 22 years old

Must be currently enrolled in secondary school (including home school or other alternative secondary education program), post-secondary education program, or other recognized educational program, and have not graduated or withdrawn
Must have a documented disability documented with an Individualized Education Program (IEP), 504 plan, or medical records
For Pre-Employment Autism Support (PEAS) services: diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Complete the Request DORS Services form available at dors.maryland.gov. The form can be completed by the student, parent, family member, medical provider, school staff, or other interested party. Assistance with the form is available by calling your local DORS office. Step 2: Allow 10 business days for a DORS representative to contact you to schedule a virtual or in-person intake meeting and determine next steps. Step 3: Provide required information including Social Security Number, documentation of disability, proof of school enrollment, and proof of age. Complete the Pre-ETS Consent to Participate form. Step 4: Submit all information through the secure SARA system. Once qualification is complete, a counselor from your local DORS office will contact you and your family to meet and plan your Pre-ETS services. For students who are blind or visually impaired, contact DORS transition services to enroll. CPSEO for Autism students is accessed through Pre-ETS enrollment. Information is available in multiple languages on the DORS website.

structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive grant program that provides funding for local education agencies and private providers to administer high-quality full-day prekindergarten and school readiness services for three- and four-year-old children from families earning up to 300% of Federal Poverty Level at no cost to families. Funded through the Blueprint for Maryland's Future, this program expands access to quality early learning statewide.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant funding of approximately $26,644,000 total, with an estimated average award of $400,000 per grantee (50 estimated awards). Funding is $19,950 per full-day slot for three- and four-year-olds. Funds support salaries and wages for qualified teaching and assistant staff; equipment, materials, and supplies; reasonable rental/mortgage and utility costs (prorated by square footage); technology costs (not to exceed 10% of total); accreditation costs; screening and intervention services; evaluation and monitoring (not to exceed 5%); meals meeting CACFP requirements; academic field trips; professional learning; and indirect costs (not to exceed 15% for nonprofits, 10% for others). Funds may not be used for supplanting existing funds, capital improvements, pre-approval costs, or transportation (except field trips). The grant period is July 1, 2026 - June 30, 2027, with programs providing a minimum of 180 instructional days and at least 6.5 hours of instruction per day. Applicants approved for funding may request a 20% payment advance (15% will be issued upon request with supporting receipts).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Wednesday, March 11, 2026. No later than 5:00 pm EDT (Amended on 3/6/2026). Applications must be submitted electronically through Qualtrics by 5:00 p.m. on March 9, 2026.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Dr. Nykia Washington, Prekindergarten and Mixed Delivery Program Manager
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local school systems, Head Start programs, and qualified private child care providers who hold a valid license or registration and will deliver prekindergarten services; as well as three- and four-year-old children from low-income families.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding supports the administration and delivery of high-quality full-day prekindergarten and school readiness services for three- and four-year-old children from eligible families. Funds may specifically be used for: salaries and wages for qualified teaching staff with commensurate pay based on qualifications and experience aligned with local education agency salary schedules; equipment, materials, and instructional supplies including MSDE-approved curriculum resources supporting Maryland Early Learning Standards; reasonable rental/mortgage and utility costs (prorated by square footage); technology costs (maximum 10%); accreditation and Maryland EXCELS rating maintenance; screening and intervention service contracts; evaluation and program monitoring (maximum 5%); meals meeting CACFP requirements; academic field trips; professional learning activities for instructional staff; and indirect costs for nonprofits (maximum 15%) and other organizations (maximum 10%).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Local Education Agency (LEA), qualified vendor as defined in COMAR 13a.06.02, private provider, or Head Start program
Applicant must hold a valid license or registration (if applicable)
Children must be three or four years old
Families must have household incomes at or below 300% of Federal Poverty Level
Programs must participate in Maryland EXCELS
Provide high-quality prekindergarten programming in alignment with the Blueprint for Maryland's Future and Maryland Early Learning Standards

Lead teachers must meet Blueprint for Maryland's Future qualifications: hold a bachelor's degree in early childhood education or related field, OR hold a bachelor's degree in any field from an accredited U.S. institution, OR hold a bachelor's degree from an accredited foreign institution (verified as comparable), OR have 10+ years of documented ECE experience at 20+ hours/week and 180+ days/year (and must obtain an associate degree in ECE by July 1, 2030). Those not qualifying through pathway 1 must achieve minimum CLASS assessment scores: Emotional Support Domain 5.00, Classroom Organization Domain 5.00, Instructional Support Domain 3.00
Lead teachers with P-3 certification must be paid salary commensurate with LEA teachers in their county
Lead teachers without P-3 certification must be paid at least the minimum salary per Lead Teacher Salary Schedule based on qualifications and experience
For classrooms with more than 10 students, an Assistant Teacher meeting Blueprint requirements must be hired

Assistant Teachers must hold a high school diploma and by July 1, 2027 (private providers) or 2027-2028 school year (public providers) earn and maintain CDA with preschool designation or associate degree in ECE, OR have 15 years ECE experience for private providers or 5 years for public providers (20+ hours/week, 180+ days/year as of July 1, 2024)
Programs must use valid and reliable child assessment tools to monitor progress
Programs must provide health screenings and referrals in vision, hearing/speech/language, general health, and physical development
Programs must offer family engagement, support services, and referrals directly or through coordination (parenting support, physical/mental health services, early intervention)

Programs must have a qualified individual with bachelor's degree or higher in ECE or related field and ECE experience responsible for instructional oversight (8-10 hours/month minimum; cannot be full-time teaching director)
Programs must develop measurable SMART goals addressing standards alignment, instructional practice, quality improvement, and child outcomes

Programs must provide at least 20 hours of professional learning for instructional staff aligned with Maryland Early Learning Standards, science of reading, early mathematics, social foundations, CLASS, and HQIM
Programs must collect, verify, and securely maintain documentation of family income eligibility using FY26 Federal Poverty Levels
Programs must have published Maryland EXCELS Level 3 or higher (private providers) or Level 4 or higher (public providers), with plans to achieve/maintain Level 5 within 5 years
Priority given to programs with Maryland EXCELS Level 5 (with plan to maintain) or Level 4/3 (with plan to achieve Level 5 in 5 years)

Priority given to programs seeking renewal/expansion with demonstrable track record of success, in areas with unmet Pre-K need, or with parental/guardian engagement and educational activities beyond classroom
All grant requirements must be met prior to start of grant year (July 1, 2026)
Lead Teachers must be hired by July 1, 2026 to avoid disruption in grant funds

For renewed/expanded grantees seeking modified short form: maintained lead teacher meeting all requirements, maintained minimum EXCELS Level 3 or higher, remained in compliance with reporting/fiscal guidelines, not under corrective action plan, and filled 85% of seats by December 31, 2025
LEAs receiving both Blueprint and Prekindergarten Expansion Grant funds must increase number of 3- and 4-year-olds served in full-day Pre-K (increase verified by September 30, 2026 enrollment count)

Must enter into Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with MSDE and any eligible private providers (due by September 30, 2026) addressing roles, responsibilities, services for children with disabilities, supports for multilingual learners, support for children experiencing homelessness, parent preference processes, centralized enrollment, payment processing, administrative costs, racial/socioeconomic integration, and proportionate concentration avoidance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested applicants must complete a competitive grant application and submit it electronically through Qualtrics (https://msde.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_0qxUC1IT7xwk08C) by 5:00 p.m. on March 9, 2026 (deadline amended March 6, 2026). Applications must be submitted electronically; paper applications are for reference only. Before submitting, applicants must answer initial eligibility questions confirming the program holds a valid license/registration and meets Maryland EXCELS rating requirements (Level 3+ for private providers, Level 4+ for public providers). Applicants seeking to expand existing approved programs with a demonstrable track record of success may submit a modified short form application (requiring minimum 45 points); all other applicants must complete the full application (requiring minimum 80 points). The full application consists of 10 sections: (1) Program Eligibility/Maryland EXCELS and Accreditation (10 points), (2) Evidence of Need/Market Analysis (10 points), (3) Measurable Goals (20 points), (4) Program Quality and Curriculum (10 points), (5) Plan of Operation (10 points), (6) Staffing, Key Personnel, and Management Plan (10 points), (7) Project Timeline/Implementation Plan (10 points), (8) Collaboration and Sustainability (10 points), (9) Fiscal Systems and Controls (10 points), and (10) Budget and Budget Narrative (10 points). The modified short form requires only sections 1, 3, Maryland EXCELS/Accreditation, Goals and Objectives, Plan of Operation (if different), Blueprint and Expansion slots information, Staffing/Management/Key Personnel (if different), Budget and Budget Narrative, and Evaluation. Applications are divided into four sections: Applicant Information, Slots Requested, Application (Full or Modified), and Appendices. Applicants can move back and forth within a section but cannot return to previous sections once completed. All required appendices must be uploaded within Qualtrics before submission. MSDE offers customer service support sessions and office hours in January and February (before March 9 deadline) to help applicants understand requirements and navigate the application. Applicants will have the opportunity to review their answers and download a PDF of their responses before submitting. Once submitted, applications cannot be changed. Timely submission is encouraged to increase likelihood of award to expedite the award process and allow grantees to transition without interruption into the 2026-2027 school year. Questions should be directed to prekexpansiongrant.msde@maryland.gov with subject line 'Pre-K Expansion Application.' All questions should be resolved by March 9, 2026.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides access to State prekindergarten funding through grants and technical assistance to help child care providers meet requirements and expand their services. Pre-K Specialists guide providers through the application process, helping them understand grant requirements and assess their organizational capacity to successfully provide services.

structured_extraction.program_description: The School Breakfast Program provides nutritious breakfasts to students in Maryland public and private nonprofit schools and residential childcare institutions. Over 898,000 students have access to school breakfasts each day. The program reimburses schools with federal dollars for meals that comply with USDA nutrition standards. Studies show breakfast is correlated with higher test scores, decreased emotional and behavioral problems, reduced food insecurity, less frequent visits to the nurse, and fewer school absences.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Schools receive reimbursement with federal dollars for meals that comply with USDA nutrition standards. Some students may qualify for free and reduced-price meals based on family income eligibility. Children from families with incomes at or below 130–185% of the poverty level may receive meals at a free or reduced price. Students in families receiving Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) and/or food stamp benefits are eligible for free meals. All 24 Maryland public school systems and 17 nonprofit private schools and residential childcare institutions participate.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students in Maryland public schools, nonprofit private schools, and residential childcare institutions
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reimbursement for nutritious breakfast meals for students that meet USDA nutrition standards and Dietary Guidelines for Americans
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland counties where participating schools are located; all 24 Maryland public school systems and 17 nonprofit private schools and residential childcare institutions participate
requirements_list: Must be a public school system, nonprofit private school, or residential childcare institution
Must serve USDA-approved nutritious breakfasts meeting federal nutrition standards and Dietary Guidelines for Americans
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Students in families at or below 130–185% of the poverty level or receiving Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) and/or food stamp benefits apply through their school for free or reduced-price meals. Cost for other students is determined by each school district.

Schools with half-day pre-kindergarten and kindergarten programs where children do not have access to other school meal programs are eligible

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland State Department of Education provides annual grants to qualified non-profit organizations that provide enriching educational programs to Maryland students. Eligible programs provide learning experiences that align with the State's curricular and educational priorities and cannot be replicated in the classroom. Educational opportunities emphasize experiential learning and one-on-one support services, including free or reduced admission, full-day and residential field trips with hands-on activities, mentoring, and tutoring. Pre- and post-visit activities for teachers and professional development opportunities that link SAI programs to the classroom are also funded.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual grants to qualified 501(c)(3) non-profit organizations for enriching educational programs to Maryland students. Approximately $6,706,449 is available with an estimated 60-65 grants to be awarded. Grants fund experiential learning, one-on-one support services, free or reduced admission, full-day and residential field trips with hands-on activities, mentoring, tutoring, pre- and post-visit teacher activities, and professional development opportunities. Funds may be used for salaries and wages for direct service staff, supplies and materials to implement educational programs, outreach and marketing tools, equipment necessary for direct service, and contractual expenses. Funds may NOT be used for construction or capital improvements, transportation of students, utilities or operating costs, or food. Funds must be used within the fiscal year for which they are granted.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Friday, June 13, 2025, no later than 5:00 p.m. EDT
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified non-profit organizations that provide enriching educational programs to Maryland students
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Salaries, wages, and stipends for direct service to students and educators; supplies and materials to implement educational programs; outreach, engagement, informational, and marketing tools to expand reach; equipment necessary for direct service to students and teachers; and contractual expenses. Funds may NOT be used for construction or capital improvements, transportation of students, utilities or operating costs, or food.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide across Maryland. No more than 20% of participants served may come from nonpublic or homeschools.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications open May 1, 2025 and must be submitted electronically by 5:00 p.m. EDT on June 13, 2025 to sai.applications@maryland.gov. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis after submission. Applicants must download the electronic SAI application, complete it with all required appendices, and save as one PDF file before submitting. MSDE will hold virtual customer service support sessions on May 5 and May 23, 2025 to review program requirements and provide an application walk-through. Applications are pre-screened for submission requirements and inclusion of all required sections; applications not meeting requirements may be returned for revisions. A review committee evaluates applications using a scoring rubric. For any section(s) scored at Level 1 (does not meet criteria), written feedback is provided and an opportunity to revise and resubmit is offered. Results are communicated to the State Superintendent in July, then to the State Board of Education for review in August. Final approval is determined in legislation as authorized by the budget bill for fiscal year 2027, with the Governor releasing the draft budget bill in January 2026 and final passage around April 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federally-funded program that provides free nutritious meals to children and teens 18 years and younger in low-income and economically disadvantaged areas during summer months when school is not in session. The program reimburses sponsoring organizations and meal sites for providing free meals through summer activity and enrichment programs. Two service options are available: SUN Meals (meals consumed on-site) and SUN Meals To-Go (multi-day meal boxes for pickup).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Reimburses sponsoring organizations and meal sites for providing free nutritious meals (breakfast, lunch, snacks) to eligible children during summer months when school is not in session. Available in economically disadvantaged areas statewide.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children and teens 18 years and younger in low-income/economically disadvantaged areas throughout Maryland during summer months. Organizations interested in becoming meal sites should contact the sponsoring organization for their county.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reimbursement for providing free meals (breakfast, lunch, snacks) that meet federal nutrition requirements to eligible children during summer when school is not in session.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Economically disadvantaged areas throughout Maryland; available statewide across all Maryland counties.

Meals must meet USDA/federal nutrition standards
Organizations must apply through their county's designated sponsoring organization

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides additional funding for local education agencies (LEAs) participating in the National School Lunch Program or Seamless Summer Option during School Year 2021-2022 to participate in a USDA Team Nutrition grant project. The goal is to build state capacity to create new, high-quality, appealing standardized recipes for Maryland schools using local agricultural products. Funding supports staff time for training and recipe tasting events, and purchase of food and supplies for these events. Training and nutrition education resources related to the recipes will be developed and made available to school nutrition staff and teachers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Direct grants awarded to Local Education Agencies participating in the National School Lunch Program (NSLP) or Seamless Summer Option (SSO). Anticipated awards of approximately ten (10) grants. Grant period: May 1, 2022 – September 30, 2023. Funding supports: (1) Salaries/wages to hire substitute school nutrition staff to allow staff to attend training; (2) Stipends for staff time to attend training activities outside of normal work hours; (3) Food and nutrition equipment and smallware costs (total equipment value cannot exceed 5% of LEA subgrant total); (4) Food costs for grant-related training and taste tests (food expenditures cannot exceed 20% of LEA subgrant total, must comply with Buy American Provision); (5) Consumable costs for grant-related training and taste tests for each school. Funds may not be used for child nutrition program costs outside the scope of the grant, purchasing meals and snacks for training participants, foods used to prepare reimbursable meals, foods used as incentives or prizes, foods provided to students and families for home preparation, foods not related to standardized recipes, any costs associated with prizes or incentive items, gardening tools or materials, or clothing such as chef hats and aprons.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No later than 5:00 pm EST on April 22, 2022
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local Education Agencies (LEAs) participating in the National School Lunch Program (NSLP) or Seamless Summer Option (SSO) during School Year 2021-2022.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Staff time for training and recipe tasting events, and purchase of food and supplies for these events. Funding supports development of high-quality, appealing standardized recipes for Maryland schools using local agricultural products. Specific uses include salaries/wages for substitute staff, stipends for staff time at trainings, food and nutrition equipment/smallware (up to 5% of total grant), food costs for training and taste tests (up to 20% of total grant), and consumable costs for training and taste tests.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide. Selection criteria provide additional points for schools located in rural zones (as defined by USDA) or in Internal Revenue Service (IRS)-designated Qualified Opportunity Zones.
requirements_list: Must be a Local Education Agency (LEA) participating in the National School Lunch Program (NSLP) or Seamless Summer Option (SSO) during 2021-2022 and in good standing
Must be registered as a Team Nutrition School prior to application submission
Must commit participation of up to three schools; if more than one school is selected, at least two schools must serve different grade levels
Must designate a Grant Coordinator to serve as primary liaison with MSDE and grant partners, manage subgrant funds, and ensure grant activities are implemented at all participating schools
School nutrition staff must attend required training events hosted by MSDE and/or grant partners
Schools must prepare at least one chef-designed recipe and host two or more student taste tests per recipe between Spring 2022 - Spring 2023
Grant Coordinator must manage collection of data from recipe tasting events and submit quarterly reports on utilization of subgrant funds
Schools must use provided nutrition education resources to implement nutrition education for local products used in recipes
Grant Coordinator must secure photographs, training attendance records, data, and success stories for MSDE quarterly progress reports to USDA
Schools must menu at least one final recipe in a reimbursable meal by the end of the grant period
LEAs must comply with state and federal statutes and regulations including Civil Rights Act, ADA, EDGAR, GEPA, and FERPA
Grantees must establish and maintain fiscal control and fund accounting procedures as set forth in 2 CFR §200
All records of financial transactions relating to grant must be retained for five years and made available for inspection and audit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested applicants must identify school(s) to participate and ensure they participate in NSLP or SSO and are registered as Team Nutrition Schools. Applicants must complete a School Agreement Form for each participating school (up to three total), requiring signatures of the School Principal, Kitchen Manager, and a third school staff member (such as a School Health Council member, Title 1 Coordinator, or Community Coordinator). Applicants must complete the Team Nutrition Grant Application including all required components: school listing, recipe selection, budget, and school agreements. The application must include signed LEA Agreement Form and School Agreement Forms. A Grant Budget Form (Excel) and Budget Narrative describing each budget category must be submitted. All materials must be saved as PDF and submitted electronically to NutritionTraining.MSDE@maryland.gov by the deadline. MSDE will review applications for eligibility, verify all required documentation is included, and score applications using selection criteria including Free and Reduced-Price meal percentage (0-49%=0 pts, 50-75%=2 pts, over 75%=3 pts), rural zone location (1 point per school, max 3), and Qualified Opportunity Zone location (1 point per school, max 3). Approximately ten LEAs will be awarded grants based on scores. Award notifications will be sent by email in spring 2022.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that connects people with disabilities who receive Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) or Supplemental Security Income (SSI) with the Department of Rehabilitation Services (DORS). Participants work with DORS to develop an Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE) and receive services including training, career counseling, vocational rehabilitation, job placement, benefits counseling, and ongoing support to achieve and maintain employment. The program provides protection from Continuing Disability Reviews as long as the Ticket is in use and timely progress is being made.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free services including job training, career counseling, job placement, job coaching, benefits planning, vocational rehabilitation, and ongoing employment support services. The program includes built-in work incentives that help participants try working without immediately losing benefits, earn more money, keep health insurance, and get cash benefits back if they have to stop working due to disability. Participants can keep Medicare for at least 93 months after starting to earn more, maintain Medicaid even after starting work, or qualify for Employed Individuals with Disabilities (EID) program once employed. The program is voluntary and at no cost to participants.
structured_extraction.program_audience: People with disabilities who receive Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) or Supplemental Security Income (SSI) and are between 18 and 64 years old
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services to help achieve employment and maintain work, including job training, career counseling, job placement, job coaching, benefits planning, and ongoing support services. Participants can use these services to learn new skills that lead to jobs with health benefits and higher income than SSDI or SSI benefits.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide
requirements_list: Must receive Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) or Supplemental Security Income (SSI)
Must be between 18 and 64 years old
Must sign an Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE) with DORS to have Ticket marked as in use
Must make timely progress on employment and educational goals as determined by SSA
Must reply to any letters sent by Social Security
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the DORS Ticket Coordinator at 410-554-9460 or email Ticket.DORS@maryland.gov to begin the process. DORS will work with SSA to ensure your Ticket is available and assignable. Once assignable, your Ticket becomes In Use when you sign an Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE) with DORS staff based on your job goals. DORS will help create this plan and provide services to help you reach your employment goals. If your Ticket is already assigned to an Employment Network, DORS will coordinate services with that provider. For additional information on the Ticket to Work Program and Employment Networks, call 1-866-YOURTICKET (1-866-968-7842) 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. Monday through Friday, or visit choosework.ssa.gov or ssa.gov/work. For TTY access, call 1-866-833-2967.

structured_extraction.program_name: Training Vouchers and Reimbursements (Maryland Child Care Credential Program)
structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides child care providers holding a Maryland Child Care Credential at Level 2 or higher with up to $400 each year to help pay for approved professional development training. The program operates through two mechanisms: Training Vouchers (advance payment before training for pre-service courses, approved college coursework, and conference registrations, with applications submitted at least 60 days in advance) and Training Reimbursement (reimbursement after training completion for approved Core of Knowledge training, pre-service training, conference registrations, and approved college coursework, with applications submitted within 180 days of training completion).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible child care providers receive up to $400 per year to cover the cost of approved training. Training Vouchers provide advance payment issued before training; Training Reimbursements provide payment after training completion. Both mechanisms cover pre-service courses, approved college coursework, Core of Knowledge training, and conference registrations. Applicants will receive notification of approval or denial via email within 30 days of application submission. For approved vouchers, applicants download and sign the training voucher PDF from their Maryland OneStop dashboard and forward it to the trainer/training organization. After training completion, applicants upload their Certificate of Successful Completion to the Maryland OneStop portal.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Training voucher applications must be submitted at least 60 days before the conference or pre-service training. Training reimbursement applications must be submitted within 180 days of training completion. Approval decisions are communicated within 30 days of application submission.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care providers in Maryland who hold a Maryland Child Care Credential at Level 2 or higher, or held a Level 2 or higher credential that expired between July 1, 2024 and August 30, 2025.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Approved Core of Knowledge training (minimum 2 clock hours), pre-service training courses (child growth and development, infant-toddler care, preschool curriculum, school-age curriculum, director administration), registration fees at statewide and national child care conferences, and approved college coursework in child development, early childhood education, special education, program administration, and related fields. Activities not listed on the PAU matrix may be evaluated for approval using the Professional Activity Unit (PAU) Approval Form.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide
requirements_list: Must hold a Maryland Child Care Credential at Level 2 or higher, OR hold a Level 2 or higher credential that expired between July 1, 2024 and August 30, 2025
Training must be approved by MSDE according to COMAR 13A.14.09
For training reimbursement, training must have taken place less than 181 days before the application date
For training vouchers, applications must be submitted at least 60 days before the conference or pre-service training
For training reimbursement, applications must be submitted within 180 days of training completion
Training fees and association membership fees are not eligible for reimbursement
CDA credential and CDA renewal fees are not eligible
Applicants must register for an individual Maryland OneStop account to submit applications
Approval notifications are sent via email within 30 days of application submission

For activities not listed on the PAU matrix, a Professional Activity Unit (PAU) Approval Form must be completed and submitted to credentialocc.msde@maryland.gov for evaluation, with processing completed within 60 days of receipt
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through the Maryland OneStop online platform. For training vouchers, submit a completed application with required documentation at least 60 days before the training or conference. Applicants will receive approval or denial notification via email within 30 days of submission. If approved, applicants log into their Maryland OneStop dashboard, navigate to 'My Dashboard', click into their application submission, scroll to the 'MSDE Approved Training Voucher' section, download the training voucher PDF, sign it, and forward it to the trainer/training organization. After training completion, applicants return to their Maryland OneStop portal, click 'My Dashboard', select their application, scroll to the 'Verification of Training Completion' section, click 'Choose File' to upload their Certificate of Successful Completion, and press 'Submit'. For training reimbursement, submit a completed application with required documentation (receipt and certificate of completion) within 180 days of training completion; reimbursement is issued directly to the credentialed provider. For activities not on the standard PAU matrix, complete the Professional Activity Unit (PAU) Approval Form with detailed information about the activity and email it to credentialocc.msde@maryland.gov; the request will be reviewed within 60 days and assigned PAUs (1 to 3) if approved.

structured_extraction.program_description: Supports domestic nutrition programs and American agricultural producers through purchases of 100 percent American-grown and produced foods for use by schools participating in the National School Lunch Program. The program provides USDA food items to eligible schools and child care facilities, including public schools, private non-profit schools, and residential child care institutions.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides USDA food commodities for distribution to eligible organizations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible recipients include public schools, private nonprofit schools, and residential child care institutions participating in the National School Lunch Program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The program provides USDA food commodities for distribution.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides virtual mentoring and support services for individuals on the autism spectrum attending college, helping them transition into and navigate college while developing self-advocacy and social skills for success in the college environment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Remote mentoring program providing weekly online individual sessions with DORS Autism Services staff and weekly online group sessions. Helps students on the autism spectrum learn skills including: successful transition from high school to college, transition from two-year to four-year college, campus supports and resources, time management and organizational skills, self-advocacy and social skills, appropriate grooming and hygiene skills, and other skills needed to navigate the college environment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: College students on the autism spectrum who are DORS participants and cannot participate in the in-person DORS Pathways program
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Virtual mentoring and support services
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to individuals attending in-state or out-of-state two- or four-year colleges where the in-person DORS Pathways program is not available.
requirements_list: Be a DORS participant on the Autism spectrum
Have an approved Individualized Plan for Employment (IEP) that includes college
Work towards an industry-recognized college degree or certification from a two-year or four-year college where the in-person DORS Pathways program is not available
Meet with DORS Autism Services staff for weekly online sessions
Attend weekly VCAMP online group sessions
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals interested in VCAMP should contact their DORS Counselor or local office to request DORS Services or for more information about enrollment.

structured_extraction.program_description: DORS reimburses employers for wages paid to employees during on-the-job training programs. This program is part of DORS's business services offering to help Maryland businesses grow and improve their workforce.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: DORS provides wage reimbursement to employers for wages paid during on-the-job training. The program is designed to help businesses train and retain employees, with a track record showing 80% of job seekers who become employed through DORS services are still working after one year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland businesses of all sizes and types seeking to train and employ individuals, particularly those with disabilities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Wage reimbursement for employees participating in on-the-job training.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local DORS Business Relations Representative or the DORS Business Relations Team at 410-554-9408 or 888-554-0334 (toll free) for more information and to apply. Email dors@maryland.gov or visit www.dors.maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: A two-part training program designed to help individuals with disabilities who have little or no work experience or those who have been out of the workforce for an extended time develop the skills needed to succeed in competitive employment. The program combines classroom instruction, community-based activities, and real-world work experience through internships and worksite training.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two six-week courses offered at no stated cost. Work Readiness 1 provides classroom-based instruction including videos, lectures, guest speakers, worksite tours, and job shadowing experiences. Work Readiness 2 combines classroom instruction with real-world work experience at community worksites, including volunteer work experiences, and covers topics such as customer service, workplace ethics, conflict management, resumes and job descriptions, mock interviews, and managing your online footprint. Participants in Work Readiness 2 spend half of each day at a community worksite with drop-in support only. Work Readiness 1 and 2 may be taken together or as stand-alone programs.
structured_extraction.contact_phone: DORS Counselor or local DORS office
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students or job seekers with disabilities who have little or no work experience or have been out of the workforce for an extended period and are seeking competitive employment.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and development of job readiness skills including soft skills development, financial management, organizational skills, self-determination and self-awareness, interpersonal skills and teamwork, workplace preparation and communication, job retention, customer service, workplace ethics, conflict management, resume writing, mock interviews, and managing online footprint. Also includes real-world work experience through volunteer work at community worksites and job shadowing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is offered at the DORS Workforce Training Center (WTC) campus in Baltimore, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must have a disability
Must have little or no work experience or have been out of the workforce for an extended period
Must be seeking competitive employment
Work Readiness 1: Must be able to function in a classroom setting and fully participate in all individual and group activities
Work Readiness 2: Must demonstrate capability and desire to participate in competitive employment and be able to spend half of each day volunteering at a community worksite with drop-in support only
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested individuals should contact their DORS Counselor or local DORS office for enrollment and program participation details. Consumers may participate in Work Readiness 1 and 2 together or as stand-alone programs.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program designed exclusively for agricultural businesses, farms, and farm owners in Washington County to support agricultural business growth and development through funding for innovation and equipment purchases. The program has $300,000 in funding sourced from the Washington County Hotel Rental Tax Fund, approved by the Board of County Commissioners in July.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding to support agricultural innovation and equipment purchases for agricultural producers and businesses in Washington County. Total program pool is $300,000 sourced from the Washington County Hotel Rental Tax Fund. Funding can be used for equipment purchases, capital improvements, agricultural innovation projects, and modernization of farming operations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural producers, farmers, agricultural businesses, farm owners, and agribusinesses in Washington County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Agricultural innovation, equipment purchases, capital improvements, farm modernization, and working capital for agricultural operations
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be an agricultural business, farm, or farm owner operating in Washington County
Must use funds for agricultural innovation and equipment purchases
Funding is available to individuals and for-profit agricultural enterprises
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should contact Kelsey Keadle at the Washington County Department of Business and Economic Development for application procedures, eligibility verification, and grant award guidelines.

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary program that encourages landowners to enter into a ten-year agreement restricting their land from development. In exchange, landowners receive protection from nuisance complaints through the Right to Farm Ordinance, become eligible to sell Development Rights Easements through the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Program (MALPP), and receive a property tax credit.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Landowners who enter the program receive: (1) County property tax credits for the farmland, farm buildings, and partial tax credit for the home; (2) protection from nuisance complaints through the Right to Farm Ordinance; (3) official county acknowledgement that farming is the preferred use of the land; and (4) eligibility to apply to sell a permanent agricultural preservation easement to the State of Maryland (MALPF). In exchange, landowners agree to a minimum ten-year restriction on development of the property, which runs with the land even if ownership changes. The land may not be used for industrial, commercial, or residential purposes except as permitted by county regulations, may not be subdivided without written approval, and must comply with soil erosion and water quality practices.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural landowners in Washington County who wish to preserve their farmland, protect against nuisance complaints, and restrict development for ten years.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Not applicable; this is a land restriction/preservation program. Landowners receive tax credits and nuisance protection in exchange for a ten-year development restriction.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland
requirements_list: Property must be located in Washington County
Minimum 50 acres stand-alone or minimum 20 acres if contiguous to other districts
Minimum 50% of soil must be classified as soil classes I, II, or III
Property must be outside water and sewer service areas
Property must be outside growth areas
Property must be in agricultural use
Landowner must voluntarily enter into the district agreement
Land must not be developed or subdivided for industrial, commercial, or residential purposes for a minimum ten-year period except as permitted by county regulations
Soil erosion and water quality practices must be implemented according to an approved soil conservation plan within 10 years of the agreement date
Agreement must be notarized and recorded in county land records
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Landowners voluntarily enter into an Agricultural Land Preservation District by: (1) completing an Agricultural District Intake Form and submitting it to the Washington County Planning Department; (2) meeting with Agricultural Land Preservation personnel to verify property eligibility; (3) executing a notarized Agricultural Preservation District Agreement with the Board of County Commissioners; and (4) having the agreement recorded in the Washington County Land Records. The agreement becomes effective upon recordation and runs for a minimum of ten years.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federally funded grant program that provides funding to eligible entities for projects addressing economic opportunities, workforce development, critical infrastructure, natural and cultural assets, and leadership and community capacity in Appalachia.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are provided for projects in five strategic areas: Economic Opportunities (entrepreneurial and business development), Ready Workforce (education, skills, health), Critical Infrastructure (broadband, transportation, water/wastewater), Natural and Cultural Assets (community and economic development), and Leadership and Community Capacity (building skills of leaders and organizations). A 50% match is required, with matching funds identified and committed at the time of application. Projects must demonstrate measurable outcomes and/or economic impact. Priority projects include Technology Development, Broadband, Education and Workforce Development, Tourism, Energy, Recovery Ecosystems, and Traditional Infrastructure.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: FY27 Project Submission (Preliminary Project Description) is April 3, 2026; formal grant application due by November 15, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible entities in Washington County seeking to fund projects addressing Appalachian regional development priorities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects related to economic opportunities, workforce development, critical infrastructure (broadband, transportation, water/wastewater systems), natural and cultural assets, and leadership and community capacity building. Priority consideration given to projects in technology development, broadband, education and workforce development, tourism, energy, recovery ecosystems, and traditional infrastructure.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland, which is part of the Appalachian region.
requirements_list: 50% match required
Matching funds must be identified and committed at time of application
Projects must demonstrate measurable outcomes and/or economic impact with quantifiable metrics
Preliminary Project Description and ARC Project Budget and Funding Sources forms must be submitted
Project must align with ARC Strategic Goals and Objectives (2024-2028)
Project should be consistent with ARC 2024 Strategy Statement
Projects should reference any plans and/or economic documents showing the project is part of an overall economic development plan
All outputs and outcomes must be quantifiable with associated numeric values
Commitment letters required for all matching funds with committed status
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the Preliminary Project Description (PPD) and ARC Project Budget and Funding Sources Worksheet to the Office of Grant Management by April 3, 2026. The PPD must include project name, applicant information, project description, organizational capacity statement, goals and objectives aligned with ARC investment goals and state objectives/strategies, and performance measures with quantifiable outputs and outcomes. Projects are reviewed and ranked by Washington County Commissioners. County-ranked projects are submitted to Tri-County Council for Western Maryland for regional ranking. Top-ranking projects receive a letter in early fall inviting submission of a formal grant application to the Appalachian Regional Commission, due by November 15, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: A financial support program that provides grants to charitable organizations within Washington County that deliver services improving the community and quality of life for Washington County residents.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual grants provided to eligible non-profit organizations serving one or more of six prioritized service areas: Families and Children ($494,400), Domestic Violence ($386,400), Arts & Cultural ($135,600), Seniors ($136,800), Recreation ($33,600), or Other ($13,200). For FY2027, the Board of County Commissioners has allocated $1,200,000 in total available funding. Grants are intended to support operating and/or capital expenses that must be expended within one year. Grant awards are disbursed in four quarterly installments (25% each quarter from July 2026 through June 2027). Administrative costs may not exceed 15% of the total request amount. The Board of County Commissioners determines the total allocation set aside for the Community Organization Fund each year during the budgeting process. Funding emphasizes efficient use of funds and results-based programmatic outcomes.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Maria Kramer, Director; Carsten Ahrens, Senior Grant Manager
structured_extraction.program_audience: Charitable non-profit organizations serving Washington County that are included on the Board of County Commissioners Recognized Non-Profit List (Code of Public Local Laws § 1-108).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services that improve the community and quality of life for Washington County citizens. May include operating expenses and capital expenses/projects that benefit one or more of the following prioritized service areas: Families and Children, Domestic Violence, Arts and Cultural, Seniors, Recreation, or Other community services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland only. Eligible organizations must be located within Washington County and provide services to Washington County residents.
requirements_list: Organization must be included on the Board of County Commissioners Recognized Non-Profit List (Code of Public Local Laws § 1-108)
Organization must be a charitable non-profit with IRS 501(c)(3) determination letter with 'Valid' status

Organization must be incorporated as a business entity with Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) and be 'In Good Standing' at the time of application submission; proof required via Maryland Business Express
Organization must have an office located in Washington County and provide services within Washington County
Organization must not have unpaid liens, judgments, or past due obligations to the Washington County Treasurer or any other government entity
Organization must be in good standing at time of submission; evidence of such must be included in submission
Organization must have submitted any required FY26 grant reports by June 30, 2026 (failure to do so may jeopardize FY27 funding)
Request must support at least one of the six prioritized service areas
Administrative costs may not exceed 15% of total request amount
Submission must be signed by an authorized representative
Funds requested cannot be intended to benefit an individual or fund an endowment
Organization must submit either a recent certified audit or detailed financial statement
Results-based programmatic outcomes required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations on the Recognized Non-Profit List receive a Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) each year. The FY27 application process begins with online access to guidelines and application forms available on or about December 1, 2025. Two informational workshops are offered via Zoom (December 2, 2025 at 9:00-10:30am or 3:00-4:30pm). Organizations must submit completed application packets containing all required sections and supporting documents. Each submission requires six hard paper copies (not bound, secured by staple, binder clip, or rubber band) placed in a manila envelope plus one electronic PDF copy. Hard copies may be mailed to or dropped off at the Washington County Office of Grant Management, 100 West Washington Street, Room 1601, Hagerstown, MD 21740. Electronic copy must be emailed as a single PDF to cahrens@washco-md.net with cc to jmackereth@washco-md.net. Applications received after the Tuesday, January 6, 2026, 3:00pm deadline will not be accepted or considered, regardless of postmark date; expedited mail services are encouraged. The OGM will not check applications for accuracy or completeness at submission—applicants must verify all documents against the submittal checklist. The COF Committee reviews and scores applications using a rubric with maximum 100 points based on: Application Submission (10 points), Statement of Need (20 points), Past Performance (5 points), Organizational Capacity and Staffing (10 points), Program Plan (30 points), Collaborations/Partnerships (10 points), and Budget/Narrative (15 points). The Committee considers funding allocations, geographic distribution, service duplication, and previous program performance. Applicants are notified in writing when the County budgeting process is complete (expected May-June 2026). Technical assistance available; applicants encouraged to contact OGM at least two weeks before deadline.

structured_extraction.program_description: A fund that reinvests cannabis sales tax revenue into communities that were disproportionately impacted by cannabis prohibition enforcement prior to July 1, 2022. The fund supports community-based initiatives that benefit low-income communities and disproportionately impacted areas.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Cannabis sales tax revenue and one-time cannabis business conversion fees are distributed to eligible organizations and government entities for community-based initiatives. Funds are maintained in a separate special revenue fund with restricted cash reserves and restricted fund balance to ensure they are used only for intended purposes.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community-based organizations and Washington County government serving low-income and disproportionately impacted communities, specifically in ZIP code 21740 which includes portions of the City of Hagerstown and surrounding unincorporated areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Community-based initiatives that benefit low-income communities and disproportionately impacted areas, including mental health and substance use services, education and after-school programs, small business grants and economic development initiatives, parks and recreational opportunities, criminal justice reform and re-entry programs, and housing assistance and homelessness prevention. Funds may also cover administrative expenses necessary to implement and manage the program. Funds may not be used for law enforcement agencies or activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, specifically ZIP code 21740 which includes portions of the City of Hagerstown and surrounding unincorporated areas. CRRF funding must supplement, not replace, existing local government funding for programs and services.
requirements_list: Programs must serve low-income communities
Programs must serve disproportionately impacted areas as defined in § 36–101
Funds may not be used for law enforcement agencies or law enforcement activities
CRRF funding must supplement, not replace, existing local government funding for programs and services
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Washington County is responsible for establishing application procedures and guidelines for eligible organizations. The County administers and monitors funded programs and provides an annual report to the Board of County Commissioners and the Maryland Comptroller.

structured_extraction.program_name: Commuter and Shuttle Bus COVID RELIEF Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides grant funding to support Maryland commuter and shuttle bus companies facing continued financial impacts from the Coronavirus.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The state established this program in 2021 through bipartisan legislation with $8 million in state relief act funding to support commuter and shuttle bus companies facing continued financial impacts from the Coronavirus.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland commuter and shuttle bus companies facing continued financial impacts from COVID-19
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Relief for commuter and shuttle bus companies facing continued financial impacts from the Coronavirus
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland

structured_extraction.program_description: A state program instituted by the Maryland General Assembly in 2009 that works with the Federal Farm Service Agency's CREP Contract Program to make CREP Contracts permanent through state-funded conservation easements. It allows landowners to add up to ten times the amount of their CREP Contract acreage to their easement to maximize land preservation and easement value. As of the latest data, the program has invested $4,835,547 to protect 1,926 acres in Washington County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program converts federal CREP contracts into permanent state-funded conservation easements. Landowners with existing FSA CREP contracts can apply to make their contracts permanent, and may add up to ten times their contract acreage to the easement to maximize preservation and easement value. Once the easement is sold, it remains effective in perpetuity. The program has invested $4,835,547 to protect 1,926 acres in Washington County.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural landowners in Washington County who have an existing FSA CREP Contract and wish to make their contract permanent.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Establishment of permanent conservation easements on land with existing CREP Contracts, converting federal contracts to state-funded permanent easements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland
requirements_list: Must have an existing FSA CREP Contract to apply
Must be willing to sell conservation easement
Once the easement is sold, it remains effective in perpetuity
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Landowners with existing FSA CREP Contracts apply to the County's Land Preservation Office. Once the easement is sold, it becomes permanent.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides qualifying businesses with State income tax credits and local real property tax credits in return for job creation and capital investments made in designated Enterprise Zones.
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State income tax credits for job creation: $1,000 one-time maximum for most new jobs; $3,000 first year, $2,000 second year, and $1,000 third year for economically disadvantaged employees (certified by Maryland Department of Labor). Local real property tax credits: 80% of property taxes on increased assessment for years 1-5, declining 10% annually for years 6-10 (70%, 60%, 50%, 40%, 30%). Exemption from commercial building excise taxes on new construction. Employees must work at least 35 hours per week, earn at least 150% of federal minimum wage, and spend at least 50% of working time in the zone.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Linda Spence, Washington County Enterprise Zone Administrator
structured_extraction.program_audience: New and existing for-profit businesses located in or relocating to designated Enterprise Zones in Washington County, Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credits for businesses making capital investments and creating jobs in Enterprise Zones; credits applied against state income tax liabilities and local real property tax bills
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Designated Enterprise Zones in Washington County: (1) City of Hagerstown/Washington County Enterprise Zone (approximately 4,000 acres, includes Hopewell Valley Industrial Park, Washington County Business Park, CSX Valley Park, City of Hagerstown Business Park, and downtown Central Business District); (2) Town of Hancock Enterprise Zone (1,500 acres, includes commercial and industrial development opportunities and Main Street commercial frontage)
requirements_list: Business must be located in designated Enterprise Zone on designation date, or relocated or started construction/expansion after designation date
For income tax credits: minimum job creation requirements of 1 new job in Central Business District or Hancock Zone, or 5 new jobs outside Central Business District
For property tax credits: minimum capital investment requirements of $5,000+ in Central Business District or Hancock Zone, or $50,000+ outside Central Business District
Employees must be hired after zone designation date
Employees must not be replacement hires
Employees must work at least 35 hours per week for at least 6 consecutive months
Employees must earn at least 150% of federal minimum wage
Employees must spend at least 50% of working time in Enterprise Zone or in activities directly related to zone

Business activities must be in eligible categories: manufacturing, warehousing, research and development, corporate or regional headquarters offices, service industries, or mercantile/retail (with special conditions)
Mercantile/retail businesses only eligible in Hancock Zone or Central Business District of Hagerstown-Washington County Zone
For property tax credits: application must be submitted before project completion and issuance of User/Occupancy Permits
Property must be certified to Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation during calendar year construction is completed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1) Determine business property is in a Zone by contacting Washington County Department of Business Development. 2) Verify minimum eligibility criteria for jobs or capital investment are met. 3) Complete and submit Request for Enterprise Zone Qualification form to Washington County Department of Business Development prior to project completion (for property tax credits) or after hiring new employees (for income tax credits). 4) For income tax credits only: submit additional 'New Jobs Created' form listing employees meeting requirements; local Job Service Office contacts applicant to review employee list and determine eligibility as 'disadvantaged' or 'non-disadvantaged.' 5) Washington County Department of Business Development sends approval letter; copies submitted to appropriate local and state agencies. 6) For property tax credits: credits automatically appear on Washington County and Town of Hancock tax bills in July; City of Hagerstown issues credit voucher to be submitted with payment. 7) For income tax credits: claim credits using Maryland Tax Form 500CR ('Enterprise Zone Tax Credit') with copy of approval letter submitted with annual tax filing. 8) No reapplication required for additional job credits after initial approval; contact Job Service to identify any disadvantaged employees to claim credits.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides reimbursement for expenses associated with international marketing projects for Maryland companies that receive an ExportMD Award.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Maryland companies that receive an ExportMD Award are eligible for up to $5,000 in reimbursement for expenses associated with an international marketing project.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland companies interested in international marketing
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Expenses associated with international marketing projects
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland company
Must receive an ExportMD Award

structured_extraction.program_description: The Gaming Commission distributes funds from the Washington County Gaming Fund to eligible charitable organizations and non-profits in accordance with state statute and county regulations. In 1995, the Maryland General Assembly passed legislation enabling tip jar gaming in Washington County. Monies collected from tip jars are deposited into a dedicated Gaming Fund account to be allocated to local charities. By statute, 50% of the Gaming Funds are allocated to the Washington County Volunteer Fire & Rescue Association, with the remaining allocated to local charitable organizations making application annually to the Gaming Commission.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Distributions from the Gaming Fund may not exceed $100,000 per application. Organizations may apply for multiple projects by submitting separate applications for each project. Funds must be used exclusively in Washington County and cannot be distributed outside of the County. The grant performance period is one year from award announcement (typically early in August). Any funds not spent within the performance period must be returned to the fund. Organizations who find they are unable to spend funds as indicated in the grant application are encouraged to contact the Office of Grant Management to discuss a budget modification.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Susan M. Buchanan, Director; J. Mackereth; S. Lapole; S. Buchanan
structured_extraction.program_audience: 501(c)(3) charitable organizations located in Washington County that provide support for health and human services, emergency services, animal welfare, civic and community activities, athletic/recreational activities, educational and cultural activities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Health and Human Services, emergency services, animal welfare, civic and community activities, athletic/recreational activities, educational and cultural activities. Funds must be used exclusively in Washington County and cannot be distributed outside of the County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland. All funds must be used exclusively in Washington County and cannot be distributed outside of the County.
requirements_list: Must be a 501(c)(3) charitable organization with valid status located in Washington County
Must provide support for health and human services, emergency services, animal welfare, civic and community activities, athletic/recreational activities, educational and cultural activities
Must provide services without discrimination on the basis of race, creed, sex, age, color, national origin, marital status, familial status, sexual orientation, or disability
Must be a corporation, limited liability company, or an unincorporated association with articles of incorporation or organization not forfeited or in good standing with State Department of Taxation
Unincorporated associations must complete a Notice of Responsible Person form
Cannot be a church or religious entity (though separate organizations with their own 501(c)(3) status operating within a church may be eligible)
Cannot be an organization holding annual tip jar operator's licenses
Cannot be a political or governmental organization or sub-organization
Cannot be an umbrella organization (with exception of United Way of Washington County)
Cannot be the Washington County Board of Education or Washington County Public Schools

Booster organizations or other entities supporting school programs cannot receive funds for real property, goods, or materials that become the property of the Washington County Board of Education without a letter from the Superintendent indicating the school holds no ownership rights
Must submit a complete application with all required components including signed application form, financial statements, prior grant reports, and supporting documentation
Must provide proof that funds received previously were expended for approved purposes through invoices, proofs of purchase, or cancelled checks
Must submit completed IRS Form W-9 and Washington County vendor forms
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are available online beginning April 1 each year. Applicants must download the Gaming Commission Grant Application and complete it along with required supporting documents. All applications must be submitted electronically via email to jmackereth@washco-md.net with a copy to slapole@washco-md.net no later than 3:00 P.M. on the deadline date (typically early May). Required attachments include: (1) completed and signed Request for Funding application, (2) organization's most recent annual financial statement, (3) prior year Gaming Fund Grant Report with evidence of fund expenditure, (4) supporting documentation such as estimates and quotes, (5) Notice of Responsible Person form (if applicable for unincorporated associations), and (6) completed IRS Form W-9 and Washington County vendor forms. A Public Funding Hearing is held (typically in June) where applicants may appear to answer Commission questions. Organizations are encouraged to schedule hearing times early as slots fill quickly. The Gaming Commission reviews all applications and makes funding recommendations after the public hearing and workshop. Award announcements are made typically in August during the Board of County Commissioners meeting, with award letters and fund disbursement following several weeks later. Technical assistance is available via email and phone appointments.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides one-time funding to organizations operating within Washington County for projects or events that were not budgeted or anticipated. The funding addresses current financial issues or situations requiring prompt response and resolution, and assists with projects or events that would not qualify for other general fund community organization funding or hotel rental tax funding.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant awards are limited to a maximum of $2,000. The total cost of your event or project may exceed this amount, but no amount greater than the maximum award can be approved. Grants are paid to the applicant, not to vendors for products or services. Unused funds must be returned to the Office of Grant Management within 30 days of the completion of the event. The Board of County Commissioners may appropriate a portion of the General Fund Contingency annually to be awarded to targeted organizations meeting the funding goals. This portion of available funding may be adjusted annually at the discretion of the Board of County Commissioners.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Requests can be made throughout the fiscal year and are contingent on available funding.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Washington County Office of Grant Management
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations operating within Washington County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: One-time projects or events requiring prompt response and resolution that address unexpected circumstances or critical community needs
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland
requirements_list: Have an unexpected circumstance requiring prompt resolution
Have provided evidence that the request meets a critical need in the community
Do not have an alternative source of funding
Have proven to be a valuable community resource
Cannot benefit individuals directly (though individuals may participate in group events)
Cannot be used for normal and routine operating and administrative expenses
Cannot support political candidates or organizations whose primary purpose is to influence or attempt to initiate legislation
Cannot be used for for-profit ventures
Maximum grant award is $2,000
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Requests can be made throughout the fiscal year and are contingent on available funding. Submit a General Fund Contingency Funding Grant Application, which can be accessed from www.washco-md.net, printed and mailed, or emailed. All applications are received by the Office of Grant Management (OGM). The OGM will determine if the applicant is qualified, if the event or project is qualified, if the request meets funding goals, and will approve or deny the request with concurrence of the County Administrator. The applicant will be notified in writing of approval or denial. All organizations receiving grant funding must complete a General Fund Contingency Grant Report and submit it with supporting documentation within 60 days of completion of the event or project.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program that provides financial incentives to property owners who undertake qualified historic preservation work on properties located within Historic Preservation Districts or the Antietam Overlay zone in Washington County. The program offers stackable tax credits at the county (25%), state (20%), and federal (20%) levels, plus an additional 5% credit for new construction attached to historic structures, for a possible total of 70% in tax credits.
