list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credits are provided as reductions in Washington County property taxes for qualified historic preservation work. The program offers a 25% county tax credit for rehabilitation, restoration, or preservation work that minimizes destruction of historic fabric with thoughtful and sympathetic design. An additional 5% tax credit is available for exterior work on new construction attached to existing historic structures. State (20%) and federal (20%) tax credits are also available and stackable with the county credit, for a possible total of 70% in credits. Any unused county credit can be carried over for up to 5 years or until expended. Qualified rehabilitation expenses include roof repair/replacement, chimney repair/replacement, window restoration, new storm doors/windows, masonry repointing, structural repairs, architectural/engineering/consulting fees, and tool/equipment rental.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing; applications must be submitted before work starts
structured_extraction.contact_name: Washington County Department of Planning and Zoning
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential or commercial property owners with historic properties in Washington County Historic Preservation Districts, the Antietam Overlay zone (AO1 or AO2), contributing structures to Historic Rural Villages (Antietam, Cavetown, Fairplay, Highfield, Leitersburg, Pen Mar, Ringgold, Rohrersville, Sandy Hook, or Tilghmanton), or contributing structures in eligible municipalities with appropriate zoning and design guidelines. Properties must be documented on the Maryland Inventory of Historic Properties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Qualified historic preservation work and improvements to eligible historic properties, including roof repair and/or replacement, chimney repair and/or replacement, window restoration, new storm doors/windows, masonry repointing, structural repairs, architectural/engineering/consulting fees, and tool/equipment rental.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Properties located within Historic Preservation Districts with the Historic Preservation (HP) Overlay, the Antietam Overlay zone (AO1 or AO2), contributing structures to surveyed and adopted Historic Rural Villages (Antietam, Cavetown, Fairplay, Highfield, Leitersburg, Pen Mar, Ringgold, Rohrersville, Sandy Hook, or Tilghmanton), or contributing structures located within towns listed on the National Register of Historic Places with appropriate zoning and design guidelines in Washington County.
requirements_list: Property must be located in an eligible historic district, overlay zone, historic rural village, or eligible municipality with appropriate zoning and design guidelines
Property must be documented on the Maryland Inventory of Historic Properties
Work must constitute qualified historic preservation activities consistent with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation
Work must comply with Washington County Design Guidelines for Historic Structures
Application must be submitted and approved before work begins
Applicant must comply with all Federal, State, and local laws including zoning, building, and safety codes
Property owners with MHT easements must include a copy of the easement document with their application
Applicant must be the fee-simple owner or provide an Owner's Representative Affidavit if not the owner
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The application process consists of three parts submitted to the Washington County Historic District Commission. Part I (Evaluation of Significance) determines if the structure qualifies for the tax credit by confirming location in a qualifying area and providing property documentation; this part may be skipped if the property already has the Historic Preservation Overlay. Part II (Description of Rehabilitation) must be submitted and approved BEFORE work begins and evaluates whether the proposed work meets the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation and County Design Guidelines; applicants must provide detailed descriptions of all exterior work, estimated qualified rehabilitation expenditures, and supporting photos and plans. Part III (Request for Certification of Completed Work) is submitted at project completion and certifies that work was completed as approved, includes itemized expenses with supporting invoices and proof of payment on the provided spreadsheet, and includes completion photos. Completed applications should be mailed to Washington County Historic District Commission, c/o Washington County Department of Planning & Zoning, 747 Northern Avenue, Hagerstown, MD 21742, or emailed to askplanning@washco-md.net. The HDC reviews applications and may inspect completed projects. Unused tax credits can be carried over for up to 5 years. The HDC reserves the right to revoke certification up to five years after completion if work was not undertaken as presented or unapproved alterations were made.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that provides funding to stimulate tourism attractions, enhance economic development, and support cultural and recreational projects in Washington County. The program helps organizations and agencies undertake activities and events that would not be possible without special funding, with the goal of establishing projects that can eventually become self-sustaining.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants funded through a 6% county hotel rental tax are distributed back into the community through the Convention and Visitors Bureau, local municipalities, and designated local projects to support approved applications. Grant applications requesting $25,000 or less are reviewed and approved by the Office of Grant Management with concurrence of the County Administrator. Applications requesting more than $25,000 are reviewed by the Office of Grant Management and County Administrator, with final approval by the Board of County Commissioners. Grants are paid to the applicant, not to vendors. Any changes exceeding 10% of approved line items require approval by the Office of Grant Management. Unused funds must be returned to the County within 30 days of project completion.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Requests can be made throughout the fiscal year
structured_extraction.contact_name: Washington County Office of Grant Management
structured_extraction.program_audience: Washington County local municipalities, businesses, organizations, residents, and visitors seeking to develop tourism attractions, enhance economic development, and support cultural and recreational projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding can be used for activities and events that stimulate tourism attractions, enhance economic development, and support cultural and recreational projects in Washington County, including develop tourism advertising, publicizing or distributing information, marketing special events and festivals, supporting tourism-related facilities, economic development projects that enhance vitality and create job opportunities, cultural projects related to County history and culture, and recreational projects that promote activities and events.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland
requirements_list: Projects must have merit sufficient to eventually grow and succeed without continued financial assistance
Projects should not be considered without special funding
Priority given to projects that generate overnight stays in the County
Projects should encourage support of County businesses, restaurants and attractions
Projects should reach a broad segment of the community
Projects should seek multiple sources of support rather than rely solely on Hotel Rental Tax Funding
Projects should yield benefits to the community relative to resources invested
Projects should promote cooperation among event organizers to reduce costs
Projects should enhance or improve the community
Individual applicants are ineligible
Normal and routine operating and administrative expenses are ineligible
Organizations supporting political candidates or whose primary purpose is to influence legislation are ineligible
For-profit ventures are ineligible
Endowments are ineligible
Organizations with budget deficits prior to application are ineligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Requests can be made throughout the fiscal year and are contingent on available funding. The application can be accessed from the County's internet site under the Office of Grant Management, submitted by email, or printed and mailed in. Upon receipt by the Office of Grant Management (OGM), the OGM will determine if the applicant is qualified, if the event or project is qualified, and if the request meets the funding goals. For requests of $25,000 and below, the OGM will approve or deny with concurrence of the County Administrator. For requests exceeding $25,000, the OGM processes the application and forwards it to the County Administrator for review; upon favorable review, the Board of County Commissioners will hear the request and may take action at their discretion. The applicant will be notified in writing of approval or denial. Grant recipients must complete a Hotel Rental Tax Grant Report with supporting documentation (budget itemizations and receipts) and submit it to the OGM within 60 days of project completion.

structured_extraction.program_description: A county program created to accelerate land preservation easement purchases by allowing agricultural landowners to sell development rights to the County through installment payments over ten years instead of receiving a lump sum. Landowners sell their agricultural preservation easement to the County and receive payment through an Installment Purchase Agreement with a fixed interest rate.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The County purchases agricultural preservation easements through an Installment Purchase Agreement. Payments are made over ten years: 10% of the principal is paid at settlement plus interest, and 10% of the principal is paid annually for the remaining nine years at a fixed interest rate.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of agricultural land in Washington County who meet minimum qualifications and seek to sell development rights through installment payments.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Sale of development rights on agricultural land to preserve it permanently. Proceeds from the sale of agricultural preservation easements may be used by landowners as they choose.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland. Easements cover the entire contiguous acreage of the property minus one acre per existing dwelling.
requirements_list: Must own agricultural land that meets minimum qualifications
Must be willing to sell the agricultural preservation easement on entire contiguous acreage except one acre per existing dwelling
Can preserve all contiguous acreage less one acre per existing dwelling on the property
Program is competitive and dependent on current economic climate
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible landowners apply to sell their agricultural preservation easement to the County. If accepted, an Installment Purchase Agreement is signed between the County and the seller, detailing the total payment amount and payment terms with a fixed interest rate.

structured_extraction.program_name: Job Creation and Capital Investment Real Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides up to fifteen years of tax credits on the County portion of real estate taxes for qualified businesses that either expand or locate in Washington County and meet specific investment and job creation thresholds. The program is designed to reduce costs associated with real property expansion, construction, or renovation and is part of Washington County's broader strategy to support business growth, job creation, and infrastructure investment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers real property tax credits on the increased assessed property value for eligible businesses. Three tiers of benefits are available: Tier 1 (3 years of credits at 55%, 40%, 25%) for businesses with 1,500 sq. ft. and 5 new FTEs within 12 months; Tier 2 (6 years at 55%, 55%, 40%, 40%, 25%, 25%) for 2,500 sq. ft. and 25 new FTEs within 24 months; Tier 3 (15 years at 75% for first five years, then reduced by 5% annually until reaching 25%) for $20M investment, 200 new FTEs within 24 months, with 80% of new FTEs paid at 200% of Maryland State minimum wage. Credits apply to the County portion of real estate taxes on newly constructed, renovated, expanded, or previously unoccupied properties that are owned or leased.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified for-profit businesses that expand or locate in Washington County and meet specific investment and job creation thresholds. Businesses in Enterprise Zones are not eligible for this program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credit applied to the County portion of real estate taxes on newly constructed, renovated, expanded, or previously unoccupied properties.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland. Businesses in Enterprise Zones are not eligible for this program and must apply under the Enterprise Zone Program instead.
requirements_list: Expand or locate in Washington County
Submit letter of intent and official application before occupying space or hiring employees
Meet minimum investment thresholds based on tier selected
Meet specific job creation thresholds within required timeframe (12 months for Tier 1, 24 months for Tiers 2 and 3)
Eligible properties must be newly constructed, renovated, expanded, or previously unoccupied
Properties can be owned or leased
For leased properties, lessor must reduce taxes by the amount of credit for which business qualifies
Create required FTEs with appropriate wage levels (Tier 3 requires 80% of new FTEs paid 200% of Maryland State minimum wage)
Maintain all program requirements for each year receiving tax credit
Submit Annual Employment and Certification Report by February 1 each year
Cannot have received tax credit or exemption for same property in same taxable year under other state or county law
Notify DBED upon construction completion with square footage documentation
Not eligible if business is located in an Enterprise Zone
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Submit intent letter before occupying space or hiring employees. 2. Submit completed application packet including letter of intent, application form, and Employee Certification Report to Washington County DBED before completing construction. 3. Notify DBED upon construction completion with square footage documentation. 4. Create required full-time employees within specified timeframe (12 months for Tier 1, 24 months for Tiers 2 and 3). 5. Receive certification from Washington County DBED. 6. Submit Annual Employment and Certification Report by February 1 each year, including employee name, last four digits of SSN, hire dates, employment end dates, home city/state, benefits provided, pay rate, and hours worked. 7. Continue meeting all program requirements annually to receive tax credit. Businesses are strongly encouraged to engage with DBED early in planning process. Failure to apply before hiring or occupying new premises may result in ineligibility.

structured_extraction.program_name: LMB ENOUGH Capacity Building Fiscal Year 2026
structured_extraction.program_description: Grant funding to support innovative programs that improve healthcare access for underserved populations in Washington County by addressing gaps in transportation and healthcare services, particularly for seniors, individuals with disabilities, and low-income households with children.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $40,000 available per award. Washington County intends to award 1 to 3 grants, with individual awards ranging from $10,000 to $40,000. Total funding pool is $74,000. Performance period runs from May 15, 2026 through September 30, 2026. Funds can be used for Non-Emergency Medical Transportation (NEMT), expansion of existing volunteer driver programs or specialized transit services, or last-mile solutions for underserved areas not reached by public transit.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations and local government agencies that provide services to Washington County residents, with a focus on organizations addressing healthcare access and transportation barriers for seniors, individuals with disabilities, and low-income households with children.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding supports innovative programs that bridge transportation and healthcare gaps, including Non-Emergency Medical Transportation (NEMT) services for primary care, dialysis, mental health services, or pharmacy pickups; expansion of existing volunteer driver programs or specialized transit services within Washington County; and last-mile solutions for residents living in underserved areas not currently reached by public transit.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must provide services exclusively to residents of Washington County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Be a registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization or a local government entity
Be in Good Standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
Provide services exclusively to residents of Washington County, Maryland
Demonstrate a proven track record of fiscal responsibility and programmatic impact
Submit application with all required documents electronically
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application electronically to cahrens@washco-md.net by Friday, March 6, 2026, at 3:00pm with all required documents including: Application Submission Form, program budget (including funds not supplied by Washington County), letters of support, 501(c)(3) nonprofit determination letter, and proof of Good Standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT).

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide program established by Maryland law that preserves high-ranking agricultural properties through Purchase of Development Rights easements. Properties are ranked based on soil quality, proximity to other easements, agricultural operation intensity, and proximity to growth areas and Priority Preservation Areas. Easement restrictions remain effective in perpetuity.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The County purchases development rights easements from qualified agricultural landowners, making the easement restrictions effective in perpetuity. As of the page date, the program has invested $49,855,542 to protect 17,008 acres in Washington County.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted in the Spring prior to July 1st each cycle year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of high-ranking agricultural properties in Washington County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of development rights easements to permanently preserve agricultural land.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland. Priority given to properties in Priority Preservation Areas.
requirements_list: Property must be enrolled in the County's Agricultural Land Preservation District program
Property must meet minimum qualifications for ranking
Ranking is based on soil quality, proximity to other easements, agricultural operation intensity, and proximity to growth areas and Priority Preservation Areas
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted in the Spring, ranked by the local Agricultural Land Preservation Advisory Board, approved by the County Commissioners, and submitted to MALPF prior to July 1st of each cycle year.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides funding to assist nonprofit organizations whose critical operations have been financially impacted by COVID-19 and the state of emergency.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Governor Hogan allocated $50 million to the Maryland Nonprofit Recovery Initiative to assist nonprofit organizations whose critical operations have been financially impacted by COVID-19 and the state of emergency.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations whose critical operations have been financially impacted by COVID-19
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Relief for nonprofit organizations whose critical operations have been financially impacted by COVID-19 and the state of emergency
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a nonprofit organization
Must have experienced financial impacts from COVID-19 and the state of emergency
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Visit the Maryland Nonprofit Recovery Initiative website to learn more and apply.

structured_extraction.program_name: Next Generation Farmland Acquisition (Next Gen) Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A state program offered by the Maryland Agricultural Resource-Based Development Corporation (MARBIDCO) that provides down payment assistance to young and beginning farmers purchasing agricultural properties in Washington County. The program covers 51% of the land-only Fair Market Value appraisal, capped at $500,000. After settlement, the landowner must actively pursue a permanent easement through an approved program within seven years, or the land becomes preserved through a MARBIDCO permanent easement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Down payment assistance equal to 51% of the land-only Fair Market Value appraisal of the property, capped at $500,000, to help young and beginning farmers purchase qualifying agricultural properties.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Young and beginning farmers seeking to purchase agricultural property in Washington County that qualifies for the County's Agricultural Land Preservation District program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment assistance for the purchase of qualifying farm/agricultural properties.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland. Property must qualify for the County's Agricultural Land Preservation District program.
requirements_list: Buyer must be a young or beginning farmer
Must have a signed sales contract for the farm
Property must qualify for the County's Agricultural District program
Must enroll property in the County's Agricultural District program
After settlement, must actively pursue a different permanent easement through an approved program within seven years
If no permanent easement is procured within seven years, the land becomes preserved through a MARBIDCO permanent easement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Buyers provide a signed sales contract and complete an application in conjunction with the County's Land Preservation Office. The application is submitted to MARBIDCO. Processing takes approximately six months to complete.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program that allows investors to receive substantial federal tax incentives over ten years by investing their capital gains into designated Opportunity Zones. Washington County hosts designated Opportunity Zones where investors can direct capital gains to qualify for these incentives.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Substantial federal tax incentives provided over ten years for investors who invest their capital gains into designated Opportunity Zones.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Investors with capital gains seeking federal tax incentives through capital gains investment.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital gains invested into designated Opportunity Zones.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Designated Opportunity Zones in Washington County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Have capital gains to invest
Invest capital gains into designated Opportunity Zones
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Consult the Opportunity Zone Map and contact the Department of Business and Economic Development.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides emergency assistance for eligible restaurants, bars, and other qualifying businesses impacted by COVID-19.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Emergency financial assistance for eligible restaurants, bars, and other qualifying businesses impacted by COVID-19.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible restaurants, bars, and other qualifying businesses impacted by COVID-19
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Emergency assistance related to COVID-19 impacts

structured_extraction.program_description: A transportation service that provides subsidized vouchers for taxi rides to help elderly people age 60 and over and individuals with disabilities meet their transportation needs when they cannot use fixed-route buses.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants purchase vouchers at a reduced rate at the Washington County Transit office or by mail. Vouchers provide at least 50% savings on taxi fares. Vouchers come in various denominations and are used to pay drivers directly for rides. A set number of vouchers can be purchased each month. Vouchers expire June 30 each year.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Elderly individuals age 60 and over and individuals with disabilities who cannot use Washington County Transit fixed-route buses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Transportation services - taxi rides for general purpose transportation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be age 60 or over OR have a disability
If under age 60, must have application certified by a healthcare professional acknowledging disability
Cannot utilize Washington County Transit fixed-route buses for one or more reasons
Must have an annually updated application on file
Reapply annually - applications expire June 30 each year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Call the Washington County Transit office to request an application by mail, or visit the office at 1000 West Washington Street, Hagerstown, MD to pick one up in person. If under age 60, have your application certified by a healthcare professional. Mail or drop off the completed application at the WCT office (faxes not accepted). You will receive notification by mail of your eligibility. Once approved, purchase vouchers at the WCT office or by mail using checks, money orders, or credit cards.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state program enacted by the Maryland General Assembly in 1997 that protects Maryland's best natural, agricultural, historical, and cultural areas and most significant rural landscapes. It works with local governments and private land trusts to purchase easements from willing landowners in designated Rural Legacy Areas that are vulnerable to sprawl development. Easement restrictions remain effective in perpetuity.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program purchases conservation easements from willing landowners within specified Rural Legacy Areas. As of the page date, the program has invested $28,499,083 to protect 9,421 acres in Washington County. Easement restrictions remain effective in perpetuity. Applications are ranked based on property size, number of development rights, proximity to other permanent easements, agricultural characteristics, historic characteristics, and environmental characteristics.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications due prior to February 1st of each cycle year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural landowners and other landowners within designated Rural Legacy Areas in Washington County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of conservation easements to protect areas vulnerable to sprawl development and preserve natural resources, farming, forestry, recreation, and tourism.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland. Program only purchases easements within specified boundaries surrounding the Towns of Sharpsburg, Keedysville, and Boonsboro and the Rural Villages of St. James, Lappans, Fairplay, Rohrersville, and Gapland.
requirements_list: Must own property within a designated Rural Legacy Area
Must be a willing landowner/seller

Property characteristics are evaluated for ranking including property size, development rights, proximity to other easements, agricultural characteristics, historic characteristics, and environmental characteristics
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Qualifying landowners apply prior to February 1st of each cycle year. Applications are ranked based on property characteristics, approved by local authorities, and then submitted to DNR for funding consideration.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state program offered by the Maryland Agricultural Resource-Based Development Corporation (MARBIDCO) that provides down payment assistance to young and beginning farmers purchasing small farms between ten and forty-nine acres in size. Unlike the Next Gen program, there is no requirement to pursue a permanent easement after purchase — properties are considered permanently preserved by MARBIDCO at the time of real estate settlement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides down payment assistance for the purchase of small farms between ten and forty-nine acres. Unlike the Next Gen program, there is no requirement to pursue additional permanent easements after settlement. The property is considered permanently preserved by MARBIDCO at the time of real estate settlement.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Young and beginning farmers seeking to purchase small farms (10 to 49 acres) in Washington County, Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment assistance for the purchase of small agricultural farm properties.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland
requirements_list: Buyer must be a young or beginning farmer
Farm property must be between 10 and 49 acres in size
Property is considered permanently preserved by MARBIDCO at the time of real estate settlement
No requirement to pursue additional permanent easements after settlement
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Buyers work with the County's Department of Planning & Zoning to apply for the program. Interested buyers should contact the department for application details. Upon real estate settlement, the property is permanently preserved by MARBIDCO.

structured_extraction.program_name: Washington County Business Incentives Program (General Overview Booklet)
structured_extraction.program_description: A comprehensive tax incentives and business development support program designed to assist businesses operating or locating in Washington County through various tax credits, grants, loans, workforce training, and infrastructure resources.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Washington County offers multiple tax incentive programs including: (1) Research & Development Equipment Tax Exemption - exempts R&D equipment from county business personal property tax; (2) Manufacturing Machinery & Equipment Tax Exemption - exempts manufacturing machinery and equipment from county business personal property tax; (3) Business Inventory Tax Exemption - exempts inventory from county business personal property tax; (4) Job Creation & Capital Investment Real Property Tax Credit Program - provides 6-15 years of tax credits on county real estate taxes for businesses that expand or locate in the county (Section 4(a): 52% years 1-2, 39% years 3-4, 26% years 5-6 for businesses with 1,500+ sq ft and 1 new employee; Section 4(b): 30% years 1-2, 20% years 3-4, 10% years 5-6 for 2,500+ sq ft and 5 new employees; Section 4(c): 100% years 1-5, 75% years 6-10, 50% years 11-15 for $10M capital investment and 100 new employees); (5) New Jobs Tax Credit Program - 6-year credit at 52% years 1-2, 39% years 3-4, 26% years 5-6 for businesses expanding by 10,000+ sq ft and creating 25+ new jobs at 135%+ of average county wage in a Priority Funding Area; (6) Pad-Ready Site Commercial Stimulus Program - 3-year tax credit of 0.4% of construction costs for qualifying projects; (7) Brownfield Revitalization Incentive Program (BRIP) - real property tax credits of 50-70% of increased site value for 5 years after cleanup (up to 10 years in Enterprise Zones); (8) C-PACE Program - commercial loans for energy efficiency, renewable energy, and water conservation projects with little/no down payment, long repayment periods, and fixed-rate financing up to 100% over 20 years; (9) Workforce training grants up to $4,500 per worker through Western Maryland Consortium; (10) City of Hagerstown programs including CDBG Microenterprise Grants, Hagerstown Revolving Loan Fund (HRLF) up to $200,000 or 80% of project cost, and Invest Hagerstown Grants ($5,000-$250,000 depending on program); (11) State Enterprise Zone credits for job creation and capital investments.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit businesses operating or locating in Washington County; small businesses and microenterprises; manufacturers; technology companies; developers; homeowners (for certain City of Hagerstown programs)
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax relief and incentives for business operations; capital investments and equipment purchases; real property improvements; energy efficiency and renewable energy projects; workforce training and development; business expansion and relocation; job creation; property rehabilitation and redevelopment; working capital; building construction and renovation; land improvements; machinery and equipment with 5+ year useful life
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland; City of Hagerstown; Priority Funding Areas as designated in Title 5, Subtitle 7B of the State Finance and Procurement Article; Enterprise Zones including Hagerstown-Washington County Enterprise Zone (5,000 acres in City of Hagerstown) and Town of Hancock Enterprise Zone (1,500 acres); Foreign Trade Zone #255 (1,700 acres including Hagerstown Regional Airport, Williamsport, Hopewell Valley, Lakeside Corporate Center at Cascade, and Hancock); Brownfield sites in participating jurisdictions
requirements_list: Business must be a private for-profit entity
Business must be located in Washington County or relocating to Washington County
For Job Creation & Capital Investment Tax Credits (Section 4(a)): minimum 1,500 sq ft of new/expanded premises and at least 1 new permanent full-time employee
For Job Creation & Capital Investment Tax Credits (Section 4(b)): minimum 2,500 sq ft and at least 5 new permanent full-time employees
For Job Creation & Capital Investment Tax Credits (Section 4(c)): $10 million capital investment and 100 new permanent full-time employees
For New Jobs Tax Credit: minimum 10,000 sq ft expansion, at least 25 new permanent full-time positions, 50% of new jobs must pay 135%+ of average weekly county wage, must be in Priority Funding Area

For CDBG Microenterprise Grants: business must have 5 or fewer employees, be located in City of Hagerstown corporate boundaries, be in good standing with City and State, comply with all applicable regulations, and be established and operating for at least 12 months

For HRLF loans: business sales must be less than $5M annually for each of last 2 years, minimum loan $10,000, maximum $200,000 or 80% of project cost (microenterprise loans up to $5,000), must create or retain 1 full-time job for each $35,000 borrowed within 2 years
For Pad-Ready Site program: must be approved parcel with qualifying new construction project
For BRIP: site must be in participating jurisdiction and owned by inculpable person, must complete environmental cleanup
For Enterprise Zone credits: business must be new or expanding in designated Enterprise Zone
For C-PACE: business or nonprofit must own commercial property and pursue eligible energy efficiency, renewable energy, or water conservation projects
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Washington County Department of Business Development and Economic Development at (240) 313-2280 or visit www.washco-md.net/business-development for information on specific program applications. For City of Hagerstown programs (CDBG Microenterprise, HRLF, Invest Hagerstown), visit https://www.hagerstownmd.org for guidelines and application forms. For State Enterprise Zone credits, contact Washington County Department of Business Development. For C-PACE financing, visit www.md-pace.com/ or contact Abacus Property Solutions through the Maryland Clean Energy Center. For workforce training grants through Western Maryland Consortium, contact Debora Gilbert at (301) 791-3164 or dgilbert@westmdcon.org. Applicants are generally required to submit business plans, financial documentation, job creation projections, and capital investment details depending on program. For HRLF loans, non-refundable application fee is required based on loan amount requested.

structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program that provides gap financing to small businesses seeking to locate or expand in Garrett, Allegany, and Washington counties. The program works with banks and other lenders to assist in financing business projects and creates and saves jobs in the Appalachian region.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides gap financing by participating with banks and other lenders to assist in financing business projects. Borrowers repay loans and the money is returned to the fund to make other loans, creating an ongoing revolving financial tool.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses seeking to locate or expand in the three-county Appalachian region
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business financing and expansion
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Garrett, Allegany, and Washington counties in Appalachian Maryland
requirements_list: Business must be seeking to locate or expand in the service area
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants work with the program to partner with banks and other lenders for project financing.
